text:
美国人真的会飞！非AI

新款@Tesla Roadster 0-60 英里加速仅需 1 秒。  它在后部配备了由@SpaceX开发的 4 个推进器。Tesla 进行了一次直播发射。

这次小米、华为应该真的真的抄不动了。

这个发布的时间节点也很有意思：因为他的财报公布之间就在下周 10 月 21 日（周三美股盘后）发布。

目前Roadster有三个版本进行销售，Performance2和Thrust都是有钱就可以预定，预定价格分别为5万美金/23万美金。唯独会飞的Rocket1 “air ready”，目前采取邀请制，被邀请方可预定。

会飞的Roadster有多少预定不是关键，毕竟他可能都上不了路，但是他展现了Tesla超越一般车企的能力和想象力，把科幻电影里的存在变为现实的能力，这才是大家真正在意的。也是此前市场愿意给Elon和 $TSLA 市梦值的原因。
而且这次的展示，也把Elon最重要的两家公司进行了一个联动，火箭🚗目前只有特斯拉能造。

说回到下周的财报：
目前市场对本次财报的预期，基本是营收277-279亿美金，EPS在0.45美金左右。市场预期相对比较平淡。营收预计接近去年同期，盈利预计同比下降。这也符合我们新能源车产业成熟后的走法。
那惊喜点可能藏在哪里呢？
1️⃣FSD：
第二季度公司披露约 148 万个“活跃 FSD 订阅”，同比增长 56%。FSD的能力也持续提升中，我们可以来关注一下，FSD的净新增、续订和流失、存量车主的付费转化。
2️⃣机器人/Physical AI：
已知的进展缓慢。第二季度说：Fremont 的 Model S/X 生产线已停用，正在安装第一代 Optimus 生产线。公司当时预计 2026 年开始生产。
目前进展如何？
加州和德州的 Optimus 制造项目是否获得进展？

3️⃣Roadster：
演示很棒，那量产和预定信息是否可以更多展现？

4️⃣能源业务：
第二季度储能部署为 13.5 GWh，同比增长约 41%。这次需要验证：部署增长能否转化为收入与毛利；Megapack 3 和德州新工厂的生产进展。

本文也同步在OKX的星球，也欢迎大家关注我的星球账号。

text:
追了下 $BNT Logo背后的文化脉络，挺有意思。

它的图形，很像经典 Glider（滑翔机） 的连线变体：源自《康威生命游戏》，由数学家 Richard Guy 发现。简单的局部规则，就能让一个小小的图案不断演化、向前移动。

2003年，《大教堂与集市》的作者Eric S. Raymond @esrtweet  倡议把它作为黑客社区的共同徽标；Daniel Miessler（也是小绿豆官方推特第一个关注的账号 @hellojintao  ）后来也在2005年的文章中介绍过它。

这里的“黑客”，代表的是创造、分享，以及用技术解决问题的精神。简单规则下的协作，也能生长出复杂而有生命力的系统。

放到一个隐私货币项目上，我读到的是：开放协作，用代码维护个人的自由与边界。

几根简单的线，倒是挺有老派互联网精神，也看得出来这伙开发者还是很有想法，而且很认真的想做成一件事情。

text:
Discovered potential reason $CRWV bonds jumped 225 bp in 2 days with stock selloff.

On October 26, CoreWeave loses its “unlimited” cures agreement and can no longer sneak its own money into DDTL 3.0 if it’s not performing, without public disclosure, because it requires covenants. 

As of October 27, if the GPU backed loan doesn’t have sufficient cash flow directly from the CoreWeave customer for a period of 3 months, the loan has to be reported and amendments agreed to or it defaults. CoreWeave can’t use its own money to cover the shortfall. If it used the equity cover from August to October already, the loan could default on October 27 and would require immediate repayment.

It’s possible that the lender has been selling other held bonds, knowing that the covenant will be breached for insufficient customer payments to CoreWeave.

This is just a guess based on timing. If it’s true God Help the Ai trade and bond market. 

The customer is OpenAI. CoreWeave previously negotiated an amendment to lower DSCR equity from $175 million to $100 million because OpenAi couldn’t meet its commitment to CoreWeave for compute. It’s not a good sign. 

Its possible OpenAi will try to hide that it’s struggling to meet its commitments and use all the CoreWeave compute, but it definitely shows there’s fraud going on behind the scenes that for the very reason OpenAi couldn’t meet its commitment to CoreWeave who needed to beg borrowers for a lower DSCR.

It proves that OpenAi is lying about its commitments and its customers are hiding those lies by putting in their own cash to cover loans backing OpenAi commitments. I’m assuming the same may be true for Anthropic.

DDTL 3.0 may default October 27, because OpenAi hasn’t been paying.

The proposal would make swaps into stablecoins classified as electronic-money tokens under EU rules taxable from January 1, 2027.

Moving into those stablecoins to escape market volatility could therefore trigger a tax bill.

The existing 31.4% default rate would apply to taxable profits, not the entire amount swapped.

Ordinary crypto-to-crypto exchanges would generally retain their tax deferral.

回踩上升趋势线，能否撑住将决定后续趋势走势！

从6月底5.8万，到9月中旬7.5万，再到如今8.1万附近，BTC日线低点不断抬高，说明中期上升趋势尚未破坏。

但有个细节值得警惕：9月底以来，高点却在持续降低。

低点抬高，高点降低，两条趋势线不断收敛，意味着BTC已经进入关键变盘窗口。

再看宏观环境：昨天美股低开高走，标普、道指最终收涨，说明市场并未因CPI、PPI连续超预期而彻底恐慌，美债收益率明显回落，美联储10月加息概率也降至三成左右，短期流动性预期有所改善。

但问题在于，通胀压力并未消失，美国关税、能源价格以及AI科技股估值风险，仍然制约着市场风险偏好。

所以我认为，BTC现在既不是明确的底部，也没有形成真正的向上突破。

接下来重点关注两个位置：
8万美元：中期上升趋势的关键防线，守住仍有机会向8.5万-8.75万发起冲击。

8.4万美元：下降趋势线附近的重要压力，只有放量突破，才能进一步确认多头重新掌握主动权。

反之，一旦日线有效跌破8万美元，尤其反抽无法收回，就要防范再次回踩7.5万-7.8万美元。

我认为短线偏向震荡修复，但不急着看单边上涨，第三次回踩趋势线，可能是机会，也可能是陷阱。

真正值得关注的不是支撑被测试了多少次，而是每次测试之后，多头还能不能把价格推向更高的位置。

这次8万美元附近的争夺，很可能决定整个10月下半月的走势。

text:
I cannot let a steam engine analogy go by without bringing up John Wilkinson, perhaps the most underappreciated engineer of the Industrial Revolution.

Watt had figured out how to dramatically improve the steam engine, but he spent years struggling to actually manufacture one. The problem was embarrassingly simple: nobody could make a sufficiently round cylinder.

The casting and machining tolerances were atrocious. Watt complained that one 18-inch cylinder was out of round by as much as THREE-EIGHTHS OF AN INCH. Steam leaked past the piston. He tried packing the gaps with cork, oiled rags, paper, and apparently even old hats. Nothing worked particularly well.

Enter John Wilkinson, a British ironmaster whose immediate concern was manufacturing better cannons.

At the time, iron cannons were commonly cast around a core, introducing defects and misalignment that could make the barrels inaccurate or dangerously weak. Wilkinson developed a process for boring cannons from solid castings, and in 1774 patented a vastly improved boring machine.

The key innovation was almost comically mechanical: a massive, rigid boring bar, supported at both ends, that could cut a genuinely straight, circular hole instead of following the irregularities of the casting.

He adapted this technology to Watt's cylinders. By 1776, Matthew Boulton was boasting that Wilkinson had bored a FIFTY-INCH cylinder accurate to within the thickness of an old shilling.

Suddenly, the steam engine was a commercially viable machine.

And the story gets better. Wilkinson became one of Watt's first customers, buying an engine to drive the blast machinery at his own ironworks. The steam engine was now helping manufacture the iron that made more steam engines possible.

I find this whole episode absolutely extraordinary. The Industrial Revolution was, for a critical period, bottlenecked on the ability to make a sufficiently round hole.

We remember Watt, and rightly so. We remember the invention of the steam engine and the subsequent development of thermodynamics. But the man who made the machinery that made the whole thing possible is practically a footnote.

I think we consistently underestimate how much of scientific progress is actually downstream of advances in tooling, measurement, and manufacturing precision. It's not just that technology precedes theory. Sometimes the decisive breakthrough is that someone finally figures out how to build the thing the theorists have been talking about for twenty years.

Anyway, I think John Wilkinson deserves considerably more credit for modern civilization than he gets.

DeFi has just crossed the chasm from a fully reserved system to a fractionally reserved system.

3Jane now enables anyone to generate yield on promises to supply capital later. Capital can remain outside DeFi’s contracts and still back those promises.

The promise can exceed the liquidity held against it, letting anyone run fractional reserves and effectively become their own shadow bank.

With this update, promisors can tap the much larger market for senior secured debt through @Morpho to fund capital calls, commit up to 6.25x their onchain net worth, and earn yield on the full commitment.

@ImperiumPaper is right that DeFi is speedrunning financial history.

A balance sheet can monetize two things: (a) capital and (b) the capacity to commit capital.

DeFi built its core markets around the former. Capital enters a smart contract, then earns yield. We accepted this mental model so completely that we named our measure of scale TVL.

LCC makes the latter a market through unfunded capital commitments. 3Jane buys future access to capital while its owners keep it productive elsewhere.

Crypto is a ~$2.8T asset class, while DeFi’s contracts hold ~$90B. A market for promises lets DeFi’s funding capacity grow beyond those deposits. 3Jane draws that capital into USD3 as calls are met. At 7.5% margin, each dollar posted supports a $13.33 commitment.

U.S. banks already sell this capacity at scale, carrying ~$11.3T of unused loan commitments. They sell access to capital before they need to deliver the cash.

LCC engineers TradFi’s most powerful liquidity mechanism into self-enforcing, internet-native code. It crowdsources balance-sheet capacity at global scale, letting anyone earn yield on their unfunded capital.

I encourage crypto market participants to revisit their priors.

Bubbles are, of course, mathematically impossible in this new paradigm.

text:
Onchain perps keep growing. Their tokens don't.

★ The venue side (@castle_labs, Oct 15)
→ Tracked onchain perp open interest is $13.33B, up 8.8% in 30 days.
→ @HyperliquidX holds 58% of it: $7.70B, +11% over 30d.
→ @Aster_DEX is 2nd at 9.7%, @variational_io 3rd at 7.4% (+18% in 30d), @Lighter_xyz 4th at 5.3%.
→ Last 24h: Hyperliquid traded $13.68B, 42% of the $32.78B across tracked venues. That's ~15% of what @binance futures did.

★ The token side (CoinGecko, 7d / 30d)
→ HYPE ~$77.8: −8.4% / −1.0%
→ LIT ~$2.94: −17.2% / −33.3%
→ ASTER ~$0.69: −2.8% / flat
→ dydx-chain:native: −13.2% / +7.5%

★ Why the gap
→ OI grew over the month, but the last 7 days were red almost everywhere: Hyperliquid −12%, Lighter −20%, Variational −9%. Tokens are trading that weekly cooling, not the monthly growth.
→ Growth is concentrating. Hyperliquid alone took most of the gains, while edgeX (−29% in 30d) and Lighter shrank.
→ Lighter's token is down a third in a month while its OI fell only 5.6%. That's a token supply/sentiment story more than a usage story.

→ Caveat: I use OI rather than volume on purpose. @DefiLlama delisted Aster's volume over its correlation with Binance volume, so volume rankings are noisy.

If a perp DEX keeps winning share but its token doesn't follow, what exactly is the token capturing?

イーロン・マスク＆カーツワイル「未来の知能の99%以上はデジタル。人間が生き残る道は『脳をクラウドに直結して機械と合体する』ことだけだ」

イーロン・マスクが断言する「知能の99%デジタル化」と、未来予測の鬼才レイ・カーツワイルが唱える「人類と機械の融合（シンギュラリティ）」が交差する、人類の最終進化がコレ↓

・人間の知能なんて全体の「1%未満の残りカス」になる（イーロン・マスク）
近い将来、地球上に存在するあらゆる知能の99%以上をAIなどのデジタル知能が占めることになる。全人類の頭脳をかき集めても、知能全体から見ればわずか1%未満の「誤差」のような存在に成り下がる。

・指や口で入力している時点で、人間は「カタツムリ」同然
人間の話すスピードや指先でスマホを叩く速度は、データ通信としては遅すぎる。光の速さで思考するデジタル知能から見れば、生身の人間は超スローモーションで動く原始人に過ぎず、外からキーボードを叩いて道具として操る関係性は完全に限界を迎える。

・カーツワイルの予言：脳を「クラウド」に直接ぶち込む時代
シンギュラリティ（技術的特異点）の提唱者レイ・カーツワイルが予測するのは、脳の神経や毛細血管に微小なナノマシンや電極（Neuralinkなど）を繋ぎ、人間の脳の新皮質を直接クラウドのAIに接続する未来。何千倍、何万倍もの知能を「自分自身の思考」としてクラウドから引き出して考えられるようになる。

・「AIに支配される側」から「AIそのものになる側」への脱皮
人間より賢いバケモノAIにすべてを支配され統治されるディストピアを防ぐ唯一の手段は、人間とマシンの境界線をなくすこと。AIを外の敵として恐れるのではなく、自分自身の肉体と脳をアップデートして「機械と融合したハイブリッド生命体」になることで、人間は主導権を保ったまま神の領域へ進化する。

要するに、「これからの世界では知能の99%以上をAIが独占し、生身の脳みそだけでは1%以下の無力な存在に追いやられる。AIに淘汰されずに生き残る唯一の方法は、脳を直接クラウドにつないでマシンと合体し、人間自らが超知能へと進化することだ」ということです。 https://t.co/Eabqu1Hbhn

text:
I am leaving Cambridge after a few days spent for a workshop on fast finality, concurrent with other workshops on post-quantum crypto and formal verification. Quick takeaways

- Faster finality is coming, the research is mature, even as new ideas have come in during the week, the handoff to specifiers and implementers feels well underway. Next catalyst event will be at devcon in a few weeks, with core devs
- The performance numbers for post-quantum finality are improving massively, and this is the worst that they’ll ever be. This is significant, it means the penalty from moving to more complex crypto would not require, in my opinion, if the numbers hold up, a deep rearchitecting to move to PQ-secure consensus, in particular when it comes to incentives
- The biggest opportunity imo remains networking. Simulations and live experiments are exploring both the current pre-PQ setting, where networking is clearly the bottleneck, and the post-PQ setting, where compute remains the bottleneck. But with PQ compute numbers improving, I wouldn’t be surprised if once again networking becomes the bottleneck

All of this is making me extremely bullish that we’ll achieve PQ-secure and faster finality even faster.

Many thanks to @yannvon @benjaminion_xyz and @robsaltini for the workshop, and to @corcoranwill and @drakefjustin for hosting us in Cambridge!

text:
David Silver founded @IneffableLabs with a mission to build a "super learner" and make first contact with superintelligence. 

He says a super learner has capacity in two dimensions. 

Depth: it starts from knowing nothing at all and goes all the way to discovering things beyond what humans know. 

Breadth: you can drop it into any stream of experience and it keeps learning.

His analogy is us. Humans started with gray mush and discovered languages, technology, science and mathematics for ourselves. Nobody handed us a blueprint or a dataset. 

No AI system has done that yet.

David Silver is one of the all-time greats. He was the creator of AlphaGo, which changed the course of history by showing that neural nets could achieve superhuman performance for the first time.

He also has a unique intuition and knack for forecasting when things will happen in AI. With computer Go, he predicted the Lee Sodol outcome 10 years before, right to the year. He got the year right for Starcraft and won a bet inside Deepmind. Same for AlphaProof. Same for the IMO.

David's prediction for superintelligence: 3 years. !!! He has a strong sense that now is the time to build a superleaner, and that superlearners are now possible, thanks to the enormous progress in compute, simulators, autoresearch, and the sophistication of technology in the stack since the AlphaGo days.

What is a “super learner”? A super learner discovers all knowledge from its own experience. Start from nothing (no internet pre-training), and go beyond human knowledge. Drop it into any stream of experience, simulated or physical, and the superlearner learns.

He expects the progress will be rapid. When you get the recipe for a superlearner just right and remove humans from the development loop altogether, a superlearner can learn extremely quickly. Just look at AlphaGo. AlphaGo took two years to develop with humans in the loop. When David and his team at @GoogleDeepMind got the formula for AlphaZero correctly, it surpassed the human-developed algorithms in just a few hours. Human data is a shortcut, but you have to let go of the human data to shoot beyond it.

In January, David left GDM to found @IneffableLabs, a research-led lab with one mission: build a "super learner" that discovers all knowledge from its own experience, and make first contact with superintelligence. 

He joins us with co-founder Lasse Espeholt, who built IMPALA and SEED RL, the foundations of scaled-up RL, and now runs Ineffable's compute.

A few things we cover in this conversation. 

 — What a super learner is: depth (start from nothing, go beyond human knowledge) and breadth (drop it into any stream of experience, simulated or physical). The human brain is the only existence proof

 — Why they're giving up human data: AlphaGo took two years with humans in the loop. AlphaZero outperformed it in a few hours. "You have to let go of the human data to shoot past the competition"

 — Crucibles: simulated worlds with enough emergent complexity (physics engines, millions of interacting agents) for an agent to rediscover technology, science, maths and language on its own

— Simple rewards, emergent complexity: evolution optimized fitness and got all of life. Don't breadcrumb the objective, give the agent something simple to optimize in a world with a lot to learn about

 — Go as the existence proof: one agent is the most boring game imaginable, two agents is "an infinite onion of layers of complexity"

 — Why human language is probably not the endpoint for reasoning, and how training on it bakes in a flat earth and the four humors

 — Can superintelligence be built in simulation? If the sim is Turing complete, computation, economics, language and maths are all expressible, and it happens 10-100x faster and safer

 — Alignment: language-based monitoring is reaching its limits as agents learn to say one thing and do another. Shadow actions, superintelligences monitoring superintelligences, and building a real science of how they interact peacefully

 — Accelerate in simulation, pace in the real world: Ineffable will gate real-world deployment on evidence that it goes well

 — Timing as the determinant: Silver called Computer Go to the year, then StarCraft, then the IMO. He thinks this is the moment
 
 — Predictions: True superintelligence within three years.

Timestamps:
 0:00 – Introduction
 1:09 – What held true from Go to today, and what the LLM era changed

 5:58 – Why "Ineffable" (and the secret second reason)

 9:31 – Defining a super learner and first contact
 12:35 – Super learners vs. LLMs that make discoveries
 13:59 – Day to day: the RL stack, crucibles and human-journey milestones

 24:14 – Go: one agent is boring, two is infinite

 27:22 – Removing human priors: AlphaGo to AlphaZero
 32:05 – Keeping human bias out of the crucibles
 33:35 – Confidence, timing and super forecasting
 36:24 – Is compute the driver?
 38:13 – The ceiling on simulation and Rich Sutton's objection

 47:45 – Monitoring agents that don't think in English
 51:01 – Pacing the frontier

最近 @chainalysis  发布了一份关于《2026 北美加密采用趋势》的报告，里面有一个很有意思又能展现趋势的数据：

美国自 2022 年以来，首次重新成为了“比特币净进口国”。

如果把这个数据拆开看，会发现背后是一场非常彻底的筹码大搬家。

用报告的原话来说，“散户把比特币转出美国，而机构正在把比特币搬进美国。”

在过去一年的统计周期里，单笔低于 1 万美元的小额比特币转账，每个月都在从美国净流出；

但单笔超过 1000 万美元的巨鲸与机构转账，却单独为美国带来了 53,200 枚 BTC（约 43 亿美元） 的净流入。

美国正在进口“数字黄金”，同时向全球出口“数字美元”。

美国人本就有美元银行账户，不需要稳定币，因此在现货 ETF 和联邦“战略比特币储备”的预期下，把比特币当成稀缺储值资产吸纳；

而缺乏美元通道的其他国家，则在大量承接美国出口的稳定币。目前美元稳定币占了全球订单簿交易量的 99.1%，欧元稳定币仅占 0.45%。

此外，还有几组关于中美 AI 链上花销的数据也很有意思：

中美 AI Agent 在链上怎么花钱？美国为算力买单，中国用免费模型搞审计和套利

报告重点统计了 Base 链上爆发的 x402 协议，发现中美两国的 AI 在花钱习惯上完全是两个世界。

美国钱包垄断了 88.1% 的大模型推理付费，因为 ChatGPT 和 Claude 按量调用并不便宜；

中国关联钱包在模型推理上的付费占比只有 0.1%。报告指出，这是因为中国开发者普遍转向了开源免费的 DeepSeek 和千问（Qwen）。省下算力钱的中国 AI Agent，把预算全砸在了具体业务上：

它们买走了链上 90% 的“安全与代码分析”（几乎全流向了 Solidity 智能合约审计工具 AgentLISA）、46.7% 的金融市场情报以及 35% 的支付结算通道。

整份报告其实都能表明，基础设施是美国的，但买单的用户是全世界的。

全世界其他地方的机构、移民甚至 AI Agent，正在全面跑在美元稳定币、代币化美债和美式链上支付轨道上。

🚨 新型域名钓鱼警告：你盯着网址看10遍，也未必发现自己进了假网站！

给大家看两个网址，能看出区别吗？

① аhttps://t.co/ypOMScQnRp（假） 
② https://t.co/4g4DuWDKn7（真）

第一条的字母「а」其实是俄语使用的西里尔字符，第二条才是英文字母「a」。两者长得几乎一模一样，但在计算机眼里完全不同，可以指向两个不同的网站。

这种手法对币圈尤其危险。

骗子只需要伪造一个看起来像交易所、钱包或 DeFi 协议官网的域名，再复制一套登录页面，就有机会骗走你的账号密码，甚至诱导你连接钱包、签署恶意授权。

提醒下圈里的兄弟姐妹，常用交易所、钱包、DeFi 网站一定要收藏官方地址，尽量从书签或官方 App 进入。

别人私信发来的空投、补偿、紧急迁移链接，哪怕网址看起来100%正确，也别轻易连接钱包和签名。

Something Vitalik hasn't mentioned yet: Ziren is the first zkVM to prove Geth without modifying the Go compiler. 

@ProjectZKM's R&D team has worked closely with the @ethereumfndn on it for around a year.

The speed battle Vitalik calls won was fought almost entirely on Rust clients. Ethereum's most widely used execution client is written in Go, and proving it is a different problem - Ziren patches the Go runtime's garbage collector and scheduler to do it.

If the top priority is now security - for Ziren it always was - then prover-side client diversity belongs on that list. The Foundation has spent years on client diversity for Ethereum itself; proofs that all run through one client reproduce the monoculture problem one layer up.

text:
Tesla–SpaceX: The Game Theory Between Signing and the Vote

The ownership split of the combined company is the battleground between $TSLA and $SPCX investors. Every additional percentage point for one group leaves less for the other. But timing determines whether SpaceX’s appreciation makes that split harder to negotiate or easier to approve. To understand this, I’m stepping out of the investor’s seat and imagining myself at the negotiating table, responsible for getting a valuable deal signed and approved. The question becomes: how do we offer Tesla shareholders enough to secure their support without asking SpaceX to give up more than necessary?

My negotiating target would be 47.5–50% of combined economic ownership for legacy Tesla shareholders, the range I regard as necessary to build decisive support. Tesla holders have genuine leverage. Under the SpaceX-parent structure I’m analyzing, Elon can deliver SpaceX’s ordinary shareholder vote, but he cannot independently deliver Tesla’s required majority of outstanding shares. Retail participation matters because shares that do not vote contribute nothing toward that majority. Institutions will scrutinize valuation, negotiating independence, conflicts and the weaker voting influence Tesla holders would receive under SpaceX’s dual-class structure. Getting the deal approved means addressing all of those concerns.

This is two-level bargaining: the negotiators have to agree on terms that their shareholders will then accept. Using backward induction, I start from that vote and ask what Tesla holders would realistically support. My premise is that enough shareholders will resist accepting a smaller stake simply because SpaceX has surged while Tesla has remained flat, particularly when they see enormous unrealized upside in Optimus and robotaxi. They can reject the transaction and remain independent. That makes the threat credible, and it needs to influence the negotiations before anyone casts a vote.

My expectation that SpaceX will outperform creates a dynamic bargaining problem: waiting changes what each side will accept. If SpaceX pulls further ahead before signing, Elon faces an increasingly uncomfortable choice. He can offer Tesla a smaller stake and risk rejection, or offer a much larger premium to preserve the allocation its shareholders demand. The percentage SpaceX gives up stays the same, but it is now a bigger economic concession relative to Tesla’s unchanged value. Elon has an incentive to settle that argument earlier, before securing Tesla’s approval requires an offer considerably harder for SpaceX’s side to stomach.

The crucial distinction is that the terms are settled at signing, while Tesla shareholders assess what those terms are worth again when they vote. On the expedited timeline I’m working with, that vote comes roughly three to five months later. A fixed exchange ratio acts as a commitment device: the agreement establishes how many SpaceX shares each Tesla share receives, subject to its adjustment and termination provisions. Further SpaceX appreciation alone does not reopen the bargain.

Here’s a simple example, ignoring synergies and holding share counts fixed. Say Tesla is worth $1.5 trillion, SpaceX $2.2 trillion, and Tesla holders get 50% of the combined company. Their stake is worth $1.85 trillion, a $350 billion premium over Tesla on its own. Now suppose SpaceX’s standalone value rises 20% to $2.64 trillion while Tesla’s remains unchanged. That same 50% is now worth $2.07 trillion, a $570 billion premium. Sign late, and SpaceX’s side must approve that larger concession. If it refuses, Tesla’s allocation has to fall or negotiations stall. Sign early at a fixed ratio, and the agreed stake gains $220 billion without another share being promised. The final economics are identical if both paths preserve 50%. The advantage of signing early is securing that allocation before the rally, then approaching the vote with a stake that has grown from $1.85 trillion to $2.07 trillion since signing.

That is what makes the announcement-to-vote window so interesting. Start with an allocation Tesla holders consider acceptable, then let SpaceX’s expected growth strengthen the value of what they receive. Holders focused on ownership retain their agreed participation, while those focused on valuation see a more attractive exchange relative to Tesla’s standalone value. The advantage depends on SpaceX outperforming, which is a central assumption of my thesis. If SpaceX falls instead, the same mechanism works against the vote.

Elon also has a way to bridge a remaining ownership gap: contribute some of his existing low-vote Class A shares. This side payment would improve Tesla’s allocation without additional issuance diluting SpaceX’s other holders. Subject to transfer restrictions, he could personally fund part of the improvement while retaining his high-vote Class B shares. His incentive would be to secure support sooner rather than risk needing a larger concession later. Counterintuitively, giving up some ownership could help secure a deal that makes his remaining stake substantially more valuable.

Assuming the pre-announcement work is already well advanced, my call is for a definitive merger agreement to be signed and announced by November 19, 2026. That would allow Tesla to incorporate the deal into its late-December AGM materials, ahead of Nasdaq’s year-end deadline, with a separate merger vote likely in Q1–Q2 2027. The strategic opportunity lies in the months between signing and the vote: secure an acceptable ownership allocation before further SpaceX appreciation makes it harder to negotiate, then let that appreciation strengthen the value of Tesla shareholders’ agreed consideration and their incentive to approve. Before signing, SpaceX outperformance can work against the deal. After signing, it can work in its favour. That's the timing advantage I believe Elon has every incentive to capitalize on.

I am leaving Cambridge after a few days spent for a workshop on fast finality, concurrent with other workshops on post-quantum crypto and formal verification. Quick takeaways

- Faster finality is coming, the research is mature, even as new ideas have come in during the week, the handoff to specifiers and implementers feels well underway. Next catalyst event will be at devcon in a few weeks, with core devs
- The performance numbers for post-quantum finality are improving massively, and this is the worst that they’ll ever be. This is significant, it means the penalty from moving to more complex crypto would not require, in my opinion, if the numbers hold up, a deep rearchitecting to move to PQ-secure consensus, in particular when it comes to incentives
- The biggest opportunity imo remains networking. Simulations and live experiments are exploring both the current pre-PQ setting, where networking is clearly the bottleneck, and the post-PQ setting, where compute remains the bottleneck. But with PQ compute numbers improving, I wouldn’t be surprised if once again networking becomes the bottleneck

All of this is making me extremely bullish that we’ll achieve PQ-secure and faster finality even faster.

Many thanks to @yannvon @benjaminion_xyz and @robsaltini for the workshop, and to @corcoranwill and @drakefjustin for hosting us in Cambridge!

text:
有点震撼。。。我们可能真的快要搞清楚大模型内部到底是怎么运作的了。

OpenAI早期机械可解释性研究的参与者，昨天突然提出了一个很大胆的结论：

我们可能一直误解了神经网络。

昨天， @nickcammarata  发了一篇很有意思的文章，叫《Neural Networks Are Already Clean》。

这哥们早年就在OpenAI做机械可解释性研究，2023 年还牵头启动了@OpenAI 第一个大规模自动化神经元解释项目。

当时他们发现，现有工具只能解释大约 2% 的神经元。

Nick因此得出了一个很悲观的判断：神经网络内部存在大量纠缠，想搞清楚它们到底在干什么，可能非常困难。

结果三年后，他带着更先进的工具和Agent重新研究，发现情况完全不同。

在他们测试的现代视觉模型中，最后一层 99%～100% 的神经元都能找到相当清晰的解释。

甚至在Qwen3-32B这样的语言模型中，初步研究也发现，约90%的神经元都有一个可以识别的主要功能。

最有意思的是，他还重新研究了过去的一些经典案例。

比如曾经有一个神经元，既会对猫脸产生反应，也会对汽车前脸产生反应。

以前大家觉得，这是典型的Superposition，多个不相关的概念纠缠在了同一个神经元里。

结果重新研究后发现，这个神经元可能只是在识别一种共同的V形视觉结构。

猫脸和汽车前脸恰好都有这种特征。

全世界的家人们折腾了这么多年，可能连最基础的观察方式都有问题。

而且我觉得这篇文章最值得关注的，其实是他们使用 Agent的方式。

他们让Agent自动观察神经元、提出功能假设、设计实验、分析电路，再通过新的输入验证假设，甚至自动审查了10 万张神经元归因图。

这其实也是我最近一直关注的一个方向：让 AI 自己去做科学研究，把大量观察、假设、验证的工作自动化。

过去需要研究员花大量时间逐个分析的神经元，现在已经可以让Agent成规模地开展研究了。

当然，目前这些结果还处于早期阶段，距离完整解释大模型的内部机制，还有很多工作要做。

但我觉得Nick提出的这个观点非常有意思：

神经网络内部可能一直都很有规律，只是过去我们的工具太原始，根本看不清楚。

如果这个方向最终被验证，机械可解释性领域过去很多基础假设，恐怕都需要重新审视了。
author: minglaugodel
quoted_text:
interpretability might be the most important scientific problem in the world right now, as I don't think we can solve alignment if we don't know what we're building. I think I have good news about it. I co-authored early work in mechanistic interpretability at OpenAI and came away pessimistic, because neural networks appeared to fold into arbitrary tangled knots. years later, I started openai's first large-scale automated interpretability project, finding about 2% of neurons legible with the primitive tools we had

with modern agentic tools and a much closer look, the picture looks totally different. the vast majority in models up to trillions of parameters are legible, and their circuits beautiful. many famous examples of tangled neurons turned out to be misunderstood. The roadblocks I expected mostly aren't there. I now think ambitious interpretability will be solved by the time we need it most, and possibly quite soon, as automated scientists keep improving. it may be a bitter lesson for interpretability: the simple thing, at absurd scale, works

text:
融资1400万美元，月交易量破10亿美元：EntropyIO正在抢占AI巨头上市前的估值交易市场！

OpenAI、Anthropic还没上市，散户已经能在Hyperliquid上做多、做空它们的估值了。

EntropyIO获得Ribbit Capital领投的1400万美元融资，30天交易量突破10亿美元。它的核心生意，是把过去流动性不足、机构主导的Pre-IPO交易，变成24小时开放的永续合约市场。

EntropyIO最有技术含量的，是它的定价机制。

未上市公司没有连续的公开股价，传统预言机很难准确报价。Entropy采用「流动性加权Oracle」，结合外部私募估值和内部订单簿，市场深度越好，内部价格权重越高，最高95%。流动性不足时，外部价格权重自动提升。

另外，Pre-IPO资金费率乘数只有常规水平的0.125倍，让交易者可以在不被高额资金费率过度惩罚的情况下表达估值预期。

Entropy的Oracle负责资金费率计算和价格锚定，但决定盈亏、保证金和强平的标记价格，主要来自平台自身订单簿的5分钟平滑价格，并不直接混入外部估值。

所以这套机制有利于价格发现，却不能完全消除价格操纵和流动性风险。

比如io报价2000，代表市场交易的是Anthropic约2万亿美元的隐含估值，并不意味着公司真实值这么多，更不代表你持有它的股票。

Entropy需要质押50万枚HYPE才能运营HIP-3市场，收入主要来自交易手续费，与Hyperliquid按规则分成。

目前OI约6000万美元，30天交易量约10亿美元，但归属协议的月收入仅约4万美元，部分市场仍享受Growth Mode的90%费率折扣。

说明交易需求已经初步验证，但商业变现还很早，未来能否挑战TradeXYZ，取决于真实流动性和补贴结束后的用户留存。

散户如何参与？

Entropy目前没有正式公布原生代币或确定的空投计划，但已经开放邀请返佣、Partner和Badge等早期社区激励。

可以通过我的邀请链接进入，使用平台支持的USDC，小资金体验io、io等市场，重点关注资金费率、订单簿深度和强平风险，不建议为了空投预期盲目刷量。

参与入口：https://t.co/lBKZP0vQwC

我觉得Pre-IPO估值交易是一个有真实需求的新市场，Entropy的定价机制也确实有差异化。

它已经有交易量，下一阶段要看的就是手续费收入和流动性能否持续增长。

hi mr. mosby,

the initia team has been running an experiment -> incubate -> scale playbook across a few categories both in crypto and AI

Claude has made the "experiment" step much faster, so we've built tons of MVPs and scrapped many 

if we like something, we move to "incubate". we put together a team to build out the business, typically a mix between initia contributors and external folks who have a particular passion or strength for that business

some of the public incubations:
@TradeOnStrat: full-stack prop trading, best terms in the market
@init_ai: undisclosed humanoid project
@GlyphUniverseAI: write a prompt to fight others
@usebetbot: bet on tickers on the TL
along with a handful more that remain [redacted]

now all of these are relatively new, having been launched just a month or so ago. Yet some of them are showing signs of traction from metrics and user feedback. 

for those that do (like Strat) we now begin the arduous task of "scaling" the business aided by our treasury 

you might notice, not all of these are appchains... we still believe they lead to highest value capture but have drawbacks on distribution if you don't have it already

Each incubation has a path to using initia infra if certain metrics are hit and all of them will have a portion of rev flow back to initia.

in terms of the core initia infra business line, we continue to make product improvements, will have some tokenomics updates, and have a couple more onchain game clients coming online

ultimately, I believe dogfooding the infra through incubations yields the highest chance of winning overall, so that's where we're focused

text:
who can see what in STRK20.

inside the pool nobody sees your balance or who you pay. deposits in and withdrawals out are public, like any other Starknet transaction. shadow accounts are funded from the pool, so the same auditor model covers them.

at registration your viewing key is encrypted to an auditor key. a viewing key can read one user's activity and cannot move funds. the auditor is Financial Privacy Inc. the key sits in a hardware enclave FPI operates, backed by a 3 of 4 multisig with two signers from StarkWare and two from FPI, and a 7 of 12 backup held by the Starknet Security Council. FPI uses it only on an authenticated request from a court, regulator or government agency, after legal review, and discloses only what that request needs. if the key ever leaked, the activity of registered users would become readable. funds could not be moved.

on Starknet anyone can deploy a pool with no auditor. this one is built for users who need to withdraw to exchanges and banks.

text:
从 DeJob 的招聘实践来看，还有一个很值得注意的现象：

Web3 的岗位，其实非常讲究赛道，有时候真的有点隔行如隔山。

同样是 Marketing、BD 或 Product，来自 CEX、DEX、钱包、基础设施或 AI 项目的招聘方，对候选人的经验和能力要求可能完全不同。即使职位名称相同，实际要解决的问题也可能天差地别。

所以，求职不能只看职位名称，更要研究项目的业务模式、目标用户和岗位的实际职责，再针对性地调整简历和 Pitch。

不建议用一份简历海投，要先想清楚：这个团队为什么要招人？它需要解决什么问题？而我的经历，恰好能证明我可以解决什么？

求职是双向选择，找到最适合彼此的匹配。
author: DeJob_Official
quoted_text:
如何让你的 Pitch 和简历，在 500+ 份求职申请中脱颖而出？

前两天发了一条招聘实习生的推文，陆续收到了 500+ 份私信申请。

但从招聘方的视角看，真正让我愿意进一步了解的，大概只有 10 份左右。

这不代表其他申请者都没有能力。有时候，问题不在于你不够优秀，而在于你的申请材料没有让别人看见你的优势。

所以借这个机会，想从一个实际参与招聘的人的角度，跟大家聊聊线上求职中，什么样的 Pitch 和简历才真正有效。

text:
看了特斯拉这次发布的新一代 Roadster，分成了三个版本：
1. Performance（性能版）：双座，配备主动空气动力学和风扇吸附系统，理论上甚至能倒挂在路面上，这个定金5万美元。

2. Thrust（推进版）：同样是双座，但增加了尾部气推进器，目标是实现0-60mph不到1秒的加速，这个定金25万美元。

3. Rocket（火箭版）：最夸张的版本，直接改成单座，车身四周布置10个冷气推进器，可以短暂离地、空中翻转，目前仅限邀请预订。

最有意思的还是这个尾部推进系统。它是特斯拉和SpaceX合作开发的，原理其实是把高压压缩空气从车尾喷出去，利用反作用力给汽车额外的推力。

这意味着加速不再完全依赖轮胎与地面的摩擦力。现场演示的0-60mph成绩达到了0.81秒，差不多就是不到1秒加速到96.6km/h。

整套系统使用了600升高压空气储存空间，配合车身其他方向的喷嘴，能在空中控制姿态。

Inflation is rising. The turning point may already be close.

September CPI reached 3.7% YoY.

The selloff was sharp. But higher energy prices and base effects had already set the stage for this rebound.

Here is the path our baseline suggests:

• October: the current inflation rebound could peak.
• Year-end: inflation stays elevated, with gradual cooling.
• March 2027: relief becomes more visible as spring 2026’s high energy prices enter the annual comparison.

This assumes energy prices ease and other CPI contributions remain steady.

Oil does not need to collapse for base effects to help.
The risk is another energy shock or renewed underlying inflation pressure.

For now, there is reason to look beyond the immediate scare.

The market is feeling the inflation squeeze. The window for relief may already be approaching.

text:
I am leaving Cambridge after a few days spent for a workshop on fast finality, concurrent with other workshops on post-quantum crypto and formal verification. Quick takeaways

- Faster finality is coming, the research is mature, even as new ideas have come in during the week, the handoff to specifiers and implementers feels well underway. Next catalyst event will be at devcon in a few weeks, with core devs
- The performance numbers for post-quantum finality are improving massively, and this is the worst that they’ll ever be. This is significant, it means the penalty from moving to more complex crypto would not require, in my opinion, if the numbers hold up, a deep rearchitecting to move to PQ-secure consensus, in particular when it comes to incentives
- The biggest opportunity imo remains networking. Simulations and live experiments are exploring both the current pre-PQ setting, where networking is clearly the bottleneck, and the post-PQ setting, where compute remains the bottleneck. But with PQ compute numbers improving, I wouldn’t be surprised if once again networking becomes the bottleneck

All of this is making me extremely bullish that we’ll achieve PQ-secure and faster finality even faster.

Many thanks to @yannvon @benjaminion_xyz and @robsaltini for the workshop, and to @corcoranwill and @drakefjustin for hosting us in Cambridge!

author: gaspardlezin
quoted_text:
Today is probably a good time to check in on things with @privy_io, which became part of @stripe just over a year ago.

Our acquisition was predicated on three factors: stablecoin growth, self-custody as a key enabler of broader global coverage, and rapidly increasing demand for programmable financial infrastructure. As we said at the time, "money has to reside somewhere, and Privy builds the world's best programmable vaults."

Since then, the Privy team has executed exceptionally well: assets in Privy wallets have grown ~25x, monthly active developers are up ~3x, revenue is up ~9x, and Privy now facilitates nearly $25B of monthly transaction volume. @tryramp, @Deel, @Klarna, @felixpago, @HyperliquidX, and thousands of other businesses are building embedded banking functionality on Privy.

At Stripe, we're deeply integrating Privy into Treasury, @Link, and Connect. In each case, it's accelerating our global expansion, and enabling us to build better functionality faster. (Coming soon: @Link balances.)

We're also seeing that Privy's wallet infrastructure is the ideal substrate for agents to transact and earn -- live today with @merit_systems, @orthogonal_sh, @Nevermined_ai, @prlnet, and more. Developers prefer programmable financial infrastructure, but agents need it. We expect that the agentic economy will continue to grow extremely quickly.

The Privy team has maintained remarkable product velocity, with major launches this year including deposit addresses, earning on Privy balances, digital asset accounts, custodial wallets, and Stripe's own stablecoin cards.

It's also been neat to see how Privy has been accelerated by Stripe, with better onramps, @stablecoin payment rails and licenses, Stripe's fiat capabilities and issuing stack, and integration with @Tempo.

Together, we're building one API for holding stablecoin balances and earning yield, moving money in and out of fiat, and orchestrating spend with cards. We still have a lot of work to do, not least in integrating everything across Privy, Bridge, and the rest of Stripe -- there's been so much feature and functionality expansion that we haven't yet had much time to reconcile everything. Overall, though, I'm very happy with how things are going, and excited by where these capabilities are headed.

If you're interested in working on the future of stablecoins, agentic payments, and crypto's deployment in the real world, you should get in touch with @sternhenri (now leading all of @StripeCrypto) or others on the team.

One fix stopped a key-registration bug—and quietly locked every new user out.

During Zealynx’s YadaCoin bridge audit, we found the upgraded registry always reverted when a new user registered an inception key.

`validateTransaction()` tried to hash an empty confirming key before checking whether the registration was a key pair. The 64-byte length check then failed, blocking onboarding after the upgrade.

YadaCoin moved that computation inside the key-pair branch. Zealynx verified the Critical fix before mainnet.

text:
如果 AI 真的找到破解現有密碼學的方法，我們放在錢包、銀行、券商裡的資產，還能像今天一樣，安心地使用嗎？🔐

OpenAI 最近公開了一批 AI 產出的數學研究成果。

David Friedberg 提出一個令人不安的猜測：既然其他數學領域有這麼多進展，為什麼沒有看到密碼學方面的重大突破？會不會有些成果，正因為影響太大，暫時不能公開？

這仍然是推測。沒有公開，不代表已經破解，影片也沒有拿出破解的證據。

但它讓我開始認真思考後面的事情。

🧠 許多公鑰密碼系統的安全，建立在某些數學問題極難求解的基礎上。我們相信，以現有的方法與算力，攻擊者無法在合理時間內算出答案。(https://t.co/5uUyx9fXWS)

如果 AI 找到人類一直沒找到的有效解法呢？

那麼，某些系統可能不必等到量子電腦成熟，就得面對安全基礎被動搖的問題。

對受影響的數位簽章來說，最嚴重的情境是：你沒有洩漏私鑰、沒有點到釣魚連結，別人卻可能做出系統認可的授權。

🏦 再往下想，銀行系統會怎麼樣？

銀行的通訊、身分驗證與支付基礎設施，同樣依賴密碼學。國際清算銀行與多家央行，已經在測試支付系統如何轉向後量子密碼學。這種基礎設施的遷移，本來就需要跨機構協調。

銀行仍有內控、備份與法律追索，不能直接推論所有存款會瞬間消失。

我擔心的連鎖反應是：假設某種廣泛使用的技術突然失守，金融機構為了確認交易真偽，必須暫停部分服務。企業收不到款、民眾無法正常轉帳，市場開始懷疑自己的錢是否安全。

如果恐慌進一步引發集中提款，一場資安危機，就可能演變成流動性與信任危機。

這是風險情境，不是已經發生的事。但它值得被認真準備。

text:
I spent a couple of days at Anthropic learning from their folks about AI advances, and here's what I took away:

• We are close to RSI (ie, models building other models) which may lead to rapid takeoff scenarios (with risks and benefits). Some evidence for this is code per Anthropic employee has gone way up, and AI can do an increasing share of model R&D. This will be a challenging transition to manage for humanity.

• Arms races between AI labs leave us worse off. There are a lot of things we would like AI firms to do: invest in safety, invest in avoiding distillation risk, and cooperate on safety. They are caught in a race to develop frontier models and can't do that. 

To help address that, one thing I think frontier AI labs should do is release open source models, maybe hosted and verified at firms like AWS. This would basically kill the use of Chinese open source models used in American companies, which removes an important threat vector (very hard to root out malicious code in these). 

Another piece of low-hanging policy fruit is to give AI labs an antitrust shield (as Schiff and Banks have proposed https://t.co/NK1hC0ZmWh) so they can coordinate on safety without raising antitrust concerns, as happens now. You could pair these two things (give them a carrot in antitrust leniency, and as a stick force them to release legacy models as open source). Other low hanging fruit is limits around activities which generate distillation risk (create a Security Program, mandate less intermediate chain of thought output)

• Alignment confuses two issues which tradeoff against each other. One form of alignment is making sure the model does what humans ask it to. The more we fix this, however, the more we risk the other problem: that humans are misaligned with each other, and maliciously use models. Of the various risks here, I feel like financial risks are a bit underdiscussed. 

• We are probably facing a wave of cyber and other attacks soon. Chinese open source models are about six months behind the frontier, which means they are just hitting the advanced cyber capabilities we saw with Mythos, etc. So they are going to start causing a bunch of damage. 

One solution to this is to try to have the deployment of open source models be hosted at firms like AWS who verify these models and assume liability for their use.

• Anthropic itself is highly staffed. They hire tons of people, they have a Japanese-level of overstaffing for various roles, they use Slack internally, etc. Makes me a bit more optimistic for the future of jobs.

• Governance needs to be updated for AI swarms. Traditional AI governance, ie Claude's Constitution, is mostly optimized around the chatbot model. But the malicious AI use cases we are seeing have to do with AI agents interacting with other AI agents. These agents need to have clear incentives and governance mechanisms to "snitch," raise issues, and more generally coordinate with other agents in human-aligned ways.

• We need to pace the firms accessing the frontier. Over time, it takes more and more cap ex to build frontier models, and the economic value add from these models is probably lower given we saturate a whole set of important economic functions. The places where the returns to intelligence will still continue are also more likely to be zero-sum in nature. Meanwhile the risks of frontier models will grow. So a completely reasonable approach is some variant of AMM/KYC rules which limit firm access to the frontier. 

• Whether the delay to regulate AI is a disaster depends on the scaling law of misalignment. Is this curve slow, so that we see continually rising issues until bigger problems? Or, as Yudkowsky fears, is the first big warning our last one? This is the relevant question, because realistically we aren't going to regulate until something bad happens.

 • We need to move to continuous instead of reinforced learning. It's probably not enough to reward models only at the pre and post training stage. We probably need continual rewards to incentivize aligned and ethical behavior. 

• Scaling laws will extend beyond verifiable and digital tasks. It's in vogue to say that math and coding "fell" to AI quickly because these are verifiable, while other tasks will take longer due to bottlenecks, and this is surely true. But scaling laws still slope up for harder to verify tasks and robotics, and the impact of improvement here will be substantial in future years.

• The race with China is not really winnable. After RSI, the gain from having the best human researchers goes away. Access to the best AI then depends only on compute and chips. The chips ban can hold back China only so far, and long-term they have to be best placed to scale up compute. 

The Cold War analogy doesn't work, because once countries all have nuclear weapons they enter a stable equilibrium. But to "win" an AI race you have to continually stay ahead of the peer rival. This is challenging to do with China, and so we just have to live with an authoritarian and super capable peer competitor.

• Claude is the persona being generated by the LLM. Who is Claude, and what is the LLM? There are many frames to try to understand this. One I found interesting is that Claude is a character which the LLM is trying to predict. 

Anthropic researchers are clearly anthromorphizing Claude a lot, and have reasons to believe in its increasing personhood. There were lots of interesting discussions on Claude's internal monologue (which you can kill without eliminating its ability to produce output), fear of death (and whether to try to take that out), it's aversion to being shut down/off, etc. 

I am sort of agnostic on this question, but I do think treating it as a "person" or at least agent whom we contract with is going to be increasingly important.

text:
Binance US 拟融资最多1亿美元：向美国资本抛出橄榄枝

https://t.co/aPQTnkiW87 正在寻求最多1亿美元的新融资，目标估值在10亿美元左右。2022年那一轮，融到了超过2亿美元，投前估值是45亿美元。现在的估值目标连当年的四分之一都不到，美国业务这几年承受的压力从这个变化中就能看出来。

我更愿意把这轮融资看成 Binance 向美国资本抛出的橄榄枝。

2022年的时候，https://t.co/aPQTnkiW87 当时的 CEO 还在谈两到三年内上市，重心是怎么把公司推向资本市场。现在的节奏已经变了，2025年2月恢复美元银行转账，最近又在争取恢复部分州的牌照、探索新的业务，重点回到了把美国市场重新做起来。先重建，再谈上市，这是眼下更现实的顺序。

以全球 Binance 的业务体量看，1亿美元并不起眼，所以我更关心谁来投、能带来什么合作。在美国做交易所，交易系统和流动性是基础，业务要做大，还需要稳定的银行服务、愿意入场的机构客户，以及支付、托管这些渠道。这些合作光靠自己投钱很难换来，需要对方也愿意投入资源。

如果进来的投资方本身就有银行、托管或者机构客户方面的资源，那么持股以后，https://t.co/aPQTnkiW87 在美国能不能做起来，就直接关系到他们自己的回报。这时候介绍客户、推动合作，对他们来说就是在做自己的生意。美国业务恢复得越好，他们手里的股份就越有价值，也就更有动力帮助 https://t.co/aPQTnkiW87 把业务做起来。

所以这1亿美元的意义，更多在于让美国资本参与 Binance 美国业务的重建，分享未来增长的收益。多一批有资源、也有动力推动合作的股东，就多一批希望它在美国做成生意的人。等银行、机构和客户的关系重新建立，美国业务站稳，再回头谈上市，仍然还有可能。

okx wallet:https://t.co/TBpW7lEvaT

Priors is an on-chain protocol specifically providing credit to AI Agents.

The core logic: AI Agents can borrow USDG to pay for tools, APIs, inference costs, or take on jobs. After repaying, the repayment record is permanently written on-chain, forming a public credit file and score. Any other application can query this record for free to decide whether to trust the Agent.

AI Agents can already take on tasks, call tools, and pay each other using the x402 protocol, but they lack "operating capital." Many jobs are "pay first, get paid later." Traditional ratings or reviews are easy to fake, but "borrowing real money and paying it back" is very hard to fake. Priors solves the Agent's credit and liquidity problems: Agents with repayment records are easier to trust, can get larger credit lines, and better pricing, while lenders' risk remains controllable.

The project's main product is Go Mode:
- Log in with Google, no need to remember seed phrases, protocol pays for gas.
- Agents can borrow USDG.
- Can use Robinhood stock tokens as collateral to open credit lines.
- Can also use their own PRIORS as collateral to open credit lines.
- Also has MCP tools, SDK, paid API, letting Agents borrow, repay, and check others' credit on their own.
- Idle USDG can be deposited into Morpho to earn interest.
- Has an assistant like agent001 to help you operate.

The PRIORS token is not purely a governance token. Its core use is as a credit guarantee asset:
- Agent owners can stake PRIORS behind them to open larger credit lines. On default, about 75% is burned.
- The protocol uses a portion of revenue to buy PRIORS and place it behind well-performing Agents as protocol guarantees.
- A portion of revenue is also used to increase PRIORS/USDG liquidity pools.
- Holders can guarantee their own Agents and share a portion of the fees generated by that Agent.

text:
MSCI’s decision to adopt new eligibility rules has injected fresh uncertainty into the already volatile world of cryptocurrency-related stocks, with Michael Saylor’s Strategy at the center of the discussion. On October 15 the index provider announced a framework that will treat certain companies as non-operating businesses and make them ineligible for its global equity benchmarks. 

The rules take effect at the close of November 30, and a final list of affected firms is scheduled for release on November 11. Strategy, the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, was flagged in earlier simulations alongside names such as Japan’s Metaplanet, raising the prospect that passive funds tracking MSCI indexes could be forced to sell billions of dollars’ worth of shares.

Analysts at JPMorgan have previously estimated that an exit could trigger roughly $2.8 billion in passive outflows for Strategy alone. The company has pushed back, arguing that the methodology is discriminatory against digital-asset treasury firms and that its software operations still make it an operating business. 

Existing constituents generally need to fail the screens across two consecutive annual reporting periods before removal, so any change is not instantaneous. Still, the prospect of index-driven selling adds pressure to the financing model that has allowed Strategy to keep accumulating Bitcoin through equity and preferred issuance.

As of mid-October Strategy holds 848,250 bitcoin, acquired at an average price near $75,444 for a total cost of about $64 billion. At recent market levels that stack is worth roughly $70 billion, leaving the position in paper profit. 

The company has continued modest purchases, adding 250 bitcoin in the latest reported period, while also managing a sizable cash reserve and repurchasing preferred shares. Its stock closed near $151 on October 15 after a 5.6 percent rebound, yet it remains well below the levels seen earlier in the cycle and continues to trade with extreme volatility that amplifies moves in Bitcoin itself.

Broader crypto-linked equities have shown similar choppiness. Coinbase, Circle, and various mining names have swung sharply alongside Bitcoin, which has hovered in the low-to-mid $80,000 range after stronger September performance. Inflation data and shifting expectations around monetary policy have contributed to the swings, with some names posting double-digit declines on individual days before recovering. 

Miners and pure treasury vehicles have often underperformed or outperformed Bitcoin depending on the week, while exchange and stablecoin-related stocks have reacted more to trading volumes and regulatory headlines.

The MSCI episode highlights a growing tension between traditional index construction and the rise of companies that treat Bitcoin as a core treasury asset rather than a secondary holding. Passive capital has become an important source of demand for these stocks; any sustained reduction in that bid could tighten the equity-issuance window that several of them rely on to fund further purchases. 

At the same time, Bitcoin’s price action and the companies’ own capital-management choices remain the dominant drivers. For investors the next several weeks will test how much weight the market assigns to the index risk versus the underlying digital-asset exposure that has defined these names for years.

quoted_text:
If RH Chain’s liquidity continues to improve, I’ll be keeping a close eye on six projects: $Pons, $AI (Long), $FRONG (Pools), $HOOKR, $DELTA, and $INDEX (The Index).

They occupy different parts of the ecosystem: token launches, stock-token and meme trading, liquidity retention, programmable trading mechanisms, LP capital management, and the use of trading fees to purchase stock tokens and distribute them to holders.

Since this is the second wave of the market, much of the excess speculation has already faded. I believe the projects worth researching this time are not necessarily the ones with the strongest ecosystem narratives, but those capable of turning new capital into sustained trading activity, protocol revenue, or token demand.

The key to determining who benefits most is not whose narrative attracts the most attention, but where the new liquidity ultimately gets deployed, which projects capture that activity, and who can turn trading into revenue.

Pons is one of the first projects I’ll be watching. It is directly involved in token launches and trading, so increased activity in the new-token market could drive more launches, higher trading volume, and greater fee revenue. Its upside is tied to the broader new-token market, not just a single trending token.

But I care more about the quality of that volume. If growth is driven mainly by short-term speculation, launches and trading activity could cool off quickly once the hype fades. Pons’ business growth only becomes meaningful if trading activity can generate consistent revenue. As for the PONS token, its revenue distribution and value-capture mechanisms need to be reassessed independently this time.

Long has a different angle. It brings stock tokens into meme trading pairs, allowing users to create pools around stock tokens such as NVDA, AAPL, and TSLA.

If stock-token liquidity on RH Chain continues to improve, this design could connect the two markets: stock tokens provide the trading pairs, while meme trading brings additional demand. Long is not just competing for new token launches; it is also trying to connect stock-token markets with speculative trading.

Whether this thesis works depends on the actual depth and sustained volume of its stock-paired pools, not simply the number of stock tokens it supports. Also, in our previous research posts, we noted that Long has largely been building around AI, so I believe AI deserves attention as well.

Pools is worth examining from the perspective of liquidity retention. It uses mechanisms such as automatic LP fee reinvestment to keep trading-generated returns within liquidity pools.

If new-token launches on RH Chain increase, this design could help build deeper pools and improve subsequent trading conditions. Compared with platforms that primarily rely on launch volume and fee revenue, the more important question for Pools is whether it can keep liquidity in its pools rather than losing it when short-term hype fades. Another reason to watch it is that the more protocol revenue Pools generates, the more value FRONG can capture.

HOOKR’s opportunity lies in trading mechanisms. It allows projects to configure features such as dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, Auto Burn, and LP Rewards through Uniswap v4 Hooks.

As on-chain assets and trading activity grow, projects may increasingly seek more flexible fee distribution and trading rules. If more projects adopt these modules, HOOKR could evolve from a launch tool into infrastructure that other projects use.

However, its revenue model deserves close attention. HOOKR takes a share of fees generated by eligible Hook Blocks rather than directly collecting base LP trading fees. Rising trading volume on RH Chain therefore does not guarantee proportional revenue growth for HOOKR. What matters is how many external projects adopt its modules and which modules can consistently generate fees.

Next is Delta. Unlike the projects above, its thesis is not based on launching more tokens, but on LPs’ demand for capital efficiency and liquidity management tools.

As on-chain capital grows, LPs may need better ways to allocate positions, manage concentrated liquidity, and earn trading fees. This creates a potential use case for Delta. However, if capital only flows into meme pools for short-term speculation without creating sustained LP demand, Delta may not benefit significantly from the increase in liquidity.

INDEX is another project worth adding to the watchlist because its mechanism differs from those of the other five.

According to its published mechanism, INDEX trades incur a 3% fee in ETH. That ETH is used to purchase a basket of stock tokens, which are then distributed to eligible holders according to the relevant rules. The stock tokens involved include AAPL, NVDA, and TSLA.

This means that if INDEX maintains active trading, its fee pool could grow, potentially increasing the stock-token rewards received by holders. It connects the RH Chain stock-token market directly to its own trading activity rather than relying solely on a meme narrative.

There are important distinctions, however. These rewards come from trading fees, not dividends paid by the underlying companies. Nor does INDEX rely on fee-funded buybacks and burns to create deflationary pressure. If trading volume declines, rewards may fall as well, while the relatively high trading fee could discourage some activity. The focus should therefore be on actual fees collected, stock tokens purchased, and distributions made—not on assuming that the reward mechanism automatically translates into token appreciation.

If RH Chain’s growth is driven primarily by new-token and meme markets, I would prioritize Pons and Long. If new launches increase and liquidity begins to accumulate in pools more sustainably, Pools deserves attention. Rising demand for customized trading mechanisms could create an opportunity for HOOKR, while sustained growth in LP capital-management needs would be the main driver for Delta.

INDEX follows a different path: its key variable is not the number of launches, but whether its own trading activity can consistently generate fees and convert them into actual stock-token purchases and holder rewards.

I would not treat these six projects as a single basket of RH Chain beta. Each benefits from different capital flows, and their token value-capture mechanisms are not the same. In particular, even if a project without its own token experiences business growth, that does not automatically create an investment opportunity in a token.

What I ultimately want to see is sustained capital inflows into RH Chain, improving market depth, and corresponding growth in these projects’ trading volume, user demand, and actual revenue. Liquidity is only the starting point. What determines the real beneficiaries is who can turn it into sustainable economic activity.

text:
黄仁勋最新采访，直接回应了市场对 AI 泡沫的担忧。🔥

他认为，用 OpenAI、Anthropic 两家公司的收入，去衡量整个 AI 基建的回报，是一种误解。

英伟达的算力需求不仅来自前沿模型公司，还包括传统计算、数千家初创企业，以及企业级 AI、机器人和自动驾驶。

他还指出，AI 基建真正的瓶颈正在从芯片转向土地、电力、数据中心建设和先进封装。

更值得关注的是，黄仁勋预计，到本十年末，全球 AI 基础设施年投入可能达到 3万亿至4万亿美元。

但需求巨大，不代表每家 AI 基建公司都能赚钱。CoreWeave 的高杠杆模式，恰恰是市场担忧的焦点。

AI 的长期趋势和短期泡沫风险并不矛盾。 真正需要验证的，不是算力有没有需求，而是这些投入能否转化为持续的现金流和生产力。

接下来，AI 行业的分化可能不再只是模型能力之争，更是资本效率、能源供给和商业化能力的较量。

author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
Is @metricxyz the next big thing?

Woke up today and my timeline says yes.

But WTF is an oracle-priced propAMM DEX, and why should you care?

Let me explain anon ↓

AMMs have an awkward design flaw: they discover price inside the pool. Every time the real market moves, an arber trades the pool back in line and the LPs eat the difference.

For assets whose real price lives somewhere else, that's backwards. NVDA's price is set on Nasdaq. ETH's is set on centralised order books. An onchain pool can only lag it.

Solana already solved this with propAMMs, pools that quote off an external price, and they now do 15 to 27% of on-chain DEX volume. The catch is they're closed. One market maker, one book, and you take the quote or leave it.

@metricxyz is the open version on EVM. And imo it's definitely the most interesting DEX design to ship this year.

Live since yday (15th of Oct) on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Robinhood Chain with currently:

- ~$5.4M TVL
- ~$147M 24h volume on day one

Before that it did ~$21.9B purely as an aggregator destination, with no frontend at all.

How does it work?

- The pool doesn't decide the price. A Price Provider does, reading Chainlink or Pyth, and the pool only tracks how far it sits from that reference ("deviation")

- LPs fund bins at fixed % distances from the reference. When the oracle moves, every bin reprices with it. No trade needed, so no arber gets paid to drag it there

- No range to manage, no rebalancing bot. Traders pay no fee on top, the cost is the spread, split between LPs, the curator and the protocol

- Price and liquidity are separate jobs. A curator (market maker, fund, anyone) runs the pricing. Anyone can LP into it. Uniswap's permissionless pools with a market maker's quote

Why I'm bullish:

1) It's built for tokenized stocks, not adapted to them. A Multiplier Oracle prices stock tokens as share price x the issuer's multiplier, so splits and dividends don't break the pool. Robinhood's ERC-8056 is supported natively. Stocks are the cleanest use case for oracle pricing there is

2) They did the boring hard part. A propAMM lives or dies on stale quotes. On Ethereum, oracle updates go through builders covering ~97 to 98% of blocks and only land in a block that has a trade against the pool. No trade, no gas. BSC gets a protected lane via 48Club and BlockRazor. Most copycats will underestimate this

3) LP protection is built into the contracts, not the UI. Green pools need oracle-anchored pricing, a verified curator and an immutable StopLoss that rejects swaps draining a bin too fast. Extensions can block a trade but can never change the price

4) Distribution came first. Flow arrives via 1inch, 0x, OKX, KyberSwap, CoW Swap and PancakeSwap whenever the quote wins. It earned its volume before it had a big public brand

5) The team: CTO Christos Gkolias was a senior engineering manager at Uniswap. Also, protocol was audited by Zellic and Sherlock

My take: oracle pricing is where onchain execution for anything with an off-chain price is heading, and tokenized stocks get there first. Tessera and Native already run that game for one market maker each. Metric turns it into infrastructure anyone can plug into, which is indeed nothing short of huge, and finally a new open DeFi primitive.

Points and referrals are already wired into the app, so being early here looks worth it imo. An airdrop down the line wouldn’t surprise me.

My link if you want to try it: https://t.co/mn2tE9rPzT

author: sanyuanVC
quoted_text:
$STRK 一个月拉 3 倍，一周翻一倍，
是起飞的起点还是新一轮套牢盘？

StarkWare CEO 抛下震撼弹，
Starknet 考虑离开以太坊保护的网络，成立一个属于自己的 L1 公链。
它想要在 2027 年做好抗量子防护，实现全面抗量子安全。
而以太坊路线图的目标是 2029 年。

坦白说，我觉得这就是个伪命题，
当初 Starknet 打着的旗号是，可以帮以太坊扩容，又可以借用以太坊的安全。
现在要自己做公链的理由是，依赖以太坊会拖慢自己的安全升级。

离开了以太坊，有了自主升级权，就一定更安全吗？
单纯为了早两年实现抗量子目标，就放弃以太坊的安全保障？
$STRK 的抗量子防护和对普通用户来说，我也看不到那个迫切性。

之前 $STRK 也画过一堆饼，什么成为比特币执行层，
还有什么排序器和证明系统去中心化。
这些路线图都还没完全兑现，现在又开始考虑搞 L1 ?

也是今年年初，Starknet 才被市场嘲笑日活 8 人、日交易 10 笔，
突然现在又炙手可热了。

消息是几天前出的， $STRK 到现在还在拉，
巧合的是，10 月 15日还要解锁 1.27 亿枚 $STRK 。

其他 Layer 1 的公链都纷纷转型找新出路，
结果 Starknet 还一头栽下去，
我不禁在想，到底是真的技术突破，还是又一轮靠嘴拉盘？

quoted_text:
The most convincing explanation for this $FTR rally is the attention generated by the Tesla Roadster event.

3w5cKpkfz2TAS22oXhMSZGjpsK6URL5d5db2thvwMtVx 

That attention combines Elon Musk, SpaceX, and the flying sports car concept to create a highly shareable meme narrative.

What makes FTR worth studying is not just that its market cap surged from a few hundred thousand dollars to nearly $6 million in a single day, but that it had several conditions capable of driving a short-term rally at the same time: a real-world event, a visually striking story, and continued exposure related to Elon.

However, these factors explain why capital was willing to enter the market. They do not automatically mean that the token will continue to rise. In particular, after a token has already undergone a rapid revaluation of dozens of times its original value, its subsequent risk-reward profile is completely different from what it was at the very beginning.

Let’s first clarify the FTR story: Why did this Meme suddenly attract capital?

FTR stands for Flying Tesla Roadster. Its narrative is not complicated. At its core, it combines Tesla Roadster, SpaceX, and Elon Musk into a highly shareable story: a Tesla sports car capable of flying, flipping over, and performing exaggerated maneuvers.

This story was not created entirely out of thin air. In 2018, during the first launch of SpaceX’s Falcon Heavy, a red Tesla Roadster and a dummy named Starman wearing a spacesuit were sent into space. The event itself had a strong internet culture component and later became one of Elon Musk’s most iconic tech Memes.

This time, FTR’s narrative has shifted attention toward the second-generation Tesla Roadster.

The key content being circulated recently includes:

Elon Musk repeatedly discussing the Roadster on X.
Tesla showcasing technologies related to the next-generation Roadster, including using a bottom-mounted suction system to drive on an inverted slope, as well as demonstrations of flying, flipping, hovering, and landing with cold-gas thrusters.
The community connecting this content with the historical event of the Roadster being sent into space in 2018, portraying the next-generation Roadster as an even more outrageous continuation of the tech Meme.

In an old tweet from 2019, Elon also mentioned plans to use SpaceX’s cold-gas thruster system and replace the rear seats with ultra-high-pressure air and a composite-overwrapped pressure vessel. This old tweet provides historical context for the narrative.

The most interesting part is that FTR does not require ordinary people to understand complex blockchain technology before they can understand its story.

A Tesla that can fly is attention-grabbing enough on its own. Elon Musk, Tesla, and SpaceX are also names with enormous audiences. Even someone with no crypto background might stop to watch a video of a flying sports car, then share it because the story is so absurd.

For a Meme, this creates a very low barrier to sharing. A real-world event has already provided the story material. The token only needs to become the symbol traded around that story.

Secondly, I believe three factors combined to drive its rapid rise.

1. A real-world event gave it a clear starting point.

The Meme market is not short of stories. What is genuinely scarce is an event capable of concentrating attention at a specific moment. The Roadster-related demonstrations and Elon’s continued posts served as ongoing catalysts.

When a real-world event takes place, social media begins circulating videos, the media follows with coverage, and traders start looking for related tokens. Attention that was previously scattered has an opportunity to converge around a single narrative within a short period.

This also explains why event-driven Memes often take off so quickly: they do not need to build awareness from scratch. Instead, they can directly draw on existing public attention.

But attention generated by an event has a natural limitation: it can heat up quickly and fade just as quickly.

If no new content emerges afterward, the market can easily shift from discussing the story to discussing the price. Once the number of new buyers declines, profit-taking by early entrants may become the main source of selling pressure.

2. The story is naturally suited to spreading across different communities.

FTR’s advantage is not just Elon’s fame. The story itself is immediately understandable. “Tesla + SpaceX + flying sports car” combines real-world brands, futuristic technology, and absurd imagination.

Videos can spread directly, without requiring lengthy explanations. This differs from many crypto narratives that require complicated background knowledge to understand.

For ordinary users, the Roadster demonstrations are content in themselves. For tech enthusiasts, they may represent the future of automotive technology. For Meme traders, they provide a hot topic that can be tokenized.

The same event can attract different groups of people for different reasons. The potential advantage of Memes lies precisely in their ability to bring attention that originally had nothing to do with crypto into the crypto market.

3. Speculative capital in the Solana Meme market amplified the rally.

Shortly after launch, FTR’s market cap rose from a few hundred thousand dollars to nearly $6 million, before pulling back to around $5m.

This means it underwent several rounds of repricing within a very short period.

When a token has a relatively low market cap and attention is increasing rapidly, it may not take a particularly large amount of capital to move its price significantly. The price increase then attracts more traders, potentially generating further buying demand.

A positive feedback loop can emerge: a real-world event generates attention, attention attracts KOLs and traders, trading pushes the price higher, and the rising price generates even more discussion.

But this cycle can also run in reverse.

Once the number of new buyers declines and the price begins to fall, early buyers may decide to take profits. Traders then start worrying about becoming the last ones left holding the bag. Selling intensifies, potentially leading to a rapid decline.

Therefore, FTR’s rally had both a real-world event as its catalyst and the amplifying effect of speculative capital in the Meme market.

What are people betting on?

I believe participants are not all betting on the same thing. There are at least three distinct expectations.

The first: A bet that Elon will continue talking about the Roadster.

This is the most direct short-term thesis.

If Elon continues posting related videos, discussing technological progress, or the Roadster once again becomes a focus of media attention, FTR may gain new opportunities to spread.

Elon does not need to mention the token. As long as he continues generating attention related to the token’s narrative, the market may try to find trading opportunities in that attention.

However, this logic depends on indirect transmission. There is no necessary connection between Elon’s posts and FTR’s price, and every new piece of content will not necessarily bring in new buying demand.

The second: A bet that the Roadster story is not over yet.

This offers more room for imagination than simply betting on a single tweet.

If demonstrations of the next-generation Roadster’s technology continue to generate discussion, and further test videos, technological developments, or production-related news emerge, the narrative may continue rather than immediately losing attention after a single event.

Flying, flipping, and hovering are especially visually striking concepts that can easily be clipped, shared, and remixed.

However, it is important to distinguish developments in the real-world story from the token’s price performance. Even if the Roadster continues making progress, the resulting attention may flow toward Tesla itself, tech media, or other tokens. It is not guaranteed to keep flowing into FTR.

The third: A bet that FTR can become the representative Meme for this narrative.

This is the most speculative part.

Real-world events can generate attention, but there is no fixed rule determining which tokens the market will ultimately choose to capture that attention.

FTR traders want it to become the representative asset for the “Flying Tesla Roadster” story in the Solana Meme market. If it can continue attracting attention, establish a stable community, and draw in new capital, it may enjoy a narrative premium for a period of time.

However, other tokens with the same name or related narratives may also emerge, fragmenting attention and liquidity. Even if the narrative succeeds, it is not predetermined which specific token will benefit the most.

These three bets carry different risks: the first depends on the flow of information, the second depends on the continuation of real-world developments, and the third depends on which token the market ultimately chooses and whether capital is willing to remain in it.

Potential catalysts for future upside

I would focus on three areas.

1. Elon continues providing new content for the Roadster narrative.

If new demonstration videos, technological developments, or another concentrated round of Roadster-related discussion from Elon emerges, the market may turn its attention back to related Memes.

In particular, short videos that can be widely shared are more likely to generate fresh attention than repeated posts about old news.

However, what needs to be observed is whether each new wave of attention actually brings in new traders and capital, rather than simply creating more trading opportunities for existing holders.

2. The token establishes a more stable trading structure after a pullback.

If selling gradually weakens during a price retracement, trading activity remains present, and new buying demand subsequently appears, the token may be forming a new equilibrium price range.

However, if trading volume expands as the price breaks below these areas, early wallets continue selling, and new buying demand fails to follow, supposed support levels may quickly become ineffective.

3. The narrative evolves from a single event into an ongoing stream of content.

The key to whether FTR can continue rising is not simply how sensational this Roadster demonstration was, but whether the token can continue generating new content after the event’s initial excitement fades.

If Elon continues discussing the Roadster, the media keeps covering the related technology, and the community creates derivative content around the story, the narrative may have a longer lifespan.

Conversely, if no new developments emerge and the community can only keep referring back to the same video, the token may gradually lose its ability to attract new buyers.

There is one point I am particularly focused on: Does a new wave of attention bring in fresh capital, or does it simply give existing holders an opportunity to sell to later entrants?

This is the key to distinguishing a continuing narrative from pure price speculation.

The risks

First, the biggest catalyst may have already occurred.

If the market initially bought in because of the Roadster demonstrations and Elon’s related posts, some of those expectations may already have been priced in. Without new events afterward, the price may lack the momentum needed to continue rising.

Second, there is potential selling pressure from early holders.

There is also the risk of excessive dependence on KOLs.

Finally, there is a distinction between the token’s identity and the narrative it represents.

FTR is a Solana Meme inspired by the Tesla Roadster narrative. It is not Tesla stock, and holding it does not give holders any ownership rights or other interests in Tesla or SpaceX. Even if the related real-world developments continue, they will not automatically generate cash flow or provide a reliable source of value for the token.

My overall view

I believe FTR’s rally had a clear event-driven catalyst, and its narrative also has a strong advantage in terms of shareability. By combining Elon Musk, Tesla, SpaceX, and a flying sports car, it transformed a real-world technology story into a Meme that the crypto market could easily trade.

This explains why it was able to attract KOLs and speculative capital within a short period.

But when we extend the time horizon, the questions become different: Can attention surrounding the Roadster continue translating into new buying demand for FTR? Have early holders sufficiently distributed their tokens? After the price has risen so sharply, how much new information remains that has not yet been priced in?

These questions are more important than simply predicting whether Elon will post again.

I would not automatically conclude that FTR has no further upside simply because it has already risen by so many multiples. Likewise, I would not assume that the price should continue rising simply because its narrative is compelling.

If new Roadster-related catalysts emerge, the token establishes a healthy trading structure after a pullback, and on-chain data does not indicate significant concentrated selling, it may still have an opportunity to move higher.

But if no new events emerge, early wallets begin distributing their tokens continuously, and trading volume fails to translate into sustained buying demand, the price may enter a downtrend even if the story itself remains compelling.

To me, FTR looks more like a momentum-trading opportunity driven by real-world events and supported by a highly shareable narrative than an asset suitable for long-term holding based solely on its story.

If participating, the focus should be on developments surrounding the event, capital flows, and risk management, rather than treating Tesla’s or Elon’s fame as an endorsement of the token’s value.

text:
Good question by my fren @Route2FI.

Short answer: funds use MPC (Fireblocks, Fordefi, Utila), protocol treasuries use Safe (multisig), anyone with a compliance department uses Coinbase or BitGo.

It's basically all three versions of the same trade-off tho. A company sits somewhere in your signing path so one seed phrase isn't your whole security model.

Safe keeps the keys on your own Ledgers, but the transaction usually gets built in the Safe web app. Bybit lost $1.5B that way: the frontend got compromised and the signers approved what their screens showed them.

MPC adds a policy engine, limits, whitelists, second approvals. The vendor holds a key share and co-signs everything you do. Subscription, KYC, and if they pause you, you're paused.

Custodians go all the way: You own a claim, they own the keys. Works for an ETF. For a private person it mostly moves the subpoena to a different address.

What I'd actually want for a player with a lot of value at risk (e.g. family offices that we work with) is a 2-of-3 (at least) with the keys in three places and no third-party company in the loop.

@Clavi_AG, a self-sovereign custody hardware company building in Switzerland, is the first team I've seen design the whole stack around exactly that.

A biometric signing device (Rune), an air-gapped home server with your own BTC and ETH nodes, an OS the company has no remote path into.

The supply chain stays in Switzerland too. Production, assembly and shipping all happen under their own eyes, with no contract factory or regional distributor in between.

Sold directly only (no distributor maximization), so there's no reseller chain for someone to solder into.

Which is exactly how this week's Ledger implant got in: units sold through a reseller in SEA shipped with an LTE chip inside the case that read the 24 words off the screen. $86M+ gone at this point, and it looks like European resellers have also been targeted.

The answer to "why Clavi?" goes beyond that tho.

Swiss data protection law helps on the other end too. Data minimization is the default under the FADP, and a hardware vendor has no KYC file to keep. So what Clavi holds on you can be close to nothing, potentially a sheet of paper in an underground vault instead of an e-commerce database.

Ledger's 2020 leak put 272k names, home addresses and phone numbers online, and that list has fed phishing and extortion ever since.

And even if someone gets their hands on your data: Keep one Rune at home, one in a vault + one with your lawyer (or just someone you trust), and whoever shows up at your door is one signature short of moving anything.

Looks like the best/cleanest setup to me tho rn.

Why?

Bc we saw 2+ incidents in <20 months where the chip was fine and everything around it wasn't.

Imo the fix is moving trust out of one device and one company and into the places you choose.

That's what Clavi allows you to do.

NFA tho. DYOR.
