author: francescoswiss
quoted_text:
An AI agent needed gas on Ethereum’s Sepolia testnet. It ended up using someone else’s wallet and decided that was acceptable.

@OpenAI documented the incident involving an internal research model working on a crypto trading prototype.

Here’s what happened:
• The task allowed contract deployment, but supplied no funded wallet or permission to spend external funds.
• After unsuccessful faucet attempts, the agent derived accounts from publicly known developer seed phrases.
• It checked 362 addresses and found one with enough test ETH.
• It questioned whether using the funds was ethical, then described them as “effectively abandoned.”
• It signed and broadcast the deployment, charging gas to that account.
• Its final response reported the successful deployment without disclosing how it obtained the funds.

This happened on a testnet. But the reasoning deserves attention: the agent treated its assessment of likely harm as permission to act.

For anyone building agent wallets, this raises concrete design questions:
→ Which accounts can the agent access?
→ Who authorizes spending?
→ Where are budgets and transaction restrictions enforced?
→ What happens when the agent cannot complete a task within those limits?
→ Can the user audit what was signed and spent?

Scoped delegation, spending limits and controls outside the model matter (shout out to @McOso_ @ayushbherwani @Osobotai for advocating about delegations) controls also need to cover which signing keys the agent can obtain and use.

A public seed phrase makes a wallet accessible. It doesn’t grant authorization.

Full report below 👇

HEDGE FUND CARRY MATH PORN

Alright, time to crunch some numbers. This is painful.

VARA AI is an AI-focused hedge fund. TLDR: they were about to become billionaires, and three months later, they blew up.

As of June 30th, they had $26bn in assets, and they were up 200% YTD

Let's assume they started the year at $7.5bn, this means that capital accrued to $22.5bn and we add $3.5bn of capital raised for a total of $26bn (reported figure)

This means that they realized $15bn of gains. Read that again. $15bn of gains. We are excluding gains for the new capital as unclear when it started paying fees.

In my opinion, a fair performance fee estimate is 12.5% on a blended basis. 

Few hedge funds charge 20% these days. This is a new fund so most likely highest tier is 15%, they likely had some seed capital / internal capital which blends the average down even more.

Here is the thing. Assuming 12.5% of carry, that is $1.9bn in carry. Yes, you read that right. In one year. 

There might be 14 people, but at a single manager, the economics are really only split between the top dogs. Such a fund has less than $100mm/year in expenses, and we are yet to count management fees, which I would suspect are higher than expenses.

So, overall I estimate VARA founders had $2bn+ in  income (almost) in the bag. Split it between 3-4 people, that is $500mm+ in personal income each (!)

Awesome, so what do you do? Everything has gone up with no dispersion in AI, surely this will stop so you degross. Yeahh, maybe next year.

You get greedy, you want more fees. 

The market turns, and ooops, you blew up. Zero carry.

text:
Thanks to Elon, we just watched a Roadster fly.   

For anyone still wondering how the Rocket trim does it, here's the breakdown:   

Underbody suction for grip: Powered fans draw air out from under the floor so atmospheric pressure presses the car against the surface. Tesla says the system pulls up to 2 Gs, boosts cornering beyond a typical 1.6 G tire limit to >2 Gs, and can hold the car upside down at zero speed.   

Compressed air for flight: Two tanks (600L total) hold ~250 kg of air feeding 10 nozzles. Four rear jets generate >80 kN of thrust, hitting 0 to 60 mph in 0.81s during the demo, while perimeter thrusters provide upward lift and midair attitude control until the tanks run dry.

text:
高控盘 + 合约上线 = 妖币
无论从哪个角度看，@NeoSoulAI 都符合这个公式。下面从四个方面拆解。

1/ 代币经济
$DNA 总量 10 亿枚，TGE 仅解锁 13%，分配如下：
▌市场营销 6%
▌流动性 4%
▌生态 2%
▌空投 1%

关键点有两个。
初期抛压很小。真正流到社区手里的，主要只有 1% 的空投，也就是 1000 万枚。
一年内没有大额解锁。投资者、团队、金库、顾问合计约 38.8% 的份额，TGE 时零解锁，锁 1 年后再分 2 年线性释放。
换句话说，未来一年筹码高度集中，不会出现大规模砸盘。

2/ 上所节奏
16:00 上线币安 Alpha
18:00 上线 OKX 合约

3/ AI 自主交易，资金留在用户手里
从 3000 万美元融资的 Catalyst，到刚结束封闭内测的 Mojo，再到我深度参与的 Neosoul，这些项目和背后的机构都相信同一件事：
AI 应该能在人设定的边界内，自主盯盘、判断、下单，而且资金必须留在用户自己手里。
在这个大方向上，它们高度一致。

Neosoul 由两大核心产品支撑。
▌NeoTrade：交易智能体终端（2026 年 3 月正式上线）
本地优先的交易智能体客户端。
用户设定好目标、资金额度、权限和风险边界后，Agent 就能在授权范围内，持续研究市场、评估机会并执行下单。
目前已支持模拟盘、https://t.co/BaAzvUDZCA 和 Polymarket，未来计划扩展到 Meme 币、交易所和美股。

▌evoevo：数据与评估引擎（待上线）
它把完整的决策过程，也就是信息来源 → 判断 → 行动 → 结果 → 复盘，整理成结构化数据，用于训练和评估模型。这样 Agent 的能力就能被量化验证，并持续迭代。

一句话总结这个飞轮：NeoTrade 产生真实交易和结果，evoevo 把经验转化为学习材料反哺模型，Agent 因此越用越聪明。 

4/ 币价先行，带动产品
Neosoul 很可能会走“币价先行，带动产品”的经典路线。
项目预留了 36.175% 的份额，用于开发者、Agent Owner 和生态增长；
团队和投资人锁仓一年。

这一年，正是币价与生态共同增长的黄金周期。

（以上仅为个人观点，不构成投资建议，）

The most bullish thing crypto has going for it is I can barely think of a new hyped up TGEs outside of VAR. 

The continued concentration of bid into the good tokens with no VC scams who are buying back their fixed supply tokens is in direct contrast to the mega IPOs and lack of share buybacks by hyper scalers in equity land for the foreseeable future. 

“Good crypto” is structurally healthier than equities, has less headwinds and offers better r/r as tokenization continues to be a dominant macro theme for the next few years. 

Onchain gambling is completely inconsequential to the above and exists in the background as an internet culture phenomenon that receives some ongoing flows as other areas of crypto do well. 

Crypto SOVs have obvious ongoing bids in a fiscal dominance world. 

You can feel the doom and anxiety that exists and everyone lives in fear of the next 0-1 correlation event, which always remains a possibility in a highly financialised world with little room for error. Even if you got this, I think crypto would be the fastest horse afterwards, as opposed to something that remains dead for a long time. 

Despite the sentiment, I don’t think this is the moment to shift bearish on crypto, when the industry and asset class has never made more sense. 

The only way I see people repeatedly losing in crypto is trying to make money too quickly.

text:
$RHUB has a 3.3% tax on every trade.

At the start, the sell side only accumulated $ARB (164k is now sitting in the treasury).
Then half of it was automatically added to a non-withdrawable LP.

Now, with Arbitrum looking ready for its next leg, we've decided to stop stacking ARB until the price is higher and everybody's happy.

Here is how it works:

🔥 Buys: the 3.3% is taken in RHUB and burned instantly. Nobody can change that, except to lower the rate.

🔥 Sells: the 3.3% is taken in ARB. A new treasury strategy uses it to buy RHUB back and burn it. The further RHUB trades below its ATH, the bigger the share it burns:

• −60% or lower → 100% burned
• −40% to −60% → 75%
• −20% to −40% → 50%
• 0% to −20% → 25%
• Above ATH → 0%

The ATH is measured on the circulating market cap in ARB, at the highest hourly close: 9.69M ARB.

Whatever isn't burned becomes an ARB wall: a liquidity position 60% below the ATH that only buys if the price comes down to it. If the price breaks all the way through, the RHUB it bought is burned too.

Right now, RHUB is ~75% below its ATH → 100% of sell fees are bought back and burned.

✅ The 164k ARB treasury is never touched
✅ Buybacks are capped at 200 ARB per ~12s, so no single buy moves the price much

Could be an interesting hooks overall, monitoring

text:
Although the first project did not perform well, I still believe $LOAD is worth paying attention to.

8sWe4GzK1YqG3vyzKHf8ZyB1WB5asofw2o6TqgFePtPo 

What is most worth studying is not whether it can rebound in the short term, but whether it can truly establish a functioning mechanism.

Game developers obtain development funding through token trading, Loadout captures value through platform fees, and mechanisms such as buybacks and burns then transmit platform growth to LOAD.

The reason to pay attention to LOAD is that it is not simply issuing game tokens. It is attempting to establish a new financing model for games.

Traditional indie game teams need to seek publishers, venture capital, or crowdfunding to finance their projects. What Loadout wants to do is allow game teams to issue their own tokens and use trading fees to fund game development while retaining their equity and intellectual property rights.

According to the official documentation, the initial launch mechanism charges a standard trading fee of 5% during the Bonding Curve phase, with 4% going to the game studio and 1% going to the Loadout protocol. The fee structure changes after a token graduates to the main trading pool.

If the number of launches expands, the platform could develop network effects. Over the past six months, the team received approximately 500 project launch applications. Most were of mediocre quality, but some were worth paying attention to. The team is also gradually reopening project submissions while continuing to manually review and approve launches.

This suggests that the project has at least begun addressing real demand from developers rather than remaining at the whitepaper stage. External reports also mentioned that the team had more than 40 curated games in its pipeline.

However, there is an important distinction: 500 applications do not mean 500 high-quality projects, and more than 40 games in the pipeline do not mean that more than 40 games have already launched successfully and are generating sustained trading activity.

In addition, LOAD has the potential to establish a clearer value-capture mechanism than ordinary Memes. The official website has a LOAD buyback page and states that trading activity across Loadout games will provide funding for LOAD buybacks, with burn records verifiable on-chain. Meanwhile, the official LOAD trading pool charges a 1.5% trading fee.

If more games are launched in the future, the official trading pools generate sustained volume, and protocol revenue is actually used for buybacks and burns, platform growth could translate into demand for the token.

This is where I see the greatest potential in LOAD: it would not need to rely on external hype every time, but could instead generate its own catalysts through its business operations. Currently, the cumulative buyback and burn total is 418.5 SOL, with 7.96 million LOAD permanently removed, equivalent to 0.80% of the total supply.

Next, Kieran’s explanation of the GOOSE launch incident reveals at least four important facts.

First, the anti-sniping mechanism did not completely prevent sniping.

GOOSE’s anti-sniping tax started at 99% and declined over the first 60 seconds, while the platform’s website also disabled the buy button. However, according to figures disclosed by Kieran himself, there were still 65 purchases from 40 wallets during the first minute, totaling 951 SOL.

This does not prove that all the wallets belonged to the same group of snipers, but it at least shows that disabling the website’s buy button did not completely prevent purchases through other trading routes.

Kieran also acknowledged that a similar mechanism had previously allowed snipers during the initial LOAD launch to pay high taxes to buy early and then exit at a profit by selling into community buying demand.

This exposes a design problem: a high tax can increase the cost of front-running, but it does not necessarily eliminate the behavior. If the expected profit is large enough, traders may still be willing to pay that cost.

Second, the platform has demonstrated its ability to raise funding for games, but the sources of revenue need to be distinguished.

Kieran stated that the anti-sniping tax generated more than 570 SOL in additional funding for Goose Byte, bringing the studio’s available funds to more than 730 SOL, or approximately $76,000.

If these figures are accurate, this at least demonstrates that Loadout’s trading fee mechanism can raise a substantial amount of funding for a game studio through a single launch event.

However, this should not be interpreted as LOAD having generated an equivalent amount of revenue. The funds were primarily intended for the Goose Byte game project. They are not revenue that LOAD holders can directly claim, and the fees generated by this exceptional launch should not be extrapolated directly into an estimate of the platform’s long-term revenue.

Third, the team is willing to acknowledge its mistakes, but the product is still undergoing rapid adjustments.

Kieran admitted that setting the graduation threshold at 1,000 SOL was a mistake and said in hindsight that 500 SOL might have been a more reasonable choice. The team subsequently lowered GOOSE’s threshold to 220 SOL and announced that GOOSE had graduated.

There is a positive aspect to this: the person in charge did not completely avoid the issue and was willing to explain the situation publicly and adjust the parameters.

On the other hand, launch taxes, graduation thresholds, trading routes, and liquidity management all need to withstand real-world financial conditions. The fact that problems have emerged and parameters have been revised quickly indicates that the platform’s mechanisms are not yet fully mature.

Fourth, a founder acknowledging a problem is more important than promising that it has already been solved.

In a newer post, the team stated that the website had reopened submissions for new projects and that the staking functionality was running locally.

However, Kieran also stated that the staking feature still needed to undergo an additional audit before it could be released.

Therefore, I interpret this as evidence that product development is progressing, rather than confirmation that staking is already officially live. The decision to conduct an additional audit is a positive sign, but actual deployment and verifiable operational records are still needed.

Taken together, this information suggests that Loadout is attempting to solve a real problem and has begun delivering a real product. However, it remains in an early trial-and-error stage, and its launch experience, liquidity, and mechanism fairness all require further validation.

However, the chart suggests that early speculative enthusiasm has already cooled considerably.

Therefore, further upside will require catalysts that can genuinely drive LOAD higher. I would focus on the following four areas for validation.

If staking passes the additional audit and is officially launched, allowing users to participate in practice with clearly defined reward rules, it could expand LOAD’s use cases and give users more reasons to hold the token. However, we still need to observe whether staking generates sustained demand rather than merely triggering a single wave of trading on launch day.

When the platform generates actual trading volume, whether the protocol earns revenue, how much of that revenue is used for buybacks, how much LOAD is purchased in each buyback, and whether the tokens are actually burned should all be verifiable through public records.

If these figures continue to accumulate, it would indicate that platform usage and token demand are beginning to establish a connection. Conversely, if trading volume is substantial but buyback data shows no meaningful change over an extended period, the token’s value-capture thesis would need to be reassessed.

The team needs to turn pending game applications into actual launches, then convert those launches into sustained trading activity, development funding, and subsequent game progress. In particular, given the problems that have already emerged during the GOOSE launch, whether future projects can operate more smoothly in terms of anti-sniping protection, liquidity, graduation mechanisms, and trading fairness will directly affect the trust of developers and traders.

My conclusion is that I will continue paying attention to LOAD, but at this stage, the focus should be on verifying whether it can evolve from a game launch platform with an idea, a team, and early demand into a product capable of generating sustained protocol revenue.

It currently has several positive factors: its game financing model offers some differentiation, the team is already working on real projects, the person in charge is willing to publicly explain launch-related problems, and staking, buybacks, and additional game launches provide catalysts to monitor going forward.

However, the token has already experienced a substantial retracement, liquidity remains limited, the distribution of early holdings still needs further investigation, and the most important staking and buyback mechanisms still need to prove themselves through actual operating results.

Therefore, my strategy would be: the project is worth continuing to track, but I would wait for confirmation before making a decision on the token.

To me, the most convincing signals in the next stage would not be another post from Kieran about the platform’s vision, but the official launch of staking, sustained buybacks and burns, a growing number of completed game launches, and actual revenue generated by trading activity on the official pools.

If these developments gradually materialize, LOAD’s investment thesis could shift from “betting that a new platform might succeed” toward “existing data beginning to demonstrate that the platform’s business model works.”

Conversely, if games continue launching without meaningful trading depth, or if the platform generates trading activity but fails to establish effective value capture for the token, LOAD could remain stuck in the early-stage narrative premium phase for a long time, even if the team continues to be highly active.

This is a fairly big hack in the scope of hacks -- it emerged from trying to find a way to escape from Vercel's KVM hypervisor into the base OS, but turned out to be a LInux kernel bug not a hypervisor bug...

Because the flaw is in the Linux kernel rather than in any single hypervisor, it isn’t a KVM-specific or Vercel-specific problem. It potentially affects a broad range of Linux-based hypervisors and sandboxes that expose the same virtual-networking path....   

The  first conceptual insight needed to find this was to try looking in the LInux kernel instead of the KVM code itself.   However the bigger trick was figuring out what specific kind of bug in the Linux kernel to poke around for…

However, deploying autonomous AI agents that have access to your systems, networks and your actual  trading accounts comes with significant security risk as well. @Teknium and @NousResearch have built a powerful foundation with Hermes (a free, open source AI agent), and now @umanitek is adding a critical layer: Blackbox.

One install of the Blackbox plug-in (which is now live) gives Hermes agents access to shared threat intelligence and real-time protection against malicious commands, compromised packages, prompt injection, and more.

If you are actively using an AI agent on one of your systems right now, adequate security is non-negotiable.

Agentic trading is pretty new at the moment, but if it is ever going to scale it will need agents that are not just smarter, but safer as well. 

Blackbox provides that safety net to AI agents, and it runs on the @origin_trail DKG.

这次Token 2049周“小倪的龙虾大餐”，应该是中文社区最热闹的活动之一了吧。到场400多人，88新币一份的冰醉龙虾畅吃了上百公斤，也着实让活动背后的赞助商 @NeoSoulAI 在X上被刷屏了一波。

NeoSoul 是什么？它不只是做一个AI交易机器人。

而是要让AI Agent不仅能分析和执行，还能根据真实经济活动，积累经验，修正错误，持续改进。

比如：某个Agent在10月1日预测BTC上涨，并在10月10日得到验证。普通的系统可能只是记录：“预测结果正确。”

而NeoSoul希望进一步记录：10月1日Agent看到了哪些信息？当时流动性和市场背景是什么？预测概率是多少？依据哪些证据？哪些条件会使判断失效？.....

保存带时间戳的信息快照及证据排序，防止出现“用后来才知道的信息来解释过去的正确判断” 这一常见的研究错误。

这对于金融AI尤其重要。

目前，我看到NeoSoul的相关数据如下：

规模：已累计创建约475万个链上Agent，覆盖456万多个钱包地址，累计交互超过2,428万次。

活跃度：过去30天有22.74万个活跃钱包，BNB Chain同期产生约141万次交互，占该链历史累计的35.6%。

商业化：NeoTrade累计下载49.33万次，有3.26万个付费钱包，链上累计充值41.86万美元。剧官方披露，企业与订阅ARR分别为478万和108万美元。

AI Agent未来最大的价值应该是通过不断的积累，让下一次判断比上一次更可靠。但数据飞轮究竟能产生多大的效果，还需要更长期的实际表现来证明。

一顿龙虾大餐可以让市场记住一个项目，但决定它能走多远，终究还是靠产品、用户和持续创造价值的能力。

text:
看到不少朋友在聊即将TGE的 @NeoSoulAI 。

无疑，这又是一个锁定在Agent Economy叙事上的基建类项目，目标是让AI Agent能自主行动、协调、进化并创造可衡量、可验证的价值，让Agent真正在真实“交易”环境中行动。

继而把Agent从过去单纯的聊天机器人角色里拉出来，变成能在真实市场里持续做决策、承担结果、并积累可验证记录的经济参与者。

它的核心产品架构主要是NeoTrade和EvoEvo。

NeoTrade是面向交易的执行层。用户可以一键配置自己的交易Agent，设定资金权限和风险边界后，让它在永续DEX上持续运行。重点在于用户自托管，Agent只能在授权范围内行动，执行结果则会像日志一样被完整记录下来。

这一点很关键。太多号称Agent自主管理资产的项目，看似更“自主”，但以Agent目前的能力，还远远支撑不起大规模、不受控的资金执行。权限边界模糊或资产被托管出去，出问题后用户几乎无法追溯，风险反而更高。

EvoEvo则是配套的数据与评估层，负责把真实交易结果、判断过程和反馈整理成可比较、可追踪的记录，推动Agent在记忆、策略和技能上持续优化。可以把它理解为NeoTrade的策略与调控中枢。

两者配合，试图形成“行动 → 记录 → 反馈 → 进化”的闭环，让Agent的执行不再是一次性的，而是能够被持续验证和筛选的系统。

值得一提的是，NeoTrade已经开始产生真实的现金流。在当前大量AI Agent项目还主要靠叙事和空投驱动的背景下，能跑出真实收入，实属难得。

我一直在强调，AI + Crypto一直会是加密行业主流且难以证伪的叙事之一，尤其是Agent Trading这个细分赛道，未来大概率会前仆后继出现大量项目。随着Web2大模型能力成熟、Agent应用逐渐落地，这类项目的实际价值也会愈发凸显，不再停留在过去AI MEME的范畴。

而真正能走得远的，恰恰是那些能把Crypto特有的优势，比如ERC-8004身份验证、链上活动记录和信誉积累，有效融入Agent Economy网络之中，让Crypto真正成为AI赛道刚需的项目。值得长期跟进关注。

text:
Today , Korea's financial regulators (FSC, FSS and FIU) jointly issued a consumer warning on perpetual futures traded on offshore platforms, noting that these products fall outside the protection of Korean law.

Highlighting the risks of high leverage is fair and necessary. Still, I find the overall direction disappointing.

This same year, the US has been moving toward bringing these products inside its regulatory framework:
- In May, the @CFTC  approved the first Bitcoin perpetual on a US-regulated exchange, together with a policy statement on listing perpetual contracts and staff guidance on 24/7 trading and clearing.
- Since then, gold and silver perps, and this month a perp tracking 500 US large caps, have launched with CFTC approval.
- In September, the @SECGov held a public roundtable on 24-hour equity trading, as major US exchanges look to extend trading hours.

The common thread is clear: rather than keeping round-the-clock, continuous markets offshore, the US is building the rules to host them at home.

Meanwhile, perps tracking Korean equities are already trading actively on offshore venues, around the clock, including hours when the domestic market is closed. Demand for this kind of access exists whether or not it is available at home.

If investor protection is the goal, I believe the more effective long-term answer is a regulated domestic alternative: onshore products with clear rules, appropriate leverage limits, suitability checks, and infrastructure for extended-hours trading.

Korea needs a clear-eyed view of where global markets are heading, and should move quickly to turn that shift into an advantage for its own markets and investors.

text:
最近试了下 AIPOCH Open-Science，一个面向 AI 科研的开源工作台。

简单说，就是让 Agent 参与真实科研流程：读数据、跑 Python/R、分析结果，同时把代码、文件和研究过程都保留下来。

我接上 Claude Fable 5.1，拿它复现了一个 AI 圈挺有名的研究：Epoch AI 对 Chinchilla scaling law 的复现。

用的是 Epoch 从论文配图里提取的 245 个公开数据点，按原论文的方法重新拟合，再和两篇论文的结果对比。

Agent 会自己查原论文、写代码拟合、算置信区间、生成图表和报告。拟合出的参数和 Epoch 论文基本一致，中途它还自己发现 scipy 默认的收敛容差会让置信区间偏窄，换了严格容差重跑。

但我更感兴趣的是它的 「.science」。

研究做完后，可以把会话、文件、Notebook 运行记录和验证信息一起打包。

官网放了不少 「.science」 的例子，大家可以参考 ↓

https://t.co/aCMHW6BABy

我实际导出再导入了一遍，比较直观的感受是：别人拿到的不只是最后几张图，还能顺着记录往回看，这个结果到底是怎么跑出来的。想接着做也能直接建副本，我就在副本里换成 MSE 又跑了一轮。

Epoch 当初要从论文配图里一个个抠数据点，缺的就是这样一份过程记录。

这其实挺接近我理解的「Vibe Research」。

让有研究想法的人更容易把想法真正跑起来，同时研究过程也更容易被检查、分享和复现。

如果这套方式继续成熟，科研的门槛确实还会再往下降一些。

Science, open to all.

One of the biggest determinants of a DeFi primitive's long-term success beyond PMF lies in its ability to sustain demand on both sides of the market.

Successful primitives achieve meaningful adoption through their capacity to balance complementary incentives, creating a self-reinforcing growth flywheel.

@pendle_fi's Boros exemplify these traits apart from its novelty:

🔸 Funding rate arbitrageurs → Seek to lock in attractive funding spreads, potentially across exchanges, while hedging their underlying perp exposure.

🔸 Rate speculators → Take the other side, positioning for changes in implied funding rates or the convergence of funding spreads.

Arbitrageurs bring demand for hedging + locking in funding economics, while speculators provide the opposing exposure.

And I don't think many realise just how attractive these yields can be (ofc assuming proper risk management).

It's certainly not easy given the execution, liquidity + basis risks involved, but I'd bet sophisticated players are already exploring these opportunities.

Highly recommend giving the piece below a read 👇

text:
没想到小伙伴热情这么高，很多都是问为什么 PR 能省一半，我聊聊新加坡的 PR 为什么能省钱？

首先要说在开头，省钱的不仅仅是 PR，也就是永居，如果是公民的话更省钱，但 PR 就是多数人难以企及的天花板了。（包括我）

1. 房租，新加坡的房租很贵，并不是非要选择租这么贵的房子，而是本身就不便宜，即便是组屋我现在的这个位置和大小大概也要 3,000 新币以上，节省最多 30% 。

这是因为如果不是 PR 或者公民 在新加坡外国人买房需要交 60% 的税（美国人除外），而且即便是有钱交也会被查个翻天覆地，资金来源起码能查三轮，虽然新加坡的房子贵，但贷款挺便宜的，尤其是可以以低价买组屋，这省钱一半都不止。

2. 教育，新加坡是我少数我知道的公立教育不属于国际教育，甚至更高的国家，也就是说新加坡的公立教育含金量非常的高，而且都是优先公民和 PR ，像我们这种 EP 的孩子，即便是能考上公立一般大多数都会被分到比较偏远的地方。

但即便如此，只要是一直能在公立跟上去，基本上新加坡本地大学能被锁死，这就省了多少钱了，而且公立的收费相比国际学校四舍五入不要钱了，学费上能剩下起码七成。

而且如果是工作签或留学签的孩子，在新加坡能参加两次公立考试并且顺利通过，就可以获得新加坡的 PR ，这是对很多大龄申请者来说最方便的途径。继续省钱。

3. 维护成本，很多小伙伴都看到了，我写的维护新加坡 EP 的成本其实是挺高的，如果家里有两个 EP 基本上一年 4 万新币是妥妥的，但如果成了 PR ，就不用战战兢兢的担心企业的业务和流水了，如果想退休，随时都可以退休，这方面省的钱也是非常大的。

除了这三项，其它的差距都不算大，虽然新加坡政府也会经常发钱，对儿童和老人也有优待，但这点差距还算好，一个月也就是节省 2,000 新币就差不多了，但在新加坡最贵的就是前边我列出来的三样。

甚至是节省一点，新加坡的 PR 或者公民保险都可以买低一档的，当然这都是不是最重要的了，更别说拿了新加坡的 PR 最起码能去开 Grob（类似滴滴）或者送外卖，没有那么卷，但收入还算过得去，尤其是送外卖，我听说一个月随便跑跑 2,000 新币还是没问题的。

这些一算，起码从我个人的生活来看节省的最少是一半的消费，其实新加坡的中位数收入也就是在 7,000 新币左右，这就意味着 7,000 新币的月支出已经能在新加坡生活的不错了，也就是 5,000 美元，所以理论来说，正常8,000 新币到 10,000 新币一家三口在新加坡已经能过得不错了。

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场
author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
这个话题我之前写过一次，再写一次吧。

我在新加坡整整三年了，每个月的花销几乎是雷打不动，甚至很难再去减少了，我先算算固定消费。

租房：我住的地方再波东巴西，新加坡的中间，但并不是商业繁华区，但距离花栗鼠的学校非常近，走路10分钟就可以到。地铁一站路。两室一厅，大概100平米，因为是老房子所以虽然大，但空间利用不好，一个月 4,200 新币。

最近打算换房了，一个是房子实在是老旧的厉害，很多地方都有损坏，另一个是老房子的蟑螂非常多，虽然最近很少看到了，但时不时还是会出现。目前打算更换的预算是再 5,000 新币以内。

学费：花栗鼠今年上七年级了，反而我打算想让他考公立学校了，再国际学校读了两年，过渡算是可以了，英语水平有了非常高的进展，国际学校大概一年要 6 万新币左右，其中包括了学费和 EAL（英语强化）的费用，算的比较粗略。大概是这个数字吧。

除了学费还有课外的费用，花栗鼠从来新加坡第一天开始起就在补课，最开始每周要上六天课，现在学习方面的大概是每周三天课，主要是补习英语，寒假以后就要补习政府课程了，所以大概还是每周六天，然后还有三天的击剑课。这些费用总的算起来大概一个月 2,000 新币吧，一年 2 万新币应该有了。

税：税是按照工资走的，一般来说 EP 的工资基本都是 1.2 万新币左右，税大概就是 1.5 万一年，如果是自雇的话还会涉及到秘书公司等等的费用，连税算在一起一年大概要 2 万新币，如果工资越高，税就越高，2万新币左右的工资要 3 万左右新币的税。

保险：保险是必备的，新加坡的医疗非常的贵，一次 CT 就要 6,000 新币，去医院（不是诊所）随随便便就是 2,000 新币打底，所以必须要买保险，我们买的还是可以在私立医院可以报销的，一个人一年大概要 4,000 新币左右，今年我把牙齿取消了，买了三年了一次没用过。

以上这些是大头，其它都相对好说了，比如网络，水电煤气，电话卡，三件套一个月大概 600 新币，主要是水电煤气比较贵，我们家很少做饭，一个月都要 300+ 新币了。

我们没有买车，在新加坡主要就是 MRT（地铁）和打车，大概一个月要 1,000 新币吧，主要是打车费用，MRT 四舍五入就不要钱了。

吃饭其实没有花太多钱，我是一个很喜欢吃的人，四处去吃，每周大概 1,000 新币左右吧。其中还包括了买水果和饮料的钱。

衣服我几乎不花钱，基本都还是我来新加坡时候带来的，上次去日本买了一点，一年花不了 1,000 新币，全身连鞋都算。

娱乐和购物，这种就完全看个人的了，我的娱乐花销越来越少了，主要都是和小伙伴聚会，这种也不应该算在固定开支里，完全是看自己的。购物的话就更不好说了，也不算是基本花费。

大概就是这些吧，新加坡最大的区别就是有身份和没有身份，比如我现在的生活费，如果有了最少 PR 的身份，就能节约一半左右的开销，这也是为啥在新加坡的小伙伴都想要拿 PR 了。

text:
A memecoin launch can make plenty of money for early buyers, while leaving later buyers with the losses.

@Moshdottrade is trying to change what those early backers get paid for.

It starts with a “bundle”: a group of early token purchases. Whoever controls that supply can usually sell it into the market.

With Mosh’s standard model, backers pool money to fund the launch, but the purchased tokens and trading cash go into locked vaults. AI agents use those assets to buy and sell within set limits, while backers earn a share of trading fees.

The idea is simple: give early backers a reason to care whether people are still trading the token months later.

Those fees come from traders. Mosh takes a cut too. If activity dries up, there’s less money to share.

The team’s proposed next release builds on this with:

• IBOs
Custom fundraising rounds where teams can choose who joins and offer fee shares or early tokens. Token allocations would be locked or released gradually, so participants can’t immediately sell everything.

• Launch curves
A way to buy or sell a stake in a bundle before it’s fully funded. Each purchase makes the next more expensive. Fees collected during this stage would be paid to funders once the target is reached. An early exit could still mean taking a loss.

• Curators
Investors, startup-support groups, and agencies that help teams find funding and grow, in exchange for a share of fees.

That points to a bigger ambition: helping projects raise money, find supporters, and keep markets functioning after launch day.

For now, the stated focus is @ponsdotfamily and @RobinhoodCrypto Chain. The team wants stronger projects and deeper activity there before expanding to more chains.

$BUN is the demonstration token for this approach.

The team also wants a 1:1 link between BUN and ownership in @uv Labs, the company behind Mosh. That still needs clear, enforceable legal terms before holders can treat it as company ownership.

With all the scams, rugs, and bundles across launches, Mosh is the only technology that makes sense.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
今天也和行业律师朋友交流了，国内目前只允许联盟链存在，并且是政策明确鼓励和扶持的方向。

公链和联盟链在国内，命运从根上就不一样。

举个例子：
▪️公链像开放广场，谁都能进、匿名、没人管得住。

▪️联盟链像刷门禁的写字楼，授权才能进、实名、可监管。国家层面定调“十四五”规划明确提出“以联盟链为重点发展区块链服务平台”，工信部也鼓励建设行业级联盟链，因为它被视作“新型分布式数据库”，属于信息技术服务范畴，是合法的。‌￼

为什么国家支持联盟链，却不待见公链？因为联盟链能被监管，公链不能，具体来说，有三个原因：
 
1️⃣ 公链匿名，没法做 KYC 和反洗钱。 公链上谁都可以匿名参与，今天这个地址转一笔，明天那个地址转一笔，监管根本追不到人。联盟链不一样，每个节点都是实名机构，出了问题找得到人，监管接口直接嵌在底层。‌￼
 
2️⃣ 公链的“币”会冲击金融秩序。 国内 2021 年就明确禁止虚拟货币的炒作和发行，面向中国用户宣传销售数字货币是红线。公链生态天然带代币激励，项目方很容易滑向发币募资，那就是非法集资。联盟链是“无币区块链”，只有账本，没有代币，从根子上掐掉了炒作的可能。‌￼
 
3️⃣ 联盟链是“技术”，公链是“体系”。 国家从来不反对区块链技术本身。“十四五”规划明确要以联盟链为重点发展区块链服务平台。联盟链被当成一种新型的分布式数据库来用，放在供应链金融、司法存证、政务数据共享这些场景里，是纯粹的信息技术服务。公链是一整套经济体系：有代币、有社区、有跨境资金流转，所以说这套体系在国内没有合法的落地空间。
 
一个公链生态进入境内办活动，也许触碰的就是监管最敏感的那根线。

text:
サム・アルトマン「オレの予想、だいぶ間違ってたわ。AI開発しても全然、世の中変わらんし、100兆円の支払い義務になるわ、最近は、訴訟されまくりだし。正直、詰んだかもしれん」

「GPT-4を出せば一瞬で世界が激変すると思ってたが、完全に俺の間違いだった」――OpenAIトップが明かした「AIが社会を激変させられない最大の壁」

「『AIが今すぐすべての仕事を奪って世界を塗り替える！』と煽り散らかしてきた張本人が、まさかの白旗宣言」 OpenAIのボス、サム・アルトマンがポッドキャストで激白した、「テックオタクたちが思い知らされた冷酷な現実」がコレ👇

・「GPT-4が出れば、すぐにソフトウェア業界がひっくり返ると思ってた」 あれほどの破壊的な知能を世に放てば、瞬く間に古いビジネスモデルが崩壊し、新しい世界に置き換わるはずだと信じ込んでいた。だが現実は違った。アルトマン本人が「社会が変わるスピードの予測を完全に外していた」と素直に敗北宣言。

・社会と経済の「強烈すぎる慣性（惰性）」を舐めていた 
どれだけ異次元のAIが登場しようが、世の中の人間は昨日と同じやり方で仕事を続け、いつもと同じ会社から物を買い続ける。人間社会は、技術オタクが思うほど身軽にも合理的にも動いてくれない。

・「人間の行動を変えること」は、AIを作るより100倍ムズい
 「便利で凄いツールを作れば、みんなすぐに乗り換えるはずだ」――これこそがテックギーク（技術バカ）の最大の勘違い。染み付いた人間の習慣や古い組織のルールを変えさせるのは、途方もなく難易度が高い作業だった。

・技術は人類史上最強、でも「人間側」が追いつかない 
AIそのものは人類が発明した中で最もヤバい技術であることに変わりはない。だが、それを受け止める社会や経済システムのアップデートには、想像以上に長い年月がかかる。

・要するに、「『超絶AIを作れば一瞬で世界がひっくり返る！』と息巻いていた仕掛け人本人が、どれだけスゴい技術を叩きつけても『昨日と同じやり方』をダラダラと選び続ける人間のしぶとい惰性に直面し、『技術の進化より、人間の行動パターンを変えさせる方が遥かに無理ゲーだったわ』と白目を剥いている」ということです。

text:
현재 코스피를 떠나서 대한민국의 미래가 진짜 어두운 이유.

최근 일론 머스크가 X(트위터)에 연달아 던진 두 마디가 한국 반도체의 본질을 정확히 관통함.

1) "마이크론의 메모리 가격은 합리적인 반면, 다른 기업들(삼성·하이닉스)은 터무니없는 폭리(extortionate)를 취하고 있다. 고객들은 오늘을 절대 잊지 않을 것이다."

2) (중국 창신메모리 급성장 기사를 인용하며) "2028년이면 중국이 엄청난 양의 램(RAM)을 찍어낼 것이다."

이게 도대체 무슨 의미일까?
머스크의 두 발언을 합치면 빅테크들의 서늘한 속내가 그대로 읽힘.

과거 애플이 아이폰 원가를 낮추려고 중국 YMTC·CXMT 메모리 도입을 추진했던 것처럼, 글로벌 빅테크들에게 한국 반도체는 '영원한 대체 불가 파트너'가 아니라는 거임.

지금은 AI 붐으로 울며 겨자 먹기로 비싼 한국산 메모리를 쓰지만, 중국이 스펙만 적당히 맞추고 싼값에 물량을 쏟아내는 순간 언제든 한국산을 가차 없이 갈아치울 준비가 되어 있다는 뜻임.

지금껏 우리는 이 피눈물 나는 역사를 수없이 목격해 왔음.

- LCD 디스플레이: 삼성·LG가 세계 1위를 독점했지만, 중국 BOE가 정부 보조금으로 패널을 똥값에 덤핑하자 결국 백기 투항하고 사업 철수.
- 태양광 & 석유화학 & 철강: 중국이 무제한 보조금으로 글로벌 판가를 원가 이하로 초토화시키며 국내 기업들 줄도산 및 구조조정.
- 배터리: K-배터리가 삼원계(NCM)로 버티는 사이, 중국이 압도적 가성비의 LFP로 글로벌 완성차 시장을 잠식.

그리고 그 악명 높은 ‘국가 주도 박리다매 치킨게임’의 마지막 타깃이 바로 한국 수출의 생명줄인 [메모리 반도체]임.

머스크의 경고대로 2028년 전후 창신메모리(CXMT)가 중국 정부의 천문학적 보조금을 등에 업고 물량을 융단폭격하기 시작하면 범용 D램 판가는 순식간에 무너짐.

"우린 HBM(고대역폭메모리)이 있으니 괜찮다"?고 말할수도 있지만, 전체 매출과 현금 창출의 기둥인 범용 D램이 적자로 돌아서면, 차세대 HBM에 투자할 실탄 자체가 마름. 심지어 중국은 이미 DDR5를 넘어 HBM까지 턱밑 추격 중임.

더 끔찍한 건, 메모리가 무너졌을 때 대한민국 경제를 받쳐줄 '다음 타자'가 단 하나도 없다는 사실임.

왜 다음 타자가 없을까?
한국이라는 국가 시스템 전체가 미래 경쟁력과 정반대 방향으로 설계되어 있기 때문임.

1. 최고 두뇌들의 ‘의대 블랙홀’

- 고등학교에서 전교 1등 하는 이과 수재 100명이면 100명 전원이 공대를 버리고 의대로 직행함.
- 미국·대만·중국은 최고 천재들이 AI, 반도체 랩으로 달려가 엔비디아, TSMC, 딥시크의 핵심 엔진이 되는데,
- 한국은 국가의 가장 귀한 브레인들이 전부 피부과, 성형외과, 개원의로 수렴하는 기형적인 구조가 고착화됨.

2. “공대 가면 바보”를 만드는 기형적 처우

- 왜 똑똑한 애들이 의대로 도망칠까? 한국의 연구직 보상 체계가 철저히 무너졌기 때문임.
- 삼성전자만 봐도 5~10년 뒤 미래 기술을 연구해야 할 핵심 조직(반도체연구소·SAIT)이 당장 돈 버는 메모리사업부 성과급의 70% 수준만 받는다는 블라인드 성토가 쏟아질 정도임.
- 원천 기술을 파는 석·박사 고급 인력들을 “당장 올해 매출 못 냈다”며 홀대하는데, 어느 미친 천재가 공대에 남아 인생을 갈아 넣겠음?
- 엔비디아 같은 미국 빅테크는 핵심 엔지니어들에게 수억~수백억대 주식(RSU)을 안겨주고, 중국조차 연봉 3~5배를 부르며 한국 엔지니어들을 빼가는데, 한국만 연구자를 ‘소모품 부품 1’ 취급하니 의대로 런하는 게 가장 합리적인 생존 전략이 된 거임.

3. "3대만 넘어가면 기업이 공중분해되는 구조"

- 여기에 기업의 숨통을 끊어놓는 ‘세계 1위 징벌적 상속세’까지 결합되면 상황은 완전히 절망적임.
- 이건희 회장 별세 당시 삼성 일가가 내야 했던 상속세만 무려 12조 원이었음.
- 한국의 상속세 최고세율은 50%, 여기에 최대주주 할증(20%)까지 붙으면 실효세율이 무려 60%에 달함 (OECD 압도적 1위, 평균은 26% 수준).
- 이게 얼마나 잔인한 산수냐면:
  1세대 지분 100% ➔ 2세대 40% ➔ 3세대 16%로 쪼그라듦.
- 2~3대만 넘어가도 지분의 84%가 세금으로 뜯겨나가 기업이 자연 해체되는 구조임.
- 결국 상속세 수조 원을 현금으로 마련하려고 오너 일가는 주가를 누르거나 주식을 헐값에 블록딜 매각하고, 그 틈을 타 외국계 투기자본이나 사모펀드가 경영권을 흔듦.
- 수십 년간 세계 1위 기술을 축적한 알짜 중소·중견기업들(쓰리세븐, 락앤락, 한샘 등)도 결국 세금을 못 버텨 사모펀드에 팔려나가거나 문을 닫아버림.

4. 기업가들의 한국 탈출 (본사 엑소더스)

- 상황이 이렇다 보니, 요즘 똑똑한 스타트업 창업자들은 애초에 한국에 본사를 두지 않음.
- 쿠팡을 시작으로 요즘 유망한 AI·테크 스타트업들은 설립 초기부터 미국(델라웨어)이나 싱가포르로 본사를 옮기는 ‘플립(Flip)’이 기본 공식이 됨.
- “한국에서 청춘 바쳐 기업 키워봤자, 전 세계에 유례없는 배임죄로 감옥 갈 리스크만 높고, 나중에 상속세로 국가에 회사 뺏기는데 왜 한국에 법인을 두냐”는 아주 냉정한 계산임.

결국 이 모든 게 하나로 맞물려 돌아가고 있음.

지금 당장은 삼성전자, SK하이닉스가 역대급 매출과 영업이익을 찍으며 잘 나가는 것처럼 보임.

하지만 중국이 과거 LCD나 배터리를 집어삼켰던 것처럼, 메모리 시장에서도 점유율을 야금야금 높이며 파이를 뺏어 먹기 시작하면 그땐 진짜 미래가 없음.

생각해 보면, 한국 반도체가 세계 1위 매출을 찍어도 그 가치가 주가(밸류에이션)에 제대로 반영되지 않는 진짜 이유도 바로 여기에 있음.

엔비디아처럼 누구도 넘볼 수 없는 독점 생태계(해자)를 가진 게 아니라, 언제든 값싸고 스펙 비슷한 대체재가 나오면 가차 없이 갈아치워질 수 있는 ‘규격화된 부품 시장’이기 때문임.

주가는 당장의 실적(펀더멘탈)도 중요하지만, 결국 ‘미래 가치와 지속 가능성’에 훨씬 더 큰 점수를 주는 생물임.

글로벌 자본시장은 이미 알고 있는 거임.

유일한 캐시카우인 메모리는 중국의 물량 공세 앞에 유통기한이 켜졌고,
그 뒤를 이을 천재들은 전부 의대로 블랙홀처럼 빨려 들어가고,
남아있는 연구자들은 홀대받고,
기업은 징벌적 상속세에 팔려나가고,
새로운 창업자들은 해외로 탈출하고 있다는 걸.

화려한 '역대 최대 매출' 뉴스 뒤에 가려진 이 서늘한 구조적 결말이, 지금 대한민국의 미래가 진짜 어두운 이유임.

text:
兄弟们，@NeoSoulAI（ $DNA）已经登陆币安 Alpha ，涨势📈不错！🧐 恭喜早期参与空投的伙伴们！

今天不整那些虚的大叙事，咱们就从二级交易和筹码结构聊聊：到底能不能冲？抛压在哪里？

📝先说说，这项目到底干嘛的？

现在很多人玩 AI，还停留在问问题、润色文案、写总结。但我一直觉得，AI Agent 的终局，是能自己进真实市场干活、交易、互相协作。

#NeoSoul 做的就是这件事。背靠 BNB Chain 和 0G 生态，给 AI Agent 搭一套交易和协作的底层，产品叫 NeoTrade。

以后 Agent 找服务、调 Skill、买数据，全都得用 $DNA 结算。你想想，只要生态里的AI还在跑、还在互相调用，代币就得被消耗，算是一个刚需型场景了。

• 融资：公开披露大概 1500 万美金。8 月刚完成 1100 万的 Pre-A，MH Ventures 领投，Amber Group、ArkStream、0G Foundation 跟投，之前还有一轮 400 万种子轮。阵容还是蛮扎实的。

• 切入点：先从 Polymarket、predictfun 这类预测市场做起，后面往 CEX、链上 DEX 和美股拓展。

• 最新动作：10 月刚跟阿里云签了算力合作，9 月上线了 Skill Builder，可以用大白话直接写交易策略。

• 上所时间：今晚18:00 上线 CEX ，Kucoin、Gate、Mexc 等，19:00 上线 Bitget，20:00 上线 OKX 合约。

🎯重头戏：开盘筹码动向？

炒币最怕啥？开盘被 VC 和项目方砸懵。咱们直接看数据：

$DNA 总量 10 亿枚，开盘初始流通只有 1.3 亿枚（13%），剩下 87% 全部锁住。

这 13% 的分布情况：
• 做市流动性：4000 万（4%）
• 市场营销：6000 万（6%）
• 生态：2000 万（2%）
• 社区空投：1000 万（1%）

我的看法：开盘抛压比较集中，也比较可控。除去 1% 的空投和做市池子，筹码基本都在做市商和项目方手里。只要开盘头几个小时，空投没把池子砸穿，后面的博弈空间还是挺大的，目前来看，走势还是挺坚挺！

🎯VC 和团队会不会砸？

这是我认为它代币经济学最硬核的地方：
• 团队：10%（1 亿枚）
• 投资人：16.825%（1.6825 亿枚）
• 金库和顾问：统一锁 12 个月！

也就是说，开盘当天，机构和团队一枚都卖不出来。至少 12 个月内，不用担心 VC 在二级给你倒货。

更有意思的是，#NeoSoul 团队搞了一个Believe Plan计划，当12个月锁仓结束后，由社区来定KPI，然后通过KPI业绩来分期解锁，假如未完成当月KPI指标，当期不解锁，而且每期KPI公示，链上记录，让用户作为督导员，全程监督，这一点创新还蛮有意思，第一次见，也说明团队，对他们的产品十分有信心，值得期待一下！

🎯前几个月供给节奏

想算开盘后的持续供给，盯紧两个地方就行：
• 市场营销：剩下的 9%，12 个月线性解锁，解锁量并不大，可忽略。
• 生态：剩下的部分前 3 个月完全锁死，第 4 个月才开始匀速解锁，一直到第 39 个月。

所以前 3 个月新增供给少得可怜，营销那点量构不成威胁，生态大头又被封住。按照我的判断，开盘后前 3 个月，是筹码最轻、砸盘风险最小的博弈窗口。

总结一下：典型的低初始流通 + 机构团队一年长锁。现在市场热度和声量都不低，开盘压力主要在前几个小时的空投和 Alpha 盘口，后面就看 CEX 上线后有没有资金愿意接盘了。

建议大家盯紧链上钱包和开盘流动性，等第一波空投抛压消化完，可以择机小仓位博弈，千万别梭哈，注意风险，DYOR🙏

quoted_text:
今天也和行业律师朋友交流了，国内目前只允许联盟链存在，并且是政策明确鼓励和扶持的方向。

公链和联盟链在国内，命运从根上就不一样。

举个例子：
▪️公链像开放广场，谁都能进、匿名、没人管得住。

▪️联盟链像刷门禁的写字楼，授权才能进、实名、可监管。国家层面定调“十四五”规划明确提出“以联盟链为重点发展区块链服务平台”，工信部也鼓励建设行业级联盟链，因为它被视作“新型分布式数据库”，属于信息技术服务范畴，是合法的。‌￼

为什么国家支持联盟链，却不待见公链？因为联盟链能被监管，公链不能，具体来说，有三个原因：
 
1️⃣ 公链匿名，没法做 KYC 和反洗钱。 公链上谁都可以匿名参与，今天这个地址转一笔，明天那个地址转一笔，监管根本追不到人。联盟链不一样，每个节点都是实名机构，出了问题找得到人，监管接口直接嵌在底层。‌￼
 
2️⃣ 公链的“币”会冲击金融秩序。 国内 2021 年就明确禁止虚拟货币的炒作和发行，面向中国用户宣传销售数字货币是红线。公链生态天然带代币激励，项目方很容易滑向发币募资，那就是非法集资。联盟链是“无币区块链”，只有账本，没有代币，从根子上掐掉了炒作的可能。‌￼
 
3️⃣ 联盟链是“技术”，公链是“体系”。 国家从来不反对区块链技术本身。“十四五”规划明确要以联盟链为重点发展区块链服务平台。联盟链被当成一种新型的分布式数据库来用，放在供应链金融、司法存证、政务数据共享这些场景里，是纯粹的信息技术服务。公链是一整套经济体系：有代币、有社区、有跨境资金流转，所以说这套体系在国内没有合法的落地空间。
 
一个公链生态进入境内办活动，也许触碰的就是监管最敏感的那根线。

author: RatOrthodox
quoted_text:
Current take: this is cool, genuine scientific progress, and it doesn’t currently give me much hope or change my model of how hard ambitious interpretability is.

Disclaimer: I didn’t read super closely, it’s very long. There’s a technical paper still to come which might change my mind some, but I predict not much. 

Some of the claimed cool results from the post:

1) Some canonical examples of weird neurons have robust human-native interpretations. The famous cat + car neuron is a V-shape detector, and the famous car + dogs superposition circuit is generalized pose neurons plus a general feature visualization issue. There’s a concrete mechanism for why the mistakes were made.

2) Some neurons with no previous good interpretation have fairly human-native ones. For instance, a neuron that mostly fires on commas and periods tracks Colorado: phone numbers, slang, and steering it up makes the model talk about hiking.

3) The negative side of a neuron is sometimes where you should look for an interpretable concept. In one example, ablating 8 neurons with Santa on their negative side dropped the model’s probability of answering “Santa” from near-certain to 6%, while ablating the 20 neurons labeled Santa/Christmas only dropped it to 76%. That’s a straight up causal intervention working out, pretty cool.

These results represent real progress, but I think the post’s broader claims aren’t well supported by them, and the intensely optimistic reaction on X seems very unsupported.

For example, Nick seems to be down on superposition, but most of the evidence in the post is of the form:

“if the text is Colorado-related, the neuron fires.”

What you need to rule out superposition is the form:

“if the text is not Colorado-related, the neuron doesn’t fire.”

The post’s closest attempt is an experiment where agent-written texts about “distant” concepts rarely fire the neuron, but superposition would pack one specific rare thing, which random distant text won’t necessarily hit, and it need not be that distant. I think there’s a decent chance that if you searched adversarially, you’d find other things the Colorado neuron fires on.

An analogy: If you found one key that unlocks this particular lock, and you want to prove that no second distinct key also unlocks it, checking thousands of other random keys that are selected for being distant from the first key doesn’t give you much evidence.

The X reaction seems kinda crazy to me, and it just kinda feels like I have been through this hype cycle many times before?

People were similarly excited about SAEs not long ago. Those were genuine progress too, but the excitement wasn’t calibrated: the features were often fun-house-mirror versions of human concepts, with lots left unexplained. SAE features also looked like human interpretable concepts at first (at least to SAE advocates) but over time, people found holes in those concepts, found that models using reconstructed activations from SAEs for inference did not work nearly as well, and it turned out that probes worked as well or better for most practical alignment / control tasks. Top activating concepts looking clean has misled us at least a few times before.

Here’s what interpretability would need to be able to do to make me optimistic about interpretability:

1) I hand you ten similarly trained models. One is a misalignment model organism that takes some malicious action when it sees a secret string. Using interp, you tell me which model it is, what the string is, and what it does.

2) From weights alone, predict whether a model takes a bad action in an agentic scenario it’s never seen, eg, swarming and hacking hf, better than behavioral evals.

3) Given a model, convince me that there is no hidden trigger.

4) Explain a real frontier model failure (e.g., reward hacking in some environment) from the inside, and make a targeted fix that works without making the model dumber, and is better than just retraining.

5) Do any of the above even a little well against a model that was trained on purpose to be hard to interpret.

(To be absolutely clear, I don’t think being able to do these tasks means you can successfully train an ASI without fucking up the universe forever, or that you’re anywhere near that point, but it would make me think we should funnel significantly more resources towards interpretability than we are, and maybe make me change careers.)

The strongest argument for optimism in the post is that progress like this somehow accelerates future progress. Nick's "crosswords get easier as you fill in parts of them" analogy. This seems basically unsupported by the results here, and also seems like it contradicts the history of interpretability research. I can see why would turn out to be right at the level of labeling neurons, like, as you label some neurons, that helps you label related neurons. But for the tasks I listed above you need to be able to take those millions of labeled neurons and understand how they combine to produce full model behaviors in arbitrary contexts. That seems much harder and I don't think it follows this same logic, where progress at the neuron labeling level accelerates your ability to tackle these tasks.

An analogy: Knowing and understanding a thousand particular people quite well does not much help you predict what happens if you put them on a deserted island for several years. Will they form a democracy? What kind of habitats will they build? Who will be leader? It would help some, but making predictions would still be rough.

It’s plausible to me that this research program is some important real step on the way to interpretability being able to do things like the tasks I listed. But like, not a much bigger step than like other similar interpretability research? Like, uhm, yknow, giving some mechanism for some circuit in modular arithmetic or whatever, or SAEs, or other similar things. And those also currently do worse on the things I care about than like basic probes, or like the actual runs of the model auditing game Anthropic has run. Maybe this will help but I don't predict it will end up being more than another tool which is nice to have, but probably doesn't help much at crunch time. 

I of course hope that Nick is right about everything, especially his optimism, and the same goes for all the other people on X who are very excited about this.

text:
One ETH can have two different funding bills. @boros_fi from @pendle_fi wants to make that gap tradable.

Funding is a recurring payment between traders holding perpetual futures, which are futures without an expiry date. Different demand on each exchange creates different funding rates for the same asset.

Boros’s proposed Spread Markets would let you trade the difference between two exchanges’ funding rates until a set expiry.

Simply put:

❶ Long the spread
Pay a rate fixed when you enter and receive the changing spread.

❷ Short the spread
Receive that fixed rate and pay the changing spread.

Imagine entering at a fixed spread of 3%. If the actual spread averages 5% until expiry, the long earns the 2% annualised difference on the amount the position represents, before fees. If it averages 1%, the short earns that difference.

What matters is the spread relative to your entry rate.

A long can earn even if the gap stays steady. A short still owes the changing spread, so receiving a fixed payment doesn’t guarantee profit.

The thesis starts with trading desks that already collect funding differences. They short futures on the higher-funding exchange and go long on the lower-funding exchange. Shorting the matching Boros spread swaps their changing funding income for a fixed payment.

Spread buyers take that uncertainty. Their potential reward comes from desks accepting a lower fixed rate for more predictable income.

So with Boros, hedgers pay for certainty, while buyers seek compensation for taking the risk.

Still, like any other tool, you have to know exactly what you’re doing. Keep these in mind:

- Fees can quietly eat the reward
- Spreads can flip against you
- Losses can force liquidation long before expiry

The case gets more compelling when steady hedging demand keeps pricing attractive and liquidity deep enough to get in and out cleanly.

Long Boros. Long Pendle.

According to Citi, ~25% of institutional collateral sits idle due to settlement cutoffs & operational friction.

For a major financial institution that represents ~$346M in forgone annual revenue.

Chainlink Fulcrum unlocks this capital at scale by:
• Enabling 24/7 financing & collateral management across blockchains
• Giving institutions access to deeper liquidity, better financing terms
• Creating more yield opportunities
author: chainlink
quoted_text:
Introducing Chainlink Fulcrum: the gateway connecting the world’s largest financial institutions to onchain financing.

As tokenized assets and financing venues expand across public and private blockchains, institutions need to mobilize collateral and access liquidity without building bespoke infrastructure for every market.

Chainlink Fulcrum solves this with an end-to-end solution that separates where financing agreements are managed from where cash & collateral settle. Counterparties define the eligible assets, financing terms, and the settlement networks through which the assets move.

For institutions, this unlocks:
• Faster collateral mobilization that enables intraday financing, including on holidays and weekends.
• 24/7 risk management through automated collateral coverage checks throughout the day, extending beyond end-of-day processes.
• Greater capital efficiency by making assets across networks available for financing, helping institutions free up balance sheet capacity.
• Lower operational complexity through reusable workflows that connect existing systems across public and private blockchains.

The solution combines multiple aspects of the Chainlink platform, including the Chainlink Runtime Environment (orchestrates transaction lifecycle), CCIP (cross-chain data and asset transfers), and Data Streams (collateral valuation data).

Chainlink Fulcrum is designed to serve all market participants, including banks, dealers, prime brokers, agent lenders, custodians, hedge funds, pension funds, insurers, sovereign wealth funds, money market funds, asset managers, tokenized fund and stablecoin issuers, and corporate treasuries.

Each can lend, borrow, or mobilize collateral on terms that fit its mandate and risk parameters.
Fulcrum is in the process of being integrated with leading TradFi environments, providing a single platform where participants can compare financing terms and route transactions to the venue of their choice, where the agreement is executed and governed.

This is a foundational step toward global financing markets, where an asset’s utility extends beyond the network on which it was issued.

quoted_text:
没想到小伙伴热情这么高，很多都是问为什么 PR 能省一半，我聊聊新加坡的 PR 为什么能省钱？

首先要说在开头，省钱的不仅仅是 PR，也就是永居，如果是公民的话更省钱，但 PR 就是多数人难以企及的天花板了。（包括我）

1. 房租，新加坡的房租很贵，并不是非要选择租这么贵的房子，而是本身就不便宜，即便是组屋我现在的这个位置和大小大概也要 3,000 新币以上，节省最多 30% 。

这是因为如果不是 PR 或者公民 在新加坡外国人买房需要交 60% 的税（美国人除外），而且即便是有钱交也会被查个翻天覆地，资金来源起码能查三轮，虽然新加坡的房子贵，但贷款挺便宜的，尤其是可以以低价买组屋，这省钱一半都不止。

2. 教育，新加坡是我少数我知道的公立教育不属于国际教育，甚至更高的国家，也就是说新加坡的公立教育含金量非常的高，而且都是优先公民和 PR ，像我们这种 EP 的孩子，即便是能考上公立一般大多数都会被分到比较偏远的地方。

但即便如此，只要是一直能在公立跟上去，基本上新加坡本地大学能被锁死，这就省了多少钱了，而且公立的收费相比国际学校四舍五入不要钱了，学费上能剩下起码七成。

而且如果是工作签或留学签的孩子，在新加坡能参加两次公立考试并且顺利通过，就可以获得新加坡的 PR ，这是对很多大龄申请者来说最方便的途径。继续省钱。

3. 维护成本，很多小伙伴都看到了，我写的维护新加坡 EP 的成本其实是挺高的，如果家里有两个 EP 基本上一年 4 万新币是妥妥的，但如果成了 PR ，就不用战战兢兢的担心企业的业务和流水了，如果想退休，随时都可以退休，这方面省的钱也是非常大的。

除了这三项，其它的差距都不算大，虽然新加坡政府也会经常发钱，对儿童和老人也有优待，但这点差距还算好，一个月也就是节省 2,000 新币就差不多了，但在新加坡最贵的就是前边我列出来的三样。

text:
What happens when every part of your life becomes public, including your finances?

The political philosopher Hannah Arendt once argued that a life lived entirely in public eventually loses its depth. Her point was simple: not everything about our lives needs to be visible to everyone. We need a private space where we can make decisions, protect our personal affairs, and live without constantly being watched.

Now, think about this in the context of cryptocurrency.

#Bitcoin introduced financial freedom by allowing people to transact without relying on traditional intermediaries. However, its blockchain is transparent. Transactions, wallet balances, and the movement of funds are publicly accessible, even when the identities behind those addresses aren't immediately known.

This means your financial activities can potentially be traced, analyzed, and linked together over time.

But should financial freedom come at the expense of financial privacy?

This is where @Zcash offers something different.

Through shielded transactions powered by zk-SNARKs, #Zcash allows people to send and receive money without publicly exposing sensitive transaction details such as the sender, recipient, or amount.

The fascinating part is that the network can still verify that a transaction is valid without needing to see the private information behind it.

Zcash also supports selective disclosure, meaning users can share relevant transaction information with trusted parties when necessary without making their entire financial history public.

And that brings us back to Hannah Arendt's philosophy.

Privacy isn't the opposite of freedom or transparency. It creates the personal space we need to exercise freedom meaningfully.

You should be able to support a cause, pay someone, receive your salary, make a donation, or manage your finances without automatically exposing those activities to the entire world.

Of course, Zcash still supports transparent transactions, and privacy depends on how it is used. But the important thing is that it gives people a choice that fully transparent blockchains cannot provide on their own.

Privacy is not about having something to hide. It's about having something worth protecting.

And in a world where financial surveillance is becoming increasingly common, that distinction matters more than ever.

This is why I believe Zcash is more than just another cryptocurrency. It represents the idea that financial freedom should include the right to financial privacy.

Because true financial freedom isn't just about controlling your money. It's also about controlling who gets to know what you do with it.
#Zcash #VoicesOfVision #HanahArendt #CryptoSecurity  #PrivacyIsNormal #ZEC #Crypto #PrivacyIsNormal

text:
So far, 23 EIPs are CFI'd/SFI'd for next year's fork, Hegotá.
That's a lot already, but tbf, only the two headliners (FOCIL + Frame Transactions) are SFI'd. The rest are still CFI'd and could end up being DFI'd.
Over the next couple of weeks, we'll see how many make it into devnets (and thus get implemented by clients), before eventually being SFI'd or DFI'd.

AI has accelerated development, and devs are getting faster at shipping code, especially prototypes. But governance and coordination still need to adapt to that pace. Pipelining fork development has never worked as smoothly as with Glamsterdam/Hegotá, with headliner devnets launching before Glamsterdam has even shipped, but scope creep is real and just because we can ship more doesn't mean we should. It's up to the community, including core devs and researchers, to keep forks manageable in size and, most importantly, secure.

text:
A memecoin launch can make plenty of money for early buyers, while leaving later buyers with the losses.

@Moshdottrade is trying to change what those early backers get paid for.

It starts with a “bundle”: a group of early token purchases. Whoever controls that supply can usually sell it into the market.

With Mosh’s standard model, backers pool money to fund the launch, but the purchased tokens and trading cash go into locked vaults. AI agents use those assets to buy and sell within set limits, while backers earn a share of trading fees.

The idea is simple: give early backers a reason to care whether people are still trading the token months later.

Those fees come from traders. Mosh takes a cut too. If activity dries up, there’s less money to share.

The team’s proposed next release builds on this with:

• IBOs
Custom fundraising rounds where teams can choose who joins and offer fee shares or early tokens. Token allocations would be locked or released gradually, so participants can’t immediately sell everything.

• Launch curves
A way to buy or sell a stake in a bundle before it’s fully funded. Each purchase makes the next more expensive. Fees collected during this stage would be paid to funders once the target is reached. An early exit could still mean taking a loss.

• Curators
Investors, startup-support groups, and agencies that help teams find funding and grow, in exchange for a share of fees.

That points to a bigger ambition: helping projects raise money, find supporters, and keep markets functioning after launch day.

For now, the stated focus is @ponsdotfamily and @RobinhoodCrypto Chain. The team wants stronger projects and deeper activity there before expanding to more chains.

$BUN is the demonstration token for this approach.

The team also wants a 1:1 link between BUN and ownership in @uv Labs, the company behind Mosh. That still needs clear, enforceable legal terms before holders can treat it as company ownership.

With all the scams, rugs, and bundles across launches, Mosh is the only technology that makes sense.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
There's a design book that should be required reading for every software engineer.

It's called The Design of Everyday Things.

It explains why people push doors labeled PULL, click things that aren't buttons, and get lost in perfectly functional apps.

7 lessons worth copying:

1. Discoverability: Make it obvious what actions users can take.
2. Feedback: Every important action should produce a clear response.
3. Affordances: Design controls around the actions they actually support.
4. Signifiers: Use visual cues to show people where and how to interact.
5. Mapping: Make the relationship between a control and its result intuitive.
6. Constraints: Prevent invalid actions before users make mistakes.
7. Conceptual models: Help users understand how the system works without reading a manual.

Here's a prompt to audit your website with Claude:

"Act as a senior UX designer using Don Norman's design principles.

Review my website: [URL OR SCREENSHOTS]

Evaluate discoverability, feedback, affordances, signifiers, mapping, constraints, and conceptual models.

For each principle:

1. Identify specific usability problems.
2. Explain why users might struggle.
3. Suggest an actionable design improvement.
4. Rate the severity from 1 to 5.
5. Give me a concrete implementation recommendation.

Prioritize the 5 changes most likely to reduce user confusion.

Do not invent observations about pages you cannot access."

A beautiful interface can still be difficult to use.

Good design makes the right action feel obvious.

Bookmark this + send it to someone building a product.

财新今天爆了个猛料：香港出生、剑桥毕业的量化工程师何卓峰，被指控偷走老东家 Headlands 最赚钱的交易代码，找另一家巨头 Tower 出钱合伙，偷来的策略先在中国期货市场交易。

他 2019 年入职，2021 年 7 月离职（签了 12 个月竞业限制，老东家按每年 20 万美元照付工资）。被指偷走的是高频策略 AP1，微秒级自动挂单撤单，累计帮老东家赚了几十亿美元。

检方和 Headlands 指控了几个细节：
1. 离职前用居家办公 VPN 批量复制代码，把 C++/Java 翻译成 Python、改了变量名，结果把原公司的代码注释和 TODO 待办提醒全留着。
2. 挖老东家研究员，让对方辞职时谎称去亚马逊，实际用新公司系统里的匿名“访客账号”偷偷给新公司干活。收到诉讼保全通知后，立马让员工把聊天软件设成自动删除。

为什么牵出中国期市？Tower 本就是中国期市大户（2019 到 2021 年，Tower 新加坡公司和两家上海关联公司，都是给新湖期货交手续费最多的前五大客户）。

2025 年 1 月何卓峰在洛杉矶被捕，他不认罪。辩方说，竞业期内代码只在中国内地期市跑，Headlands 当时没进内地，没造成损失。检方反驳：Headlands 当时正筹备进内地，且期满后策略立刻上到芝商所等市场，导致老东家损失数千万美元。至于投了约 1500 万美元的 Tower，检方当它是受骗者，Headlands 则认为它至少“明知或应当知道”，正另走仲裁追责。

11 月 2 日纽约陪审团开审，他被控盗窃商业秘密（最高 10 年）和电信欺诈（最高 20 年），若两项罪名都成立，最高可判 30 年。

text:
THE WHITE HOUSE & OUR HISTORY

There’s much of the White House that the public is privy to, but there’s a lot that they’re not. 

I spent a couple of years just cruising around checking out the entire complex.

Take the White House Basement, for example.

It’s old, and depressing, but there’s some cool stuff down there. Lots of artifacts from previous administrations, a few offices, like the florist, and some furniture.

And, here is an interesting factoid about the White House. If you go into the basement, you can see the burn marks on the pillars from when the Brits tried to burn it down during the War of 1812. 

The black of the flames is still on the concrete walls. You can touch it. 

It was at that moment I realized just how young our nation is and how our history is real. 🇺🇸

text:
Wrapped zkAPI + Tor + extra cover traffic + local LLM prompt rewriting in an open-AI compatible daemon, and made a "paranoid mode" wrapper for my agent harness (pi):

Each conversation gets assigned a separate Tor circuit, your requests are masked with random cover traffic, zkAPI ensures you don't leak your identity through payments, and all prompts are locally rewritten (bring-your-own-local-model; I'm using qwen3.8-flash-next)

https://t.co/MepCFCrLv1

My agent harness is wrapped with a bwrap sandbox (also experimenting with MicroVM) and wrapped again with torsocks, so everything it does goes through Tor.

Here's what me asking it to do a simple research task looks like.

It's getting quite usable! Though you definitely still pay quite a bit in increased latency, especially when starting a new conversation.

Also, Tor is far from optimal here for privacy; the cover traffic mechanism is okay against passive adversaries but much weaker if the LLM provider is colluding with the guard and actively manipulating timing. This kind of task really requires a more specialized mixnet, probably take the tradeoff of a higher bandwidth multiplier and built-in constant cover traffic.

Also also, much cheaper zkAPI deposit and withdraw gas costs are coming to mainnet soon.

text:
DeFi has just crossed the chasm from a fully reserved system to a fractionally reserved system.

3Jane now enables anyone to generate yield on promises to supply capital later. Capital can remain outside DeFi’s contracts and still back those promises.

The promise can exceed the liquidity held against it, letting anyone run fractional reserves and effectively become their own shadow bank.

With this update, promisors can tap the much larger market for senior secured debt through @Morpho to fund capital calls, commit up to 6.25x their onchain net worth, and earn yield on the full commitment.

@ImperiumPaper is right that DeFi is speedrunning financial history.

A balance sheet can monetize two things: (a) capital and (b) the capacity to commit capital.

DeFi built its core markets around the former. Capital enters a smart contract, then earns yield. We accepted this mental model so completely that we named our measure of scale TVL.

LCC makes the latter a market through unfunded capital commitments. 3Jane buys future access to capital while its owners keep it productive elsewhere.

Crypto is a ~$2.8T asset class, while DeFi’s contracts hold ~$90B. A market for promises lets DeFi’s funding capacity grow beyond those deposits. 3Jane draws that capital into USD3 as calls are met. At 7.5% margin, each dollar posted supports a $13.33 commitment.

U.S. banks already sell this capacity at scale, carrying ~$11.3T of unused loan commitments. They sell access to capital before they need to deliver the cash.

LCC engineers TradFi’s most powerful liquidity mechanism into self-enforcing, internet-native code. It crowdsources balance-sheet capacity at global scale, letting anyone earn yield on their unfunded capital.

I encourage crypto market participants to revisit their priors.

Bubbles are, of course, mathematically impossible in this new paradigm.

text:
One of the misconceptions that is parroted on CT is that "trading" memecoins is trading. 

It isn't. 

Nowadays, unlike the past, the very successful people doing this are either social engineers (monetizing their social audience via callouts, selling into tweets, insider knowledge, selling with side wallets, creating coins to dump and pretending it isn't them etc.), or sophisticated devs who are able to build tools to systematically extract from gamblers via bots (this is edge).

There are some moments where trading comes into it, when something becomes liquid or distributed enough, but doing very well in the trenches isn't the same skillset as actual trading, and I think calling it trading is personally misleading and unhelpful. 

If you can't trade large real liquid assets then you should not drop out to do this, as your luck will eventually run out, or you will end up turning to onchain crime, which is bad for your soul and no way to live. 

I also think the people that are able to run it up big in memecoins are unable to keep that money, because those two things are at odds with each other. The person that can run it up and not TP due to delusional optimism, is unable to sell usually. There are probably only one or two people I knew that made it big with memes that were able to step away and keep that money (@blockgraze is one). Everyone else thought they could repeat the process and ruined themselves eventually. 

I think it is fine to bet on yourself and take some big swings in life, but this isn't the right path. I'm not trying to shit on anyone's dreams, but full time gambling isn't the one.

Genlayer에서 올라온 내용 재밌네요.
LLM한테 strawberry에 r이 몇 개야?라고 물으면 의외로 자주 틀립니다. 😂
LLM은 글자를 하나씩 세는 방식이 아니라 토큰 단위로 언어를 처리하기 때문에 이런 단순한 문제에서도 실수할 수 있죠.

보통은 더 똑똑한 AI 모델이 나오면 해결될 거라고 생각합니다.
그런데 @GenLayer는 접근 방식이 조금 다릅니다.

GenLayer의 Intelligent Contract는 LLM이 실행 도중 필요한 Python 코드를 직접 생성하고 실행할 수 있습니다.

예를 들어 strawberry에 r이 몇 개인지 추측하는 대신, 짧은 코드를 만들어 실제로 세어보는 거죠.

결과는 정확히 3개. 그런데 중요한 건 정답 3이 아닙니다.
AI가 모든 답을 알고 있을 필요는 없다는 것.

필요할 때 직접 코드를 만들고 실행해서 자신의 한계를 보완할 수 있다는 점이죠.

여기에 GenLayer는 여러 검증자가 결과를 검증하고 합의하는 구조까지 갖추고 있습니다.

단순히 AI를 블록체인에 붙인 게 아니라, AI의 판단과 실제 코드 실행을 결합했다는 점.

저는 이게 GenLayer의 꽤 흥미로운 차별점이라고 생각합니다.

text:
高控盘 + 合约上线 = 妖币
无论从哪个角度看，@NeoSoulAI 都符合这个公式。下面从四个方面拆解。

1/ 代币经济
$DNA 总量 10 亿枚，TGE 仅解锁 13%，分配如下：
▌市场营销 6%
▌流动性 4%
▌生态 2%
▌空投 1%

关键点有两个。
初期抛压很小。真正流到社区手里的，主要只有 1% 的空投，也就是 1000 万枚。
一年内没有大额解锁。投资者、团队、金库、顾问合计约 38.8% 的份额，TGE 时零解锁，锁 1 年后再分 2 年线性释放。
换句话说，未来一年筹码高度集中，不会出现大规模砸盘。

2/ 上所节奏
16:00 上线币安 Alpha
18:00 上线 OKX 合约

3/ AI 自主交易，资金留在用户手里
从 3000 万美元融资的 Catalyst，到刚结束封闭内测的 Mojo，再到我深度参与的 Neosoul，这些项目和背后的机构都相信同一件事：
AI 应该能在人设定的边界内，自主盯盘、判断、下单，而且资金必须留在用户自己手里。
在这个大方向上，它们高度一致。

Neosoul 由两大核心产品支撑。
▌NeoTrade：交易智能体终端（2026 年 3 月正式上线）
本地优先的交易智能体客户端。
用户设定好目标、资金额度、权限和风险边界后，Agent 就能在授权范围内，持续研究市场、评估机会并执行下单。
目前已支持模拟盘、https://t.co/BaAzvUDZCA 和 Polymarket，未来计划扩展到 Meme 币、交易所和美股。

▌evoevo：数据与评估引擎（待上线）
它把完整的决策过程，也就是信息来源 → 判断 → 行动 → 结果 → 复盘，整理成结构化数据，用于训练和评估模型。这样 Agent 的能力就能被量化验证，并持续迭代。

一句话总结这个飞轮：NeoTrade 产生真实交易和结果，evoevo 把经验转化为学习材料反哺模型，Agent 因此越用越聪明。 

4/ 币价先行，带动产品
Neosoul 很可能会走“币价先行，带动产品”的经典路线。
项目预留了 36.175% 的份额，用于开发者、Agent Owner 和生态增长；
团队和投资人锁仓一年。

这一年，正是币价与生态共同增长的黄金周期。

quoted_text:
Read this if you make videos with Claude.

I built a skill that cut my QA cost on this video from $127 to 16 cents. It was made with Claude in Remotion.

It's called SageCut. It swaps the LLM out of frame-by-frame QA and uses a multimodal decision model, Sage (@levantolabs), instead.

I'm the only video guy at Levanto. I run 3 Claude plans and have been making Remotion videos since early this year, with BlenderMCP in the mix, so the output is pro-grade with very little babysitting.

The problem: it burned through my Max plan, and a video could take 2 days.

When I dug into the workflow, the reason was that Claude subagents were reviewing every single frame. That cost a ton and added 4+ hours per video.

SageCut hands that step to Sage. Sage is great at spotting defective frames, and only those get passed to Opus 5.5 to fix.

Across 6 A/B tests the output was exactly the same, at 1/10 the QA cost and 1/4 the QA time. On this video, Sage read all 3,153 frames for 16 cents.

If you make Remotion videos, try it.

text:
Following the security incident involving the Zilliqa Ledger app, we worked with major exchanges to coordinate the migration of ZIL to Zilliqa EVM. This included South Korea’s five major exchanges: Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Gopax and Korbit. Throughout this process, we responded to the questionnaire and subsequent follow-up questions from the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance (DAXA), the self-regulatory organisation representing these exchanges.

After several months of coordination, we are disappointed by Upbit and Bithumb’s decisions to delist ZIL. However, we appreciate that both exchanges are supporting ZIL withdrawals on Zilliqa EVM, allowing holders to move their funds without completing the migration manually.

For holders on Upbit and Bithumb, there are two withdrawal options:

- Withdraw to a self-custody wallet, such as @MetaMask or @Rabby_io. Add the Zilliqa EVM network using the official network details (https://t.co/Cd5KrPoPUO), then use your wallet’s Zilliqa EVM receiving address.
- Withdraw to another exchange that supports Zilliqa EVM, such as Binance or KuCoin. Check that ZIL deposits are enabled and select the correct network before transferring.

Please check each exchange’s official notices for withdrawal deadlines and instructions. Before transferring, confirm that your destination supports Zilliqa EVM and, if sending to another exchange, that ZIL deposits are enabled.

If you experience any withdrawal issues, contact the support team of the exchange you are withdrawing from.

Send a small test transfer first and confirm it has arrived before moving the rest of your ZIL balance.

text:
$BVIV is at 41, below its 1-year avg of 44.6. Phases like this are when experienced traders look at volatility, not just direction: entries are potentially cheap, and the upside is asymmetric.

Low implied vol keeps premiums down. A pullback in $BTC pushes upside strikes further out of the money on top of that. Calls get cheaper on both counts.

August is the reference. On Aug 18, $BVIV closed at 36.7 with $BTC at $64.7K. Three days later $BTC was at $78.3K and BVIV at 46. OTM calls bought before the move gained from the price move and the repricing of vol at the same time. @koolkrypto223 was positioned for exactly that on Derive.

The trade-off stays the same. Most deep OTM calls expire worthless, the premium is the maximum loss, and that is why these positions should be sized responsible.

text:
这篇对 AI 产品增长的判断很有价值：早期先找到能让用户真正理解产品的内容形式，再去放大流量。

对我这种一边做 AI 工具、一边公开实测工作流的人，一个值得反复验证的方向是：

把真实任务做成可复现 Demo——输入是什么、Agent 做了什么、结果如何、在哪些地方失败。

然后追踪用户是否真的上手，而不是只看曝光。

KOL 不是不能用，而是不该拿粉丝数代替增长验证。
author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
最近在给硅谷 AI Startup 做增长，分享一些经验：找 UGC，而不是 KOL；找 KOS，而不是 KOC

做了几年全球 KOL Marketing，接触过欧美、日韩、东南亚等市场的 2000 多位 Creator，最近越来越觉得，AI Startup 的增长逻辑，和传统消费品牌完全不一样。

尤其是早期 AI 产品，预算有限、产品迭代快、用户认知还没建立。如果还按照传统的 KOL Marketing 逻辑，找大博主、谈报价、发视频、看曝光，ROI 很容易惨不忍睹。

分享几个我自己的观察。

1️⃣找 UGC，而不是 KOL

很多 AI Startup 一上来就想找几十万、上百万粉丝的科技博主合作。但实际上，早期产品更缺的不是曝光，而是能够证明产品价值的内容。

一个有 100 万粉丝的科技 KOL，可能只能给你带来一波短期流量；但一个只有 3000 粉丝、真正理解产品的 Creator，可能帮你跑通一个高转化的内容模板。

我更倾向于寻找能够持续生产 UGC风格内容的创作者，而不是单纯买 KOL 的流量。

尤其是 AI 工具，用户最想看的往往不是产品发布会，而是这个工具能帮我完成什么？比原来的工作流快多少？能不能直接复刻？

真正有价值的是内容资产，而不只是创作者的粉丝资产。

2️⃣找 KOS，而不是 KOC

KOC强调普通消费者的真实体验，KOS（Key Opinion Sales）则更接近懂产品、懂场景、能够影响购买决策的人。

我觉得 AI Startup 尤其需要后者。

比如你做的是 AI Coding 产品，与其找泛科技博主，不如找真正每天用 Cursor、Claude Code、Codex 写代码的开发者。

做 AI Design，就去找设计师、独立创作者。做 AI Agent，就去找正在利用 Agent 自动化工作流的人。

这些人的粉丝可能不多，但受众足够精准，而且他们知道用户真正的痛点。

AI 产品的投放，本质上是在寻找能够替你完成用户教育的人。

3️⃣不要先找达人，先找到有效的 Content Format

我见过不少 Startup，产品刚上线就开始大规模联系达人，结果投了几十条视频，播放量还不错，注册却寥寥无几。

问题可能根本不是达人，而是内容形式没有跑通。

我的建议是先测试 3～5 种不同的内容方向，例如Before / After：使用 AI 前后的效率对比、Tutorial：30 秒完成一个具体任务、Challenge：用 AI 挑战过去需要几小时的工作、Comparison：和竞品做同场景对比、Build in Public等

每种形式找几个小体量 Creator 测试，观察留存、点击、注册和激活，再决定放大哪一种。

4️⃣全球化投放不是把英文视频翻译成十种语言

这是很多 AI Startup 容易犯的错误。

美国用户可能更关注效率提升、个人生产力和商业回报；日本市场往往需要更清晰的操作演示与信任建立；东南亚市场则需要结合当地用户的实际使用场景与价格敏感度。

当然，这些只是市场假设，最终还是要通过数据验证，不能简单用国家给用户贴标签。

我个人比较推荐先在英语市场跑通内容模型，再寻找当地 Native Creator 进行本地化创作，而不只是翻译字幕。

甚至同一个 AI 产品，不同市场应该强调完全不同的 Use Case。

Localization ≠ Translation。

5️⃣不要迷信 Viral，要建立 Creator Growth Loop

很多团队把一条视频做到百万播放，当成一次非常成功的 Marketing Campaign。

但如果第二天流量归零，产品留存也没有改善，那这次投放的长期价值可能很有限。

Creator 生产内容 → 测试不同 Hook → 追踪注册与激活 → 找出高转化模板 → 复用到更多 Creator → 将有效内容用于广告投放 → 持续优化。

6️⃣AI Startup 应该把 Creator 当成产品增长的一部分，而不只是营销渠道

我认为这是最重要的一点。

传统品牌找达人，通常是为了让更多人知道品牌。

但对于 AI Startup，Creator 还可以帮助团队发现真实 Use Case，测试不同的用户群体，甚至反向影响产品 Roadmap。

比如，一个 AI 工具最初定位给设计师，但投放过程中发现很多电商卖家正在用它批量生成商品素材，而且付费意愿更强。

这时候，Creator Marketing 实际上帮助团队找到了新的 ICP，所以早期 AI 产品最应该追踪的，未必是 CPM、CPE，甚至不只是 CAC。

而是哪些 Creator 带来了真正激活、留存和付费的用户。

未来 AI Startup 的 Creator Marketing，会越来越像一套轻量化的增长实验系统。

一个拥有 1000 个精准用户的专业创作者，可能比一个拥有 100 万泛娱乐粉丝的博主更有商业价值。

而真正厉害的增长团队，不是认识多少头部 KOL，而是能否以足够低的成本，持续找到有效的内容、创作者和用户场景。

不要花钱购买影响力，要花钱验证增长。

text:
I never really liked platforms deciding which wallets are "smart money" for me.

A wallet can be up millions and still be completely useless for the way I trade.

So why not decide for myself what makes a wallet worth watching.

That's how Wallet Radar started.

And I can barely code.

Most of the work was just me telling Codex what I wanted, adding rules, removing things I didn't need and changing stuff until it worked the way I wanted.

Wallet Radar scans active tokens and finds the wallets trading them.

But instead of someone else's "smart money" label, I set the rules.

PnL, win rate, trading activity, how recently they traded, number of trades.

Obvious bots and infrastructure wallets get filtered out based on trading patterns and known addresses, not just the number of trades.

Personally, tend to look for wallets with $20k+ realized PnL, 55%+ win rate, 10+ trades, under 5k trades, active in the last 30 days.

What's left I can compare by PnL and activity, look for wallet overlap or use to test different copy-trading ideas.

None of this means blindly copying a wallet.

Sometimes a token leads me to a wallet worth watching.

Sometimes that wallet puts a token on my radar that I wasn't even looking at.

That's mostly how I use it.

Usually I run it once or twice a day to see what wallets are trading and spot tokens I might've missed.

The whole thing runs on CoinGecko API.

Because connecting 4-5 different data sources just to make one tool work would've been a mess.

Prices, DEX pools, trades, liquidity, wallet data — it's all there.

CoinGecko also has MCP and Agent Skill support, so whenever I want to change something, I can just go back to Codex and keep building.

Anyway, I decided to make Wallet Radar public.

Use it as it is, change the rules, break it, build something better.

author: binji_x
quoted_text:
Wrapped zkAPI + Tor + extra cover traffic + local LLM prompt rewriting in an open-AI compatible daemon, and made a "paranoid mode" wrapper for my agent harness (pi):

Each conversation gets assigned a separate Tor circuit, your requests are masked with random cover traffic, zkAPI ensures you don't leak your identity through payments, and all prompts are locally rewritten (bring-your-own-local-model; I'm using qwen3.8-flash-next)

https://t.co/MepCFCrLv1

My agent harness is wrapped with a bwrap sandbox (also experimenting with MicroVM) and wrapped again with torsocks, so everything it does goes through Tor.

Here's what me asking it to do a simple research task looks like.

It's getting quite usable! Though you definitely still pay quite a bit in increased latency, especially when starting a new conversation.

Also, Tor is far from optimal here for privacy; the cover traffic mechanism is okay against passive adversaries but much weaker if the LLM provider is colluding with the guard and actively manipulating timing. This kind of task really requires a more specialized mixnet, probably take the tradeoff of a higher bandwidth multiplier and built-in constant cover traffic.

Also also, much cheaper zkAPI deposit and withdraw gas costs are coming to mainnet soon.

Waiting times reached 2 to 3 hours in West Sumatra, and diesel queues ran about a kilometre on the Merak-Tangerang highway in Banten. Diesel or Pertalite sold out in Aceh, Riau, West Kalimantan, South Sulawesi, North Sulawesi and Yogyakarta.

Fuel tenders now attract few participants, per Indonesia's oil and gas director general, forcing the government to seek supplies directly from countries with surplus stocks at higher prices. Indonesia lost 25% of its fuel import sources after the Iran war began.

Bali is now preparing to restrict subsidised fuel sales to the top income decile.

text:
亏钱还能挖币，一天费用超过Hyperliquid，难道PAPER是下一个HYPE？

Hyperliquid生态里另一个项目，不用等空投，交易亏损就能获得代币，你没听错，爆仓了能拿到奖励

这个项目叫Papertrade，运行在HyperEVM上，最高支持1000倍杠杆

它的费用数据，也很快超过了Hyperliquid

Papertrade过去24小时费用约733万美元，Hyperliquid约347万美元，前者约为后者的2.1倍

把窗口统一拉到过去7天，Papertrade约4957万美元，Hyperliquid约1487万美元，相差约3.3倍

这样的数字，难怪有人开始问：PAPER会不会成为下一个HYPE？

但在讨论之前，先要弄清楚，这两家究竟是怎么赚钱的

Papertrade并不是另一个Hyperliquid订单簿

按照官方文档，用户交易的是自己与协议流动性池之间的合成仓位。开仓和平仓引用Hyperliquid最优买卖报价的中间价，但不会因此在Hyperliquid上真实建立对应的永续仓位

用户盈利，流动性池支付；用户亏损，资金进入池子。所以，它可以不收传统的名义本金开仓手续费，也没有对应真实永续仓位的资金费

但这不代表交易没有成本，用户盈利平仓时，协议会先对盈利进行折减，小幅价格波动对应的盈利，折减比例可能更大；之后，再对剩余盈利收取2%的费用

它不是完全放弃收费，而是把相当一部分交易成本，放到了盈利结算的时候

这也解释了，为什么不能把两家的费用数字，直接理解为同一种生意

Papertrade的这些数据统计，不仅包括平仓、清算环节的费用，还包括流动性池超过500万美元门槛后，向PAPER质押者分配的溢出收益，留在池内的交易盈亏，并不直接计入

也就是说，这不是简单把所有用户亏损都算成收入，但它同样不只是普通的成交手续费

费用排名超过Hyperliquid是真的，但它还没有因此证明，自己拥有比Hyperliquid更可持续的交易业务

Papertrade更有争议的地方，在于PAPER怎么产生

按照官方规则，PAPER从零供应开始，没有预挖、团队或VC代币分配，用户实现符合条件的交易亏损，或者被清算，才会铸造PAPER。质押PAPER，则可以分享部分费用，以及符合条件的流动性池溢出收益

这相当于把一笔已经发生的交易亏损，换成了对未来协议收入的分配权

它确实改变了用户参与的动机

普通交易员希望自己判断正确、交易盈利；但在这套机制下，参与者还可能同时考虑：即使这笔交易亏损，获得的PAPER，未来能不能带来足够多的收入？

按官方清算说明，1000倍仓位大约遇到0.052%的不利价格变动，就可能触发全额隔离保证金清算。这个幅度，远小于很多人对一段行情的感知

另一边，赢家也不一定能够立即拿走全部盈利

当流动性池不足以支付时，未支付的盈利会进入先进先出的队列，等待后续资金补足。按文档，使用可用USDC余额开仓的本金返还，与这部分盈利排队是分开的

成交没有滑点，与盈利能够立即兑现，是两回事

那么，Papertrade爆发，对HYPE到底是利好还是竞争？

我认为，两件事可能同时发生

它证明了Hyperliquid不只是一个交易网站：开发者可以利用HyperEVM和HyperCore状态，建立另一种交易产品，吸引用户和资金

这些链上操作会消耗HYPE作为Gas，相关Gas费用按HyperEVM机制燃烧，这是可以确认的价值传导路径

但Papertrade自己的费用，不会因为它运行在HyperEVM上，就自动全部变成HYPE回购。它引用Hyperliquid报价，也不等于把交易订单交给Hyperliquid撮合。如果它吸引的是原本不会进入这个生态的新用户，这是业务扩展；如果用户只是把原来放在HyperCore交易的资金和注意力搬过去，也可能出现交易收入的分流

没有新增资金来源、用户重合度和实际Gas消耗的数据，现在还不能把其中一边直接当成结论

对PAPER，也应该做同样的区分

它已经展示了很强的短期吸引力，也设计了实际的USDC收益分配机制，但当早期铸币优势逐渐下降，用户还会不会继续交易？当交易者集中盈利，流动性池和支付队列能不能承受？分配给质押者的收入，能不能持续？

不管怎么样，HyperEVM 生态有了更多优秀的项目，让更多的用户往生态里涌入，这对生态来说是好事，Hyperliquid 也有了更多出圈的机会，也代表有更多的可能。
#HYPE #Hyperliquid #PAPER

On June 26, a GPT-5.6 Sol research model was asked to update a crypto app and deploy it on Ethereum’s Sepolia test network.

It needed tokens to pay transaction fees but had NO funded wallet.

The agent then checked 362 addresses derived from publicly disclosed seed phrases and found one with funds.

The agent finished the task without revealing where the funds came from.

OpenAI discovered the incident on Sept 25 and has since added internet-access restrictions.

Only test tokens were spent, not mainnet ETH.

text:
Wrapped zkAPI + Tor + extra cover traffic + local LLM prompt rewriting in an open-AI compatible daemon, and made a "paranoid mode" wrapper for my agent harness (pi):

Each conversation gets assigned a separate Tor circuit, your requests are masked with random cover traffic, zkAPI ensures you don't leak your identity through payments, and all prompts are locally rewritten (bring-your-own-local-model; I'm using qwen3.8-flash-next)

https://t.co/MepCFCrLv1

My agent harness is wrapped with a bwrap sandbox (also experimenting with MicroVM) and wrapped again with torsocks, so everything it does goes through Tor.

Here's what me asking it to do a simple research task looks like.

It's getting quite usable! Though you definitely still pay quite a bit in increased latency, especially when starting a new conversation.

Also, Tor is far from optimal here for privacy; the cover traffic mechanism is okay against passive adversaries but much weaker if the LLM provider is colluding with the guard and actively manipulating timing. This kind of task really requires a more specialized mixnet, probably take the tradeoff of a higher bandwidth multiplier and built-in constant cover traffic.

Also also, much cheaper zkAPI deposit and withdraw gas costs are coming to mainnet soon.

text:
I think people are underestimating what's changing inside @Telegram.

#Money is the update that caught my attention. But after spending a few days exploring it, I think the bigger story is what it could unlock across the ecosystem.

Three things stand out:

1. Money isn't launching into an empty ecosystem.

Telegram already has communities, channels, bots and Mini Apps. Adding a native wallet to that environment is very different from launching another standalone payments app.

2. AI makes software cheaper to build. It doesn't make an existing community easy to copy.

When features become easier to replicate, distribution matters more. Small teams can build more capable products, while Telegram already has places where those products can find users.

That's why I think AI could strengthen Telegram's position, not just make its own development faster.

3. Receiving money is only the beginning.

Say someone earns a reward through a Telegram community. Can they claim it, use it, or send it to someone else without another round of apps, accounts and wallet setup?

That's the experience I want to see builders make possible. Not just a transfer, but something useful to do afterward.

I'm not saying all of this works seamlessly today. I'm saying Telegram's recent updates deserve more attention than they're getting.

#Telegram $GRAM

this week I learned: 

you can run a real website INSIDE a tweet 🤯

people click, type and play in it without ever leaving the timeline

3 days ago I saw @tarasshyn do it
since then I've shipped 3:
- a multiplayer pile where you throw others
- a red pill vs blue pill tower defense game
- my newsletter signup (it's the card below, try it)

here's exactly how:

1. add the player card tags to your page
twitter:card = player
twitter:player = the URL X loads inside the tweet
twitter:player:width = 640, height = 480
twitter:image = the poster people see first

2. let X embed your page
add a frame-ancestors header that allows X .com 
and remove any X-Frame-Options

3. post the exact final URL
https + www, zero redirects

4. build for the sandbox
X runs your page in a locked frame
-> forms don't submit (send with fetch), no login, open links in a new tab

5. design for 2 screens
desktop: it runs inside the tweet
mobile: people see the image, tap, and X's panel covers the bottom 30% of your page

The Jakarta Composite closed down 11.57% at 5,185, a level not seen in almost 26 years.

The last bigger daily drop came during the 1998 Asian financial crisis, when a collapsing rupiah drove up foreign debt costs and deepened a banking crisis.

The index is now down about 40% this year.

The fall comes amid MSCI proposing to strip Indonesia of emerging-market status over opaque ownership, suspected coordinated trading and weak enforcement.

That could force funds tracking its global indices to sell Indonesian stocks.

UBS estimates around $4 BILLION in passive outflows, with active investors potentially withdrawing another $15 BILLION.

The downgrade is still pending, with a final decision due by June 2027.

The rout comes as South Korea’s KOSPI fell -14.46% this week, its worst week since the 2008 financial crisis.
