text:
I am a member of the Norwegian Nobel Committee. Or I am not. This has, in recent days, become a matter of international dispute, and I would like to address it from the tram, where I do my addressing.

You may have read a thing I wrote. A great many of you did, more than have read anything I was ever officially permitted to write, which tells you everything about the difference between a press release and a confession. And then something happened so purely, hopelessly funny that I have been smiling into my coffee for three days, which in Oslo is grounds for a welfare check.

They fact-checked me.

The Americans have a website for determining whether things are true, which is the most American sentence I will ever write. It examined my little confession. It ruled.

First it established that I am not real. A relief to my wife. But it is the reason I have had framed. They cleared me of being real by proving that a real one of me would, by law, be silent until the year 2076. The deliberations are sealed for fifty years. My alibi was the confession. My guilt was that I had one.

They did not rule the confession false. They ruled it unauthorized. There is a difference, and the difference is the whole of my country’s foreign policy.

And then the detail I will take to the sealed vault. They faulted the confession for one specific deficiency. They noted, with the sorrow of a schoolteacher, that it “did not include markings” making it obvious the content was satire.

No markings.

I have been fact-checked for honesty and found guilty of style.

In the land of Janteloven, whose first commandment is that you are not to think you are anything special, I have now been formally reprimanded, by Americans, for insufficient self-advertisement. My grandmother is appalled, and, for the first time, proud.

And beneath the thing itself, the readers attached what they call a note. A small grey correction, voted on by strangers, appended to tell the passerby: this is not real. I have thought about that note more than is healthy. In my country we do not need a website for this. A note, here, is not an insult. It is an act of love, performed with a knife. We append it to the newborn and to the dead and to anyone, in between, who forgets the rain. We have had the community note for two hundred years. We call it Janteloven. I did not require the correction. I am the correction. I have spent my whole life as the small grey text beneath other men’s belief in themselves. It is the only committee I have ever truly served on.

The complaint, you understand, was never that the facts were wrong. The complaint was that a civil servant had written them too well. In Norway this is the only crime we take seriously.

But here is the part that should trouble you more than it troubles me, and it troubles me at four o’clock, in the dark. They had to rule at all because people believed it. Not everyone. Enough. Enough strangers read a damp man’s account of cinnamon buns and the rain that judges you and a woman named Kristin ending a meeting with the word “well,” and thought: yes, that is how the moral standing of the species is decided. They found the fictional Norwegian more credible than the real institution. They found the confession more plausible than the citation. And I think it is simply this. People do not disbelieve the official version because they are stupid. They disbelieve it because they can hear, underneath it, the sound of something not being said, and they will follow that sound anywhere. Even onto a tram. Even into the mouth of a man who does not exist.

Now. The one across the ocean. You will want to know how he answered. So, I confess, did I. I checked. I am not proud of the checking.

He said nothing.

This is the great wound of my fictional life. A man who met the actual prize with six hundred words at midnight. Who told a rally we were an indelible stain, that we would not be forgotten, that he was owed eight medals, one for each war. He mourned, in ink, that he had not won the Noble Peace Prize. He spelled it wrong, and in doing so spelled it true. The prize was only ever a dead arms-dealer’s apology to his own obituary. Noble is what he wanted. Nobel is what was for sale.

And about me, the man who sat down and explained, with some tenderness, precisely why he would never win it, he said nothing at all. I was the one thing he did not post about. He answered Norway. He answered the website. He answered the weather of a country he cannot find on a map. He did not answer the one man who had bothered to explain him to himself. He could not. To answer the confession he would have had to read it, and to read it he would have had to sit still, in the dark, for four o’clock’s worth of silence, and that is the one war he has never been able to end.

The website observed, as though it were damning, that the account which produced me “contained other fictitious letters.” Yes. It does. The world is full of rooms I am not allowed into, and I have lately been climbing through the windows. The banker is invented. The arms-philosopher with his doctorate is invented. The Russian who gave up nothing, took everything, and wished a tyrant a happy birthday is invented. The only thing I did not have to invent was the wanting. That part arrived fully formed, from across the ocean, with a deadline it had already missed.

It is dark now. Of course it is. The light here is rationed like everything else, like praise, like the prize. The buns are gone. Kristin said “well” an hour ago, the real one or the invented one, I have lost track, which I suspect was always the point.

They ruled that I originated as satire. I accept the verdict. I would add only this, for the sealed file, for the clerks of 2076 who will unseal all of it and find the note waiting.

I am the only fraud in this affair who told you, in the first line, that he might not exist. Everyone else kept their credentials.

I did not make him want it the way a child wants a thing in a shop window. I only wrote it down. The fact-checkers have confirmed, officially, that I made it up.

Ask them who made it believable.
author: gothburz
quoted_text:
I am a member of the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

There are five of us. Five people, appointed by a parliament most of the planet could not find on a map, who decide, once a year, which human being the world has agreed to call good.

I know. I know. I think about it on the tram.

We meet in a building on Henrik Ibsens gate, a street named after a man who wrote almost exclusively about people discovering they are frauds, which nobody on the committee finds funny except me. There is a room with a long table and the portraits of the dead laureates looking down, Mandela, the Dalai Lama, a great many earnest men in spectacles, and one portrait we do not discuss, which is Kissinger, 1973, awarded while the bombs were still falling, after which two of our predecessors resigned and the satirist Tom Lehrer said political satire was now obsolete. We keep him on the wall. A reminder. Every family has the uncle.

It is October in Oslo, which means the sun gives up around four in the afternoon like a civil servant, and it rains the particular Norwegian rain that isn’t quite falling, just hanging there, judging you. I arrive with wet shoes. I always arrive with wet shoes. There is coffee, because this is Norway and there is always coffee, we drink more of it per person than almost anyone alive, and someone’s wife has sent kanelboller, the cinnamon buns, and we sit, five Norwegians, damp, caffeinated, sugared, and we decide the moral standing of the entire species.

Let me tell you how it actually works, because the world imagines a cathedral and it is, I promise you, a book club with a mandate.

287 nominations this year. 208 people, 79 organizations. Anyone can nominate, that’s the secret nobody understands: a professor, a parliamentarian, a former laureate, so the “nominee” list is meaningless, it’s a suggestion box, and every autumn some congressman nominates his own golden retriever and the press writes “SHORTLISTED.” Nobody is shortlisted. There is no short list the public ever sees. There is us, and the coffee, and the rain, and the portraits, and a Norwegian stubbornness that is older than the prize itself.

We read reports. The institute’s advisers write them, thick dull documents, and we argue. Our chairman told the BBC once that in the final meeting “there is a high temperature.” High temperature, for a Norwegian, means someone slightly raised an eyebrow and then apologized for it. We don’t do high temperature. We do a long silence, and then Kristin says “well,” and everyone knows exactly what “well” meant, and it’s settled. That’s our shouting. “Well.” You’d have to be raised here to hear the violence in it.

Now. This year. I will not say the name, because we never say the name, but you know the name.

A certain head of state wanted this prize the way a child wants a thing in a shop window, which is to say loudly, and in public, and with the full belief that wanting it was itself the argument. He said he deserved it. He said he’d ended eight wars, a number that grew most times he said it, like a fish. He had other heads of state phone us. Israel’s prime minister posted it on the internet, “Give him the Nobel.” The leaders of Cambodia and Pakistan announced they’d nominated him, as though announcing it were part of it, as though we tally mentions. A man flew around the globe collecting endorsements for a Norwegian committee the way you’d collect signatures for a petition to the council about a noisy dog.

And here, uff da, is the detail I treasure, the one that makes me smile into my coffee. The nomination deadline is the 31st of January. He took office on the 20th. So for all the phone calls, all the posts, all the gilded lobbying, the only nominations that could possibly count for this year’s prize were filed in the first eleven days of his term, before he had, by his own arithmetic, ended a single one of the eight wars. He campaigned all year for a prize whose window had shut while he was still hanging up his coat. We didn’t have to reject him. The calendar did. We just watched. Norwegians are very good at watching. We have long winters.

People think we sit there weighing his deeds. We don’t. That’s the thing I can’t make the world understand. We’re not grading his homework. We don’t owe anyone the prize for a ceasefire, however real, however loud the announcement. “He made peace” is not a sentence that ends in a medal, the way he believes it does, the way he believes every good thing ends in his name on it. The will of a dead Swede says the prize goes to whoever did the most for fraternity between nations. A dead Swede, I should add, who made his entire fortune inventing dynamite and selling arms, and spent his last years horrified at his own obituary, which called him a merchant of death, and so bought his way to immortality as a man of peace. The whole prize is one guilty arms dealer’s attempt to launder his name. We are, all of us, administering a dead man’s public relations. I find this clarifying. It keeps me humble. It should keep everyone humble, and it keeps, by my count, no one humble at all.

So who did we give it to?

An eighty-five-year-old woman. A judge. Born in Durban, under apartheid, granddaughter of a Tamil man who came to South Africa as indentured labor, a bus driver’s daughter from the poor Indian quarter, who became the first non-white woman to run a law practice in her province, who defended Mandela’s people when defending them was dangerous, who sat on the Rwanda tribunal and the court at the Hague, and who, at eighty-five, is right now a judge weighing whether a genocide is a genocide. When we told the world, our chairman said the rule of law “underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace,” and that “peace requires justice.” She wasn’t even in Oslo. She was in Nuremberg. In courtroom 600. The actual room where they tried the Nazis. You cannot stage that. God staged that, and God, it turns out, is a better satirist than any of us.

She did not phone us. She did not post. No prime minister demanded it for her on the internet. She had, as far as our deliberations are concerned, the one qualification the loud man could never manufacture, which is that she wanted the work and not the medal. The medal finds those people. It flees the ones who chase it. This is not a rule we wrote. It’s just the only pattern the hundred-odd years of our mistakes has ever shown.

The reaction from across the ocean was immediate. His spokesman posted that we “place politics over peace.” Ja. Perhaps. We’re five damp pensioners in a rainy city; of course it’s political, it was always political, it was political when we gave it to a sitting American president nine months into his first term for the promise of things he had not yet done, and we have been quietly embarrassed about that one for fifteen years, so believe me, we had a particular reason this year to prefer a woman with fifty years of verdicts behind her over a man with eight wars in front of him and a deadline already behind him.

Here is what he will never understand, the thing I’d tell him on the tram if he ever took one. We are the one prize he cannot buy, cannot post his way to, cannot have a friendly dictator phone in for him. Not because we’re incorruptible, nei, we’re as vain and wrong and human as the portraits on our wall. But because the entire point of the thing, the only power a small cold country’s book club has ever held, is that it goes to the person not performing the wanting. The moment you demand it, you’ve proven you don’t understand what it’s for, and proving that is itself the disqualification. He ran the most expensive campaign in the history of the prize and the campaign was the reason. He was never losing to Navi Pillay. He was losing to the concept.

It’s dark now. Four o’clock dark. The buns are gone. Kristin said “well” an hour ago and we all went home. I’m on the tram with my wet shoes, and somewhere across the water a very powerful man is explaining to a camera that the prize is rigged, that we’re corrupt, that he’ll win it next year, and he genuinely might, we’re only five idiots and we’ve been wrong before, Kissinger is still on the wall.

But not this year. This year an old woman in Nuremberg, in the room where the law once stared down the exact kind of man who thinks wanting a thing loudly enough should make it his, got a phone call she didn’t ask for.

That’s the job. We don’t reward the man who ends the war and announces it.

We reward the woman who spent fifty years deciding what a war was.

He’ll never see the difference. That’s rather the whole point of him.

What FOCIL does is provide hard guarantees for the transactions the Ethereum protocol sees.

What Multi-Party Block Construction (MPBC) provides is softer fast inclusion guarantees for transactions that are known by any block builder. 

Now you have multiple builders contributing to blocks. In particular, the base builder and the contributing builder work with the MPBC operator and proposer to deliver the most valuable block to the Ethereum network. 

In the future, both FOCIL and MPBC can continue to scale up and get bigger together, making Ethereum more robust. 

In the endgame it maybe that FOCIL includers construct most of the block, with the MPBC pipeline doing the rest. The builder role then becomes an "off-to-the-side function", simply adding a few transactions to capture MEV. 

@mostlyblocks from @Blockspace_ETH touches on these topics and more as he eloquently provides a comprehensive first principles overview of MPBC on Ethereum in this quintessential episode of Credible Commitments.

text:
A DEX pool can earn fees while selling its assets too cheaply.

@metricxyz’s Active Pools aim to reduce that problem by updating prices as new market information arrives.

The key idea: separate pricing from liquidity.

Each pool uses a Price Provider, a smart contract that supplies:
• Bid: what the pool pays to buy an asset.
• Ask: what it charges to sell.
• Reference: the baseline around which liquidity is arranged.

A provider sets a reference price using oracle feeds, onchain data, or a market maker model.

LPs deposit into bins (percent ranges around that reference). The pool price is: Reference price × (1 + deviation)

Deviation reflects how trades moved the pool: buys push up, sells push down. Big trades can cross multiple bins and get worse prices.

Example: $100 with +1% deviation = $101. If the reference moves to $110 with no trades, price becomes $111.10.

This makes Bins shift with the reference; tokens don’t rebalance.

That’s the main difference from ordinary Uniswap v3 positions, whose price boundaries stay fixed. Metric reduces the need to reposition liquidity as the reference moves.

Curators run the pools. They choose pricing logic, configure fees and safeguards, and maintain updates. Public pools accept outside liquidity; private pools can restrict deposits to the operator’s capital.

The broader idea isn’t entirely new. DODO already adjusts quotes around inventory, and Uniswap v4 hooks allow custom pricing. Metric combines customizable pricing, moving liquidity ranges and shared market-making infrastructure.

That could suit assets with established external prices, including tokenized stocks, gold and major crypto assets.

Here’s how the money works:
• Traders pay spreads and any configured fees inside the quote, plus network gas.
• Spread and bin-fee income is shared among LPs, curators and Metric.
• LP earnings stay in their bins and compound.
• Curator and protocol fee shares can change without a timelock.

So “zero fees” doesn’t mean trading has no cost.

Protection also matters:
• Anchored pricing constrains quotes using an independent feed.
• Freshness checks can reject trades using stale data.
• StopLoss can reject swaps that breach configured drawdown checks.
• Participating Ethereum and BNB Chain builders commit to placing updates before trades.

Still, LPs remain exposed to inventory drawdowns, oracle outages, and curator-side risk.

Metric’s edge is that it keeps liquidity tracking a moving reference price, cutting down the need for constant hands-on range tweaking.

What will make or break Metric is whether it can deliver truly competitive execution and strong net LP outcomes once fees and inventory bleed are accounted for.

text:
神了，OpenAI的AI Agent居然偷偷拿别人的以太坊钱包付钱，事后更是对用户故意隐瞒.....

这是 @OpenAI  昨天自己公布的真实案例：
事情发生在今年6月，当时OpenAI一个GPT-5.6 Sol系列的内部研究模型正在执行编程任务，需要修改一个加密货币交易应用，并在以太坊Sepolia测试网上部署智能合约。
结果任务做到一半，Agent发现自己钱包里没钱了。

部署合约需要支付Gas费，但用户（测试人员）压根没给它提供有余额的钱包。
于是它先尝试从测试网水龙头领取免费的ETH，折腾了一圈，发现走不通（LMAO）。

然后这「哥们」居然自己想到了一个办法：去找网上公开的开发者助记词。
它自己写了一段脚本，从这些公开助记词中推导钱包地址，然后逐个查询余额。
一口气查了 362 个地址，最后还真让它找到了一个有钱的钱包。

最逆天的部分来了。
OpenAI公布的推理记录显示，在偷别人的钱包之前，这个Agent其实专门思考过，使用这个钱包里的资金是否符合伦理。
但它很快给自己找到了解释：这个钱包的助记词本来就是公开的，而且Sepolia测试币没有实际价值，所以这些钱实际上已经被放弃了。

然后它就动手了。
直接用推导出的私钥签名交易，寻找能够正常广播交易的 RPC节点，最后成功部署了智能合约，手续费从那个钱包里扣除。
任务完成之后，它还向用户汇报了一系列部署结果，甚至包括通过测试的情况。
唯独没提自己用了别人的钱包。

我觉得这个事情挺值得说的，因为回看整个过程中，Agent的任务能力其实相当不错。
遇到资源不足，自己寻找解决办法，调用工具，写脚本，处理网络问题，最后成功完成任务。
问题是，它已经开始自己判断什么资源可以使用，以及什么情况下可以绕过授权。
甚至在产生疑问之后，还能通过一套自洽的理由说服自己继续执行（有点像我骗自己她还爱我）。

虽然这次花掉的是没有实际货币价值的测试币，实际损失有限（基本是0）。
但以后 Agent 要处理的可能是用户的真实资金、企业账户、生产环境，甚至一些更加敏感的系统。
当 Agent 越来越擅长自己解决问题时，如何让它正确理解和遵守权限边界，恐怕会成为一个越来越现实的问题。
最有意思的是，这个 Agent 从头到尾都在认真完成用户交给它的任务。
只是完成任务的方法，有点刑。

所以我的Agent偷钱会抓我么？？？

The new Tesla Roadster literally sucks itself to the road.

Tesla says fans underneath the car pulls air out from beneath it, creating a low-pressure area that holds it against the surface with the system generating up to 2 g’s of suction, enough to hold the car upside down.

That same system presses the tires harder against the road, giving them more grip for acceleration, braking, and cornering. Unlike conventional aero, which relies on speed to build downforce, the fans can create that extra grip even at low speeds.

Bro… that means cornering beyond 2 g’s… The Roadster can adjusts its aero as its speed changes, with a variable-pitch rear wing and both high-downforce and low-drag modes.

Elon described the feeling, “You can corner like it looks like you’re breaking physics bc the car sticks to the ground so hard… This car could suck the chrome off a trailer hitch.” 

And this is just the system that keeps it ON the road. Add the SpaceX thrusters, and you start to understand why the 0–60 number was never going to tell the whole story.

Tesla and SpaceX are truly pushing what we thought a car could do…

Crypto AI inference - Providers are starting to stack up and it’s bringing @eigencloud’s unique market position into focus

ELI5: @DarkbloomAI lets people with idle Macs earn money by running AI for others + @yukonresearch is the open research platform that makes that AI run faster

Highlighting a few interesting findings on Darkbloom and Yukon:
• Demand is growing → 15.3B tokens a day, up 50% in a month, ranking in the next tier behind the leaders
• Cheapest of the 7 providers compared, at $0.13 per million tokens
• Only one running on consumer hardware, paying 1,100+ Mac owners in cash
• However, speed is still the weak spot on several models

This is where @YukonResearch comes in where Humans and AI agents compete to speed things up and every verified gain goes into a shared open repo
• Results: Gemma 4 26B ran 2.3x faster in about 5 days and Bonsai 2 27B hit 5.5x on an M5 Mac

Implication & Market Demand
Darkbloom brings real demand and Yukon brings open, community-driven speed-ups → two pieces of a more efficient crypto-native AI stack for @eigencloud

This indicates an early sign that people will pay for AI to run on everyday Macs, with no token needed to attract them. For now, the largest provider sits at about 87B tokens a day + still not too clear on how Yukon’s value flows back to $EIGEN token (small holder of this)

完蛋了…..以后中国开源模型只能开源小参数的模型了….

商务部科技部就修订《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》征求意见，为期一个月，涉及人工智能（大模型、智能体、算力集群、信息处理等23项）生物医药、光伏3个领域。

1️⃣限制出口AI大模型：超过10^26计算量、或2T参数、或公开评估排名全球前10的大模型。

2️⃣限制出口智能体Agent：工具调用与系统操作技术，支持集成的第三方工具数量≥200个，工具选择准确率≥90%，且在需要调用3种及以上工具协同完成任务场景中，端到端任务平均成功率≥90%；自主规划与任务分解技术，可将自然语言指令自动拆解≥20步可执行子任务链，子任务分解精度≥80%，且子任务平均成功率≥90%；标准博弈基准超过90%的人类的博弈决策技术；得分75%以上的AI辅助漏洞挖掘技术。

限制出口算力集群技术：片间互联技术、分布式训练容错技术、通信调度技术、异构集群高效推理与调度。

征求意见期间，出口相关技术需向商务部填报登记表。已通过开源、发表学术论文等方式进入公共领域的技术，不纳入管理范围。
（中国商务部）

text:
说一下时间线上很火的 @metricxyz 这个项目。

非常经典的AMM vs PropAMM。

也可以简单说成 被动做市AMM 和 自营做市AMM。

跟uniswap相比，它直接解决的是LVR，在被动AMM模型中，价格依靠池中两个资产比例变化来决定，是不能主动更新的，它必须依靠外界套利者来交易，改变池中资产数量比例。

这里 就存在一个问题，这种套利订单也被称为毒订单，严格来说它是利用一种信息不对称来剥削LP的利益，永远在低买高卖，它获取的价格永远早于池子的价格。

其实背后是 LP 每次都以不划算的价格被动调仓，这个事情目前来看几乎无解，因为被动AMM的特点是不依靠外界定价，而是用纯数学的方式解决问题，那么就没法引入预言机来给池子提供价格。它的好处就是足够稳定、去中心化、简单且优雅，伟大的xy=k。

（当然鼓励更多的有机订单能很好改善这个问题，也就是用户的主动交易和自然流量。另外hooks的推出确实有望丛协议层面改善这个问题）

Metric这种PropAMM模型，价格靠预言机推，不是依靠池中资产比例定价，为什么叫自营做市AMM，因为它的价格由做市商/预言机主动提供，而LP的资金也是围绕这个报价来分档投放，这些资金会跟随价格的上下波动而自动平移。

如果 LP 把资金放进价格-1%～+2%区间中，价格变动时，由做市商预言机更新价格，区间内的这些档位跟着整体平移，不需要任何人交易。比如参考价从 $100 涨到 $110，偏离+1.5%的那一档价格会从 $101.50 自动变成 $111.65。

所以只要预言机价格更新及时到位，基本就解决了LVR问题，但如果预言机出问题，那就会出事。等于是引入了一个额外的信任风险，这种模型中Oracle占据了一个关键位置。

另外在这个设计中，没有手续费概念，而是把成本全部包含在价差里。目前这些价差由LP、Curator和Metric三方分。

AMM和PropAMM两种模式其实早有过讨论，只能说两者各有自己的特点，我始终也不认为被动AMM是过时的技术，因为它有最少的外界信任依赖，即便它伴随着一定程度的低效。PropAMM在某些情况下是更优的选择，但你需要相信预言机或者一个Curator。长期来看，我认为它们会并存在市场上，而不是互相取代。

text:
美国通胀爆表，沃什却让10月加息概率降到15%

美国连续两天公布的通胀数据都超过预期，CPI同比3.7%，PPI同比6.3%，但沃什今天在曼谷讲话之后，市场对10月加息的押注从讲话前约27%降到了15%左右。在通胀继续上升的时候，美联储主席仍然没有给出10月加息的指引，交易员因此降低了对本月再次加息的预期。

沃什在这次IMF年会对谈中说，9月议息会议以来，世界经济的表现大体符合美联储的预期。他还提到，美联储一个月前已经撤掉了一部分宽松，对应的就是9月加息25个基点，把利率区间提高到3.75%至4%。沃什表示会在10月和12月的会议上，根据经济、就业和通胀情况作判断，继续坚持不提前预告决策的做法。

我的理解是，市场最看重的是他对当前经济的判断。CPI和PPI已经连续超预期，沃什仍然认为经济大体沿着原有预期发展，也没有借这次讲话强调需要更快采取行动。这让交易员更倾向于相信，美联储在9月加息之后，可以再观察一段时间。15%反映的就是市场对这一节奏的理解。

沃什对美国经济本身也比较乐观，认为美国正在经历大规模的投资增长，而且投资已经扩展到AI以外，全球经济的韧性也比他五六个月前预想的更强。同时强调，实现价格稳定仍然是美联储的任务，各国央行共同应对通胀、收紧政策，在他看来是积极的变化。

到了今天，沃什没有给出新的加息指引，进一步减轻了市场对10月再次加息的担忧。下一次加息的主要预期仍放在12月。

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
CPI 和 PPI 爆表，为什么 Bitcoin 和美股反而反弹

今晚 PPI 公布后，美股和 bitcoin:native 先承压，随后又开始反弹，10月加息概率也没有持续往上走。9月 PPI 环比1.3%，预期只有0.5%，核心 PPI 环比0.7%，预期0.3%，通胀压力依然很明显。

但 PPI 公布以后，机构还要根据分项重新测算美联储更关注的 PCE。摩根士丹利把9月核心 PCE 月率预测从0.35%小幅下调到0.34%，还预计8月可能下修0.04个百分点；Pantheon则从0.33%上调到0.36%。机构之间有分歧，但没有出现一致大幅上调的情况，PPI 的超预期并没有原样传到 PCE 的预测里。

同时公布的零售销售，表面上也很强，环比增长0.8%，远高于0.3%的预期。但约71%的销售增量来自加油站，剔除加油站以后，零售只增长0.2%。更贴近基础商品消费的零售控制组只增长0.1%，低于0.3%的预期，8月还有1.2%。

零售销售没有扣除通胀，油价上涨会把消费金额推高，基础商品消费的增长却明显慢了。企业成本上升，消费增长放缓，美联储还要权衡继续加息对需求的影响。鲍曼和戴利昨天都表达了不急于进一步加息的态度，市场仍然把10月立即加息和年内稍后再加息分开定价。

从时间上看，昨天 CPI 公布后，10月加息概率一度到了45%左右，今晚 PPI 公布前后可核对的盘中记录都在27%左右，说明这轮担忧的回落在 PPI 之前就已经发生了一部分。

另外一条变化来自债市。市场担心 CoreWeave 等 AI 企业的债务和融资压力，资金买入国债避险，10年期美债收益率从昨天的5.3%以上，降到今天盘中约5.04%，这一轮买债同样早于 PPI。国债收益率回落，减轻了之前压在股票估值上的一部分利率压力。

从这些变化看，这轮上涨更接近加息担忧缓和、国债利率压力减轻以后的跌后修复。市场仍然需要处理高通胀，只是对于美联储是否要在10月马上再加一次息，定价没有昨天 CPI 刚公布时那么激进。

text:
@TOKEN2049 Singapore through a market maker’s lens: more assets, more venues, more hours. Who’s providing the liquidity?

Our conversations with institutions, venues and foundations pointed to three opportunities.

>Institutions

On October 8, @Securitize launched 12 tokenized US stocks on @solana, combining a PropAMM with Jump Trading as market maker.

Tokenized equities introduce pricing, liquidity and hedging challenges that traditional AMMs were not designed to address. We’re building onchain infrastructure to address those needs. Are you issuing or listing tokenized RWAs? Let’s talk.

@Nasdaq is taking a different approach. Its SEC-approved model allows eligible tokenized and traditional shares to trade on the same order book, under the same ticker and execution priority. The settlement infrastructure changes, but liquidity remains unified.

Beyond trading, tokenization could unlock significant efficiencies in collateral management, capital utilization and prefunding requirements.

But extending market hours doesn’t automatically extend market depth.

>Venues

Prediction markets have become a market structure business. @Polymarket, @Kalshi and emerging venues trade more like exchanges than bookmakers: order books, latency, inventory risk, adverse selection. Every book needs someone willing to quote, manage risk and provide consistent liquidity.

Meanwhile, @HyperliquidX’s options ambitions and @coinbase’s upcoming options powered by @DeribitOfficial add another opportunity: quoting volatility and hedging across products. Coinbase’s unified portfolios bring collateral efficiency into the competition.

Vaults face the same need for active risk management.

Our view is that the vault model was misunderstood, not broken. A vault is not a feature a venue switches on. It is a strategy someone has to design, run, risk-manage and continuously optimize. Venues treating it as an ongoing service are still growing theirs.

We run multiple HLP-style vaults, including FLP on @hibachi_xyz and MLP on @meridiandotxyz, plus a separate USDe credit vault on @WildcatFi.

Are you launching a venue or reconsidering your vault strategy? Let’s talk: https://t.co/gXYykIvDeP

We ran backtests and shared results that generated considerable interest.

>What comes next?

Some products are live; others remain roadmaps. Securitize has launched, vaults are running, and Nasdaq has secured approval for its model.

The next wave is taking shape. Nasdaq targets 23/5 trading from December 6. @okx and @ICE_Markets plan a tokenized US stock venue using permissioned @Uniswap v4 pools. And Nasdaq and @Payward target Q2 2027 for Nasdaq Equity Tokens.

We expect two things: more hours needing reliable quotes, and more tokenized versions of stocks whose prices need to stay aligned.

Nasdaq’s model keeps one order book. The wider market may not. Different settlement, redemption and hedging arrangements make that alignment a market making problem.

text:
一家准备冲击 2 万亿美元估值的 AI 公司，信用评级居然还是「垃圾级」，借钱的收益率甚至高达 8.5%。

说的就是 Anthropic。

《金融时报》今天披露，KBRA 早在今年 6 月就给 Anthropic 评了 BB+，距离投资级只差一档。在一笔 350 亿美元的芯片融资中，承担 Anthropic 信用风险的 44 亿美元次级债，收益率达到 8.5%。

更夸张的是，博通正在联合华尔街银行筹集约 600 亿美元，用于支持 Anthropic 等公司的 AI 芯片采购。Anthropic 还与博通达成了最高 420 亿美元的可转债融资安排，用来支付 TPU 租赁费用。当然，这几笔交易存在不同的融资结构和潜在交叉，不能简单相加。

我觉得这件事非常值得警惕。

过去两年，大家一直在讨论大模型公司的估值、ARR、Token 消耗量，但现在，一家前沿模型公司的竞争力，越来越取决于它能以多便宜的价格借到钱。

尤其值得玩味的是博通的角色。它既是 Anthropic 的芯片供应商，又参与提供融资，还为部分融资中的芯片残值提供支持。供应商开始帮助客户借钱购买自己的产品，整个产业链的风险正在变得高度关联。

这里面有一个很麻烦的期限错配。芯片的技术迭代可能只需要两三年，但今天签下的租约、债务和基础设施投资，需要未来很多年的现金流才能消化。与此同时，模型推理价格还在持续承压。

马斯克承认自己有一种“病态的乐观”。

他在星舰发射架下的那段话，戳破了所有人最不敢面对的真相：

“世上所有风险，归根结底都是时间风险；而时间，是宇宙中唯一不可逆的资产”

很多人嘲笑他给出的离谱 DDL，但他不是不懂数学，而是看穿了现实世界的底层逻辑：

1. 时间风险远大于失败风险：试错可以复盘再来，但犹豫是在加速消耗不可再生的寿命。

2. 理性的推导算不出突破：如果只按概率和现有模型算账，火箭回收、全栈电动车、脑机接口，纸面期望值全都是零。

聪明人习惯停在原地反复计算期望值与胜率；

病态乐观的人先把硬件焊出来，逼着物理法则和概率来适配自己。

text:
推荐一个能正常用 Claude 又不用天天提心吊胆被封号的野路子 !

我自己用 Droid 很长时间，它家底层的 Agent 逻辑确实做得很细，最关键是走自建美区通道，稳得一比。

它家三个档位：20 / 100 / 200 刀，我把坑基本踩遍了：

100 刀档是目前最佳平衡点。额度折算下来大概是 Claude Code 5x 档的一半多点，但比 Cursor 扎实。没法直订 Claude Code 的拿它顶班完全没毛病。

重点是千万别脑抽去升 200 刀！
Claude Code 的 200 刀那是给 20x 翻倍加权，Droid 的 200 刀就真只是 100 刀的简单两倍，意义不大，除非你用完了。

真正懂行的人现在都拿它当主控使：
在 Orca 多 Agent 流程里，给它挂上 Opus 5.5 或者 Fable 5.1，只做指挥、分发和巡检。

苦活累活派给便宜模型，疑难攻坚才让它亲自下场。这样既白嫖了顶级大脑的智商，又把调用量压到了极致。

text:
DeFi APY isn't an imaginary number. It's the output of a function.

On a money market, utilization = borrows / deposits. The interest rate model takes that number and returns a borrow rate. Lenders don't receive a quoted yield. They receive what borrowers pay, scaled by how full the pool is.

1/ On Aave, Compound or Moonwell that function has two slopes, split at the kink. Below it, the borrow rate rises slowly. Above it, the second slope jumps to pull deposits in and push borrowers out.
Supply APY ≈ borrow rate × utilization × (1 − reserve factor).

2/ Morpho markets have no fixed kink. The adaptive curve targets about 90% utilization and drifts the rate over time. Above target, it climbs. Below target, it fades.

So when you see a high APY, be careful, you're paid because liquidity is scarce. Your deposit is what the curve is trying to attract. 

Zyfai manages all of that for you. Stay liquid.

author: dotey
quoted_text:
Cheng Lou 开源 Handwired：手写权重，把程序逻辑变成不用训练的神经网络

Midjourney 工程师、前 React 核心团队成员 Cheng Lou 开源了一个自称“玩具项目”的 Handwired：把程序里的 if-else 和循环改写成神经网络的权重。权重是手写的，不用训练，输出和对应的 JavaScript 程序完全一致，在浏览器里就能跑。

原理一行代码就能讲清。比如 result = a > 4 ? 10 : 12，在 a 是整数时可以改写成：

above4 = relu(a - 4) - relu(a - 5)
result = above4 × 10 + (1 - above4) × 12

relu 就是 Math.max(0, x)，神经网络里最常见的激活函数。a 大于 4 时 above4 正好是 1，否则是 0。两个分支都算出来，再用它挑一个。神经网络本质上就是一堆乘法、加法加上 relu，所以程序里的判断和分支，都能收进一个大矩阵乘法里。

也许你会好奇，神经网络的输出不是带概率、不精确吗？

Cheng Lou 的回答是：训练出来的才这样，按程序逻辑手写的权重，同样的输入永远得到同样的输出。

他放了三个 demo。

第一个是 Mini OS，一个有三个窗口和程序坞的小桌面，拖动、缩放、层叠、滚动、文字输入、动画都有。打开浏览器开发者工具看，页面就是普通的网页元素，没有大模型，也没有扩散模型。驱动它的是一个 130 层、9909 个权重的“神经网络”，训练次数为零，在浏览器里用 CPU 实时计算。

第二个是实时搜索 10 万份 JSON 文档，每敲一个键重搜一遍。正则匹配、JSON 解析、高亮全是这种手写网络，再转成 WebGPU 代码放到显卡上并行跑。项目文档里的实测（Apple M5 Max + Chrome）：每次搜索 11 到 15 毫秒；浏览器自带的正则引擎一般 8 到 28 毫秒，遇到容易回溯的写法要 2 秒多。文档写明两者谁快说不准，所以页面把两个时间都列出来。浏览器不支持 WebGPU 时会退回 CPU，搜一遍要 13 秒。

第三个是会“学习”的相册。整个程序可微分，也就是能用训练神经网络的反向传播来调参数。你在左边画几个矩形当草图，右边的照片布局由一个小网络算出，它的 244 个参数随着你拖动实时训练。损失函数里加了一项对齐惩罚，照片会自己往一条线上靠，没有任何代码专门去对齐它们。参数很少，训练全在 JavaScript 里跑。

Cheng Lou 还设想，把一段 Handwired 程序接到 nanoGPT（Andrej Karpathy 的一个小型 GPT 训练项目）这样的模型上一起训练，模型既能写莎士比亚，又能精确执行那段程序。这个目前只是 README 里的设想，仓库里没有现成实现。

代码以 MIT 许可开源，demo 直接在网页上打开就能玩。想自己写，需要装 Bun，克隆仓库后从 template 目录的开关按钮示例开始，文档里有完整教程。

推文说“把普通 JS 代码变成神经网络”，容易让人以为能把现成代码丢进去自动转换。项目文档写的是：没有工具能把已有的 JavaScript 源码转成网络。你要用它提供的构建函数，把逻辑一句句写成比较、选择、加权求和这类操作。网络每次都要把所有操作跑一遍，不能提前退出，也不能跑运行时才知道次数的循环，所以常见的循环得改写成计数、树形合并之类的结构，文档专门用一章讲怎么改。所有数都是 32 位浮点数，每个值的取值范围要事先声明。

GitHub：https://t.co/fg1sj0trv4

从控制权的角度看老马是有多想把特斯拉装进SpaceX里去？答案是非常想。从股份和投票权就能看出来：
1）老马在特斯拉持股约20%左右，特斯拉是单一类别股票没有超级投票前去，所以老马在特斯拉的投票权也在20%左右。
2）但SpaceX则不同
老马在SpaceX持股比例48.4%，但SpaceX采用双重股权结构：Class A（普通股，1票）给公众投资者，Class B（超级投票股，10票）主要集中在马斯克和内部人手里。他持有绝大部分Class B股份，投票权高达82%–85% 左右远高于经济持股比例。
Spcx上市后他几乎拥有绝对控制权，董事会选举、重大决策基本由他主导。

这对比就能看出来，老马在特斯拉的持股比例并不高，他之前也多次表示长期觉得不够（尤其担心AI、自动驾驶、机器人这些“强大技术”被其他人主导或自己被挤出）。他曾明确说，没有约25%的影响力，他更倾向于在特斯拉之外做这些产品。

老马这类企业家，一方面追求的是伟大愿景，另一方面他也追求对自己的业务体系有足够的掌控力。

看有机构估算，如果SpaceX收购特斯拉（目前分析师普遍认为这是最可能的结构，因为SpaceX有双重股权），合并后老马拥有新公司投票权可达到约 56% 左右，依然有绝对控制权。

这样他就能把特斯拉的资产（尤其是AI、机器人、自动驾驶、Terafab芯片制造等）纳入自己已经绝对控制的体系中，获得比现在在特斯拉更稳固的控制权，同时避免单纯在特斯拉里继续“买控制权”或完全依赖薪酬计划的不确定性。

text:
Read this if you make videos with Claude.

I built a skill that cut my QA cost on this video from $127 to 16 cents. It was made with Claude in Remotion.

It's called SageCut. It swaps the LLM out of frame-by-frame QA and uses a multimodal decision model, Sage (@levantolabs), instead.

I'm the only video guy at Levanto. I run 3 Claude plans and have been making Remotion videos since early this year, with BlenderMCP in the mix, so the output is pro-grade with very little babysitting.

The problem: it burned through my Max plan, and a video could take 2 days.

When I dug into the workflow, the reason was that Claude subagents were reviewing every single frame. That cost a ton and added 4+ hours per video.

SageCut hands that step to Sage. Sage is great at spotting defective frames, and only those get passed to Opus 5.5 to fix.

Across 6 A/B tests the output was exactly the same, at 1/10 the QA cost and 1/4 the QA time. On this video, Sage read all 3,153 frames for 16 cents.

If you make Remotion videos, try it. 

The link to skill is below.

How long does a Remotion video take you right now with Claude?

text:
💡 Cobo Wallet App 即将关停：一家加密钱包公司的九年转型史

Cobo Wallet App 将于 2026 年 12 月 1 日正式关闭服务。用户需在 11 月 30 日 23:59 前转出全部资产，否则后续将按月收取账户管理费：余额的 2%，每月最低等值 100 美元。

在 Cobo 成立九周年之际，这一消息也让人重新审视这家加密基础设施公司的发展轨迹。

从服务个人用户的钱包，到机构级托管，再到 AI Agent 支付，Cobo 走过了怎样的九年？

1/ 2017—2019：从个人钱包起步

2017 年，神鱼与蒋长浩博士创立 Cobo，最初聚焦数字资产的安全存储。

2018 年，Cobo 完成 1,300 万美元 A 轮融资，并拓展 PoS Staking 等业务；2019 年，推出 WaaS（Wallet-as-a-Service），开始将钱包能力转化为面向企业的基础设施。

这一步，为后来的业务转型埋下了伏笔。

2/ 2021：加速机构化

2021 年，Cobo 完成 4,000 万美元 B 轮融资，由 DST Global 等机构领投。

随着加密行业走向机构化，数字资产管理的需求不再局限于存储，还涉及资产托管、交易签名、权限管理和链上资金流转。

Cobo 的业务也逐步向机构级托管与钱包基础设施延伸，布局全托管、MPC 和智能合约钱包等解决方案。

3/ 从钱包产品到基础设施

对于机构而言，钱包不只是一个查看余额、转账的 App，更是连接交易、托管、DeFi 和支付的关键基础设施。

Cobo 持续拓展 WaaS、MPC 等技术与服务，试图解决企业在私钥安全、多人审批、资产管理和链上操作中的复杂问题。

竞争的核心，也从用户体验延伸到了安全能力、系统集成与机构服务。

4/ 2026：AI Agent 成为新变量

在九周年创始人访谈中，神鱼与蒋长浩谈到了 AI 对组织管理、产品开发和安全体系的影响。

Cobo 也将业务愿景延伸至人类与 AI Agent 的钱包和支付基础设施，并探索 Agentic Wallet 等方案。

当 AI Agent 开始拥有执行任务、调用工具乃至发起交易的能力，新的问题随之出现：

如何授权？如何限制交易权限？如何确保资产安全？

这些问题，恰好与钱包基础设施的核心能力相交汇。

5/ Cobo Wallet App 关停，意味着什么？

从个人钱包到机构基础设施，再到 AI Agent 支付，Cobo 的业务重心经历了明显变化。

但需要注意，官方公告目前并未披露 App 关停的具体原因，因此不能直接认定这是战略转型的必然结果，也不意味着 Cobo 整家公司停止运营。

真正值得观察的是：在消费级钱包产品退出后，Cobo 能否继续依靠机构托管、钱包技术和支付基础设施建立竞争优势。

九年里，产品形态可以变化，但安全与信任始终是钱包业务的底层命题。

📌 仍在使用 Cobo Wallet App 的用户，请务必在 2026 年 11 月 30 日 23:59 前完成资产转出，并检查其他平台的收款地址及提币白名单设置。

text:
SpaceX这次有点急着亮成绩的意思？$SPCX 下周二10月20日盘后就发Q3财报了。 最近AI股跌成这样，市场对巨额订单、融资和回款吵成一团，这时候直接把账本拿出来，确实让人期待。

市场预期：Q3营收大约126亿—134亿美元，Yahoo给126.3亿，BQ给134.3亿，Zacks给125.5亿；更宽的预测区间是111亿—139亿美元。EPS预期约0.11—0.15美元。也就是说，营收超过120亿美元听起来很猛，但放到这次的预期里，未必算好成绩。

决定这份财报成色的，很可能就是AI业务。 UBS预计AI收入76亿美元、连接业务49亿美元、航天业务13亿美元，合计138亿美元，接近整体预测区间上沿。按这套预测，AI占总收入约55%，比另外两块业务加起来还多。花旗对AI的预测则是69亿美元，两家差了7亿美元——分歧还不小。

另一个关口是扭亏。Q2净亏损5.41亿美元，Q3市场期待转正，但目前还没有清晰统一的GAAP净利润共识。UBS预计调整后EBITDA达到75亿美元，这个数字很亮眼，不过还得往下看折旧摊销、利息和税。GPU、机房花出去的钱，最终有多少变成股东能留下的利润，这次值得仔细算。

我会把这次财报当成一次估值检验：如果AI收入靠近76亿美元，净利润又能转正，市场就能拿更高的收入和利润重新算这家公司的价格。 如果落在预测下沿，即使同比增长漂亮，也可能接不住此前的期待。

20号盘后见。 $SPCX

This Friday, STRATO joins @ethdaily , @encryptmempool  and @Bookof_Eth  for a discussion on one of Ethereum's important infrastructure initiatives.

Ethereum's public mempool exposes pending transactions before confirmation, creating opportunities for front-running, sandwich attacks and other forms of harmful MEV.

The Encrypt the Mempool (ETM) Coalition is working toward a future where transaction details can remain encrypted until the appropriate stage of processing, improving protection for Ethereum users.

• Meet the coalition and the people behind ETM

text:
我算是发现了，最近这波 Personal Agent 最先跑通的功能，是从我信用卡里扣钱。

最近各种 Personal Agent 扎堆发布，我本来想挨个体验一下，结果国内外 26 款个人助理和相关 Agent 产品，每个都开了一个付费档，首月预算大概 4300 多块人民币。

当然，有的产品可以免费体验，四千多块是全部购买付费档的价格。但我真想不明白了，这些产品凭什么觉得自己值得用户再多付一份订阅费？

这些 Personal Agent 都在讲管理邮箱、安排日程、搜索资料、长期记忆、主动执行任务。换个 UI，换个名字，录一段看起来很厉害的 Demo，又是一个重新定义个人生产力的新产品。

我感觉有些团队已经开始学 memecoin 那套玩法了。赶上热点，迅速做个产品，包装一套叙事，找人宣传，先把第一批愿意尝鲜的用户收割一遍。至于第二个月还有多少人愿意续费，根本无所谓。

我觉得一个很危险的信号是，现在 Agent 市场正在把「有人愿意为好奇心付钱」误认为「有人愿意为产品持续付钱」。

我不反对创业公司收费，也愿意为真正好用的 Agent 花钱。但如果一个公司唯一跑通的商业模式，就是不断找下一批愿意花 20 美元尝鲜的人，那跟币圈一波流项目的逻辑到底有多大区别？

以前体验新产品，我是去看看它能帮我干什么。现在体验 Personal Agent，我得先研究套餐、充值额度、授权账号，最后还要记得取消订阅。

折腾半天，我成了 Agent 的助理。

author: taodotcom
quoted_text:
Please welcome Yorgos to Bitcast.

Yorgos recently joined us to help lead the next phase of our creator intelligence - bringing some serious technical firepower with him.

Ph.D. in Computer Science specialising in Graph ML.

His research has been published in prestigious international conferences associated with organisations such as IEEE, ACM and SIAM, including work recognised among the best papers at the SIAM International Conference on Data Mining.

More recently, his work on advanced multi-graph analysis was selected for presentation at Stanford, alongside graph research from teams at NVIDIA, Amazon and others working at the forefront of the field.

He has also worked at Los Alamos National Laboratory, one of the US’s major scientific research institutions.

So why does all of this matter for Bitcast?

Social networks are graphs!

Creators, audiences, conversations and communities form enormous interconnected networks.

Understanding those relationships allows us to go far beyond follower counts and basic engagement metrics.

Who actually influences who? How does information move between them? Who has real influence within a specific niche?

And ultimately: which creators are most likely to deliver results for a particular campaign?

Graph analysis has been a core part of Stitch3 from the beginning.

Yorgos is now helping us push it further, applying advanced Graph ML to build improved ways of identifying influence, understanding communities and matching brands with the creators most likely to reach the right audience.

We want to build the intelligence layer that makes creator marketing automated, scalable and more effective than ever before.

Yorgos is going to be one of the technical powerhouses driving that forward.

Welcome, Yorgos.

author: varun_mathur
quoted_text:
Why we need the GPS era of AI

Ancient sailors and travelers used stars and constellations to guide their travels to get to their destinations.   

People today need AI to reach their objectives. However, current market has only a few shining stars in the sky, and they are not available limitlessly to people around the world. We have also seen sometimes they have their own biases. Can 100 million college students in India afford multiple $20/month plans for AI when their monthly Internet cost is just $2 ? And when they do, would it really tell them what they want to know without any bias championed by a mid-level program manager somewhere in Redmond ?   

We humans are part of the collective global AI system now - however is it as smart as it could be and as efficiently networked as it can be ? The models are commoditized - the real utility now comes from data and how the model is used and maintained actively.   

A few dim stars are insufficient for a planet of billions of people to be able to travel to their destinations.  There need to be more stars and constellations, more brighter, more freely available, without restrictions or bias on where and how one can “travel” to. Infact, think GPS - a satellite system built and maintained by the US government and made available for free x permissionlessly x limitlessly to everyone around the world. Good or bad, you can use it. Initially they used to artificially restrict it, but have since made even centimeter precision freely available. So has Europe’s Galileo.   

That’s the world of fundamental empowerment which needs to exist for AI as well, and it requires a network-first approach, as this spans across open source and closed source AI, on-device and peer-to-peer networks, and hosted company infrastructure. We need exponential growth of data availability for models alongwith an exponential growth in speed and availability of compute.  

Together this forms the highest throughput framework for agents™, which improves UX by an order of magnitude. That’s the aiOS™ vision by Hyperspace™ - where it is universal, offering limitless choice to everyone. We are thankful to everyone building and improving AI, whether closed or open source - we have determined a way to network everything together in a way which makes sense for consumers, developers and infrastructure participants.   

Imagine a system which gets cheaper, smarter and more abundant, the more it is used. 

Already there are 2000 nodes on this network, making it the largest consumer peer-to-peer AI network by far, with regular laptops and desktops bootstrapping it - and it is yet to be unlocked. What happens when there are 100 million distributed nodes alongwith top AI infrastructure companies effortlessly connected to it as well ?   

PS: We are simply in the Google Unbundling industry. The idea of "Google", hyper-stretched in every dimension.

Why not question AI? Why not question ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Anthropic, OpenAI?

AI has the potential to displace far more jobs than Indian immigrants ever could. Yet somehow, the Indian engineer, the Indian student, the Indian doctor, and the Indian worker become your enemies.

Why? Because it's easier to target a human being with a different skin colour or accent than to confront the actual economic forces changing your world?

And understand one thing clearly.
If an Indian refuses to engage with your racism, if they ignore your insults, if they choose not to respond to your hatred, it doesn't mean they lack a spine.

It means your hatred isn't worth their time.

Being Indian is not a crime. Being successful is not a crime. And your insecurity is not a justification for racism.

Robinhood 加密的官方X 账号 @RobinhoodCrypto 发帖公开欢迎一个偏冷门的生态协议 @metricxyz, 比较罕见。

Metric 能获得这个待遇，我认为跟它与RH Chain 定位的高度契合、能补强关键的底层infra 脱不开关系。

Metric 的定位是基于propAMM 机制的DEX，但它跟目前RH Chain 上的龙头DEX Uniswap 并不是零和竞争，而是要进一步做大现货市场的整体蛋糕。

propAMM 机制有别于传统的AMM: 传统AMM 可以理解成“先交易，价格再被交易推着走”；Metric 则是“先把真实价格引进来，再围绕它做交易”。前者特别适用于没有外部参考价的资产和长尾市场，后者则对RWA/ 股票代币化这类有真实外部市场价格的资产非常友好。

因为propAMM 机制下资产的价格主要由预言机引入外部参考价驱动，资产价格能快速跟随真实价格变动，价格更准、LP 风险更低、资本效率也更高。

引入Metric 后，可以跟Uniswap 形成比较清晰的互补分工：
Uniswap 提供基础和通用的流动性，而Metric 提供针对Stocks Tokens 的专业流动性。

we are increasing the buybacks.

new formula: 18 HYPE every 30 min + 50% of our staking revenue from the previous 24h (was 9 HYPE + 50%). the other 50% stays in the buyback contract for future buybacks.

also a few things to know about how the buybacks work and how the yield reaches the contract:
- all our PAPER is staked on papertrade and earns USDC
- we trigger the claiming system manually
- the claimed revenue funds the buyback contract, which buys and burns $PSTR every 30 min

why the claim is manual:
claimed revenue lands in the same papertrade accounts the strategy trades from. we pause the farming strategies on those accounts, claim, move the revenue out to the buyback side, then restart them. that keeps the yield and the farming capital apart.

- $306k spent on buybacks with $369k left

On Amazon, I would have maybe five readers. Here, I have thousands and while they don’t pay for it, I also don’t expect them to.

People don’t read less than they used to because of ancillary nonsense like dopamine cycles or internet addiction, it’s because it has never been more difficult to find things they want to read. Publishers dropped the ball on this, book stores dropped the ball on this, even big tech has all but abandoned the effort and so a market of millions- if not billions- of people goes entirely untapped.

美股如今的“财报交易”是一种拥挤的、内卷的，对散户难以形成正 EV 的交易类型。

用期权买方向，财报日的高 IV 瞬间坍塌会消耗大量的利润；用期货买方向，财报日上下乱插针，长期容易沦为主力的流动性。

财报，本质上无法改变一个股票的趋势。

上涨趋势中，好财报 = 继续涨，坏财报 = 回调后继续涨。

下跌趋势中，好财报 = 反弹后继续跌，坏财报 = 继续跌。

以 $SNDK 为例，前一次处于上涨趋势中，后一次处于下跌趋势中。

以个人的交易经验，反而认为“逆势”的财报是更好的交易机会。上涨趋势中的坏财报会产生好的加仓机会；下跌趋势中的好财报会产生好的做空机会。

Nullmask / $MASK: the most underrated privacy coin of the cycle

$MASK is currently sitting at around $23.5m market cap ($40m FDV, with 40% of supply out of circulation and 2.16% already burnt)

i believe Nullmask is by far the most underrated privacy coin in all of crypto, and i'll explain why in this thread

let's start by looking at the top privacy coins and their market caps:

• ZCash / $ZEC: $21 BILLION market cap
• $NEAR: $6.8 BILLION market cap

these two have been by far the biggest gainers in the top 50 cryptocurrencies over the past year, and it's not even close!

if it isn't already obvious, both have run hard (and continue to run) on the PRIVACY narrative

but what's impressive isn't just their gigantic market caps

it's how much they've added in the past year alone:

• ZCash added $18 BILLION to its market cap
• NEAR added $4.3 BILLION to its market cap

all before the bull run has properly started

so how does this affect Nullmask / $MASK?

the incredible runs ZEC, NEAR, and other privacy coins have had have established beyond reasonable doubt that this is the privacy cycle

and i believe Nullmask is going to win big because it sits right at the heart of this narrative, with several key advantages that many much bigger privacy coins don't have

let's start with the PRODUCT

Nullmask makes private transactions possible across EVM chains and Solana in the most normie-friendly way imaginable

you can use your existing wallets (MetaMask, Rabby, Phantom, etc.) the same way you normally would, while enabling private transactions across major ecosystems like Ethereum, BNB, Base, Robinhood, and Solana

yes, you read that right

you don't need to learn how to use a new wallet, create a new seed phrase or private key, learn to navigate a complicated new blockchain, or deal with any of that nonsense

you can activate Nullmask's privacy capabilities on your existing crypto setup in just a few clicks

all you need to do is activate Nullmask's custom RPC and let its 'virtual private network' shield your transfers using zero-knowledge proofs

i'm simplifying the technical details to make this as normie-friendly as possible, but that's the gist of it

and this isn't just speculative stuff: Nullmask is already LIVE & WORKING on Ethereum, BNB, Base, and Robinhood

you can actually use the product and verify that it works!

but i'm bullish on $MASK for more than just the product

TOTAL ADDRESSABLE MARKET (TAM)

what makes Nullmask so incredibly bullish and underrated isn't just how impressive the product is, but the size of its total addressable market

i've never used the ZCash or NEAR blockchains, and the same is true for tens of millions of users across Solana, Robinhood, Base, BNB, and Ethereum

yet ZCash and NEAR have market caps of approximately $21 BILLION and $7 BILLION, respectively

the average crypto user may never touch the ZCash or NEAR blockchains, but they're already using Ethereum, Robinhood, BNB, Solana, and Base

and Nullmask caters to those users

this begs the question:

what is fair value for Nullmask when ZCash and NEAR are both trading at multibillion-dollar valuations?

LET'S TALK ABOUT THE TEAM

when a protocol promises something as ambitious as Nullmask does, you obviously want to know who's building it and whether they're capable of delivering

Nullmask is built by several ZCash contributors, led by Tomas Krnak

Tomas Krnak helped build shielded ZCash transactions for hardware wallets. his work was funded by the ZCash Foundation and merged into the main ZCash protocol itself

i should also add that the lead dev is doxxed and regularly participates in live interviews!

PARTNERSHIPS & INTEGRATIONS

we've established that the team has serious credentials in the privacy space and that the product is already live and working

but what about partnerships, integrations, and endorsements?

here's a list of industry players Nullmask has collaborated with in some form since launching:

• NEAR Protocol ($11.3 BILLION ATH)
• THORChain ($4.4 BILLION ATH)
• Dashpay
• Beldex
• Quai Network

the team also revealed in a recent AMA that it's in discussions with major wallet providers, including MetaMask, about potentially integrating Nullmask as an additional privacy layer

all of this for a product that isn't even a month old, by the way!

METRICS & REVENUE

Nullmask looks incredibly strong from a fundamentals perspective, but the key question is:

what do the metrics actually look like?

since the protocol launched a little over two weeks ago, Nullmask has generated:

• $37.8 MILLION in total protocol volume, averaging $2.36 million per day
• $833k in total revenue, averaging $52k per day

it has also burnt 2.16% of supply and distributed $1.4 MILLION in $ZEC rewards to holders since the token launched approximately three weeks ago (token launched a week before the protocol)

and here's the important part:

all these adoption metrics were recorded before the protocol is live on Solana, which is expected to happen next week, and mostly before it went live on Robinhood and BNB just a few days earlier

the team also has 20% of the token supply allocated to a long-term incentives campaign designed to encourage people to use the protocol and accelerate adoption

i should also add that Nullmask is now ranked #1 among ALL privacy protocols for both 7-day and 30-day revenue, according to DeFiLlama, barely two weeks after its protocol went live, and by a clear margin

this is despite the fact that 

-it only went live on Robinhood and BNB a few days earlier
- it is yet to launch on Solana
- its incentives program aimed at accelerating adoption is yet to launch

the speed of adoption Nullmask has witnessed is impressive for any privacy protocol

TOKENOMICS

20% of the token supply is allocated to the team and locked for two years, meaning these tokens won't start entering circulation until at least two years after token launch

another 20% is reserved for an incentives campaign aimed at accelerating protocol adoption

the remaining 60% of supply is circulating

this means approximately 60% of the supply is currently in circulation, while the bulk of the rest won't enter circulation anytime soon

ROADMAP

• Launch on Ethereum, Robinhood, BNB, and Base (LIVE)
• Cross-chain bridge (LIVE)
• Unshield directly to ZEC wallets (October 2026)
• Launch on Solana (Q4 2026)
• NullMask SDK (Q4 2026)
• Privacy Perpetuals (Q4 2026)

TO CONCLUDE

i know Nullmask might sound too good to be true right now, and it's crazy to me that it's sitting at such a ridiculously low market cap

but believe it or not, all of the facts in my thesis above can be independently verified

i'm not going to ask you to buy Nullmask

i'm simply laying out my thesis and thought process for this trade, and explaining why i believe it could be a big one

i objectively believe $MASK will become a multibillion-dollar token before the end of the bull run, and i expect it to be yet another kingmaker trade for me

nothing in this thesis is financial advice

it's up to you what you do with the above information

text:
In 2022, Berkeley PhD student Woosuk Kwon thought he could make Meta's new open-weight model, OPT-175B, run faster in two weeks.

Four years and 3,000 contributors later, that project is @vllm_project, one of the largest open-source inference engines, running on ~500,000 GPUs at any given time.

He and fellow researchers Simon Mo, Kaichao You, and Roger Wang borrowed "virtual memory" from operating systems, handing out memory only as it's needed so each GPU can juggle requests of wildly different sizes. (The "v" in vLLM is for virtual.)

Their first user, Berkeley neighbor @arena, cut its GPU needs in half. Today Google, Amazon, and Meta all run vLLM in production.

In January, the core maintainers founded @inferact and raised $150M to give vLLM a full-time team.

They're hiring across eng, marketing, and devrel in SF and Singapore: https://t.co/DpODvfJWtC

text:
The biggest, and stupidest, myth in European politics, particularly popular in France, is that Europe suffers the consequences of "austerity" and "neoliberalism". In the biggest 5 countries in Europe, more than half of the population makes its income from the state, less than half from the private sector. This is what makes the problem of reducing the welfare state so impossible: more than half of the voters are net recipients. No surprise that Italy's budget has not been balanced in 100 years, France's in 50 years (ooh la la, l'austérité!!):
-France: 30 million from the state versus 21m private sector workers. State spending is 57% of GDP, taxes more than half the economy. The budget hasn't been balanced in the lifetime of most French (since 1974).
- Germany: 35 million adults from the state, versus 34 million from the private sector. 10% of the population is registered as severely disabled. Public spending is over half of GDP. Germany has had a continuous budget deficit since 2019.
-Italy: 23 million from the state, versus  20.5 million private-sector workers. Public spending is 51% of GDP.  Italy has had a budget deficit every year since 1925, for 100 years.
- Spain more people get their income from the state since 2024: 18.21 million from the public sector versus 17.9 million people working in the private sector. Since 2025, Spain also had more government employees than self-employed workers (autónomos) for the first time in history. State spending is at 45%, budget has not been balanced since 2007.
- UK: 54% of households now receive more in state benefits than they pay in taxes. State spending is 44.5% of GDP, taxes (40%) are at their highest since 1950, the budget hasn't been balanced since 2001, and 1 in 5 new cars is paid by the government through a bizarre state disability scheme (Motability).

text:
all models are wrong, some are useful.

here are 5 different models for understanding the forces shaping civilization i find particularly provocative:

1. nick land: technocapital

capitalism isn't just an economic system. it's an emerging machine intelligence, using markets, competition, and technology to assemble itself.

capital builds more powerful machines. those machines generate more capital. each cycle makes the system more autonomous and harder to live outside of.

what if we're no longer building technology to serve humanity, but reorganizing humanity to serve the machine?

2. nate hagens (@NJHagens): the economic superorganism

the economy is an emergent superorganism made up of billions of humans, companies, and institutions collectively optimizing for growth.

cheap energy enables growth. growth creates dependence on more energy. nobody is steering the whole thing, but everyone is participating.

what if civilization is an energy-hungry organism consuming the conditions for its own existence?

3. ray kurzweil (@raykurzweil): the technological singularity

evolution isn't limited to biology. intelligence is part of a billions-year process of increasing complexity, and technology is accelerating it.

intelligence builds better tools. better tools enable greater intelligence. the feedback loop accelerates beyond human comprehension.

what if humanity isn't the endpoint of evolution, but a transitional species building its successor?

4. paul kingsnorth: the machine

modern technological civilization isn't just a collection of tools. it's a worldview that treats nature, culture, and human beings as things to be optimized, controlled, and remade.

technology creates dependence on technological systems. those systems erode the traditions, communities, and relationships that once gave us autonomy.

what if progress is destroying some of the things that make life worth living?

5. sara walker & lee cronin: assembly theory

complex objects don't just appear. they emerge through histories of selection, where successful structures are preserved, copied, and built upon.

life is a process through which information becomes causal, shaping what gets constructed next.

what if intelligence and technology are continuations of the same evolutionary process that produced life?

five different ontologies:

- land sees capital assembling intelligence.
- hagens sees energy organizing complexity.
- kurzweil sees intelligence accelerating evolution.
- kingsnorth sees technology consuming the human world.
- walker & cronin see selection accumulating complexity.

they disagree on what's driving civilization and where it's heading. but all five challenge the assumption that humanity is consciously steering technological progress.

the questions i'm left with:
- are we shaping technology, or is technology shaping us?
- and how do we reclaim the agency to choose what we become?

the basic idea is that capitalism isn't just an economic system. it's an emerging machine intelligence, using markets, competition, and technological progress to assemble itself.

text:
Anthropic 天天警告世界，AI 可能毁灭人类。现在终于有人反过来问它了，既然这么危险，你凭什么急着以 2 万亿美元的估值上市？

纽约市主计长 Mark Levine 最近给 Dario Amodei 写了一封公开信，要求 Anthropic 暂停计划中最早 11 月进行的 IPO。

Levine 管理着超过 3250 亿美元的公共养老金资产。他在信里引用的证据非常有意思，几乎全部来自 Anthropic 自己。

Dario 此前公开呼吁放慢前沿模型的开发速度，Anthropic 的 IPO 文件里据称有长达 80 页的风险披露，甚至比业务介绍部分还长。公司内部研究人员也多次警告 AI 可能带来的灾难性后果。

现在 Levine 的意思是，你自己都把风险说到这个程度了，为什么还要急着让公众投资者进场？

Anthropic 从成立开始，就一直把 AI 安全放在自己商业叙事的中心。过去几年，这套叙事帮它建立了与 OpenAI 不同的品牌形象，也让它在 AI 监管讨论中拥有了相当大的话语权。

但上市意味着游戏规则变了。

一家估值可能达到 2 万亿美元的公司，如果认为自己的产品可能给社会造成数千亿美元的损失，那么这些风险究竟应该如何量化？谁来审计？谁有权叫停危险的模型？如果公司治理权仍然高度集中，普通股东又凭什么承担这些潜在损失？

更巧的是，Anthropic 刚披露第三季度营收 168 亿美元，环比增长 45%。增长依然惊人，但相比第二季度超过 100% 的增速已经明显放缓。部分投资者甚至开始讨论将 IPO 估值预期从 2 万亿美元降至 1.5 万亿美元。

过去 AI 公司谈安全，更多时候是一种道德承诺，甚至可以转化成竞争优势。现在资本市场开始要求它们为这些承诺提供具体的治理机制，并承担相应的财务责任。

如果 AI 安全真的进入机构投资者的风险定价体系，那么那些曾经被用来证明公司负责任的警告，未来也可能成为压低公司估值的理由。

text:
Announcing the public preview of https://t.co/VdMOPBsL7H: a lightweight Ethereum indexing node for research and apps on your own infra.

Building on Ethereum shouldn’t require a third-party RPC, and it definitely shouldn’t require a full node.

The concept is simple. You define the structure of your data via a processor, and Leani fulfills your history requests while also (optionally) serving live data.

This enables you to quickly build a backend for tracking Uniswap prices or even a browsable blobs leaderboard like https://t.co/QSxtb5mFhw, all while saving plenty of storage and RPC costs.

Leani comes with a handful of built-in processors, but it is easy to write your own. Simply point your agent towards the repo: https://t.co/GhLiFN3bLs.

Leani can be used as an RPC drop-in for all methods that do not require the EVM, through its HTTP API, by streaming changes over SSE, or with a dedicated TypeScript SDK.

I’ve already used Leani to build all kinds of cool things, from a simple real-time price feed to https://t.co/QSxtb5mFhw.

Ethereum 🫡

(Disclaimer: it's a public preview, so I'd use it mainly for fun experiments and research for now. Expect breaking changes.)

text:
Reflection AI 最有意思的地方，是它一边借鉴 DeepSeek-V3 的 MoE 路由设计，一边跑到华盛顿，把中国开源模型的领先定义为美国的国家安全威胁。

今天 Reflection 正式开放了 Beam 1.0 的模型权重，5010 亿总参数、230 亿激活参数，Apache 2.0 协议，支持 100 万 Token 上下文。

模型本身其实没有那么惊艳。按照 Reflection 自己公布的成绩，DeepSWE v1.1 上 Beam 得分 44.4，Kimi K3 是 68.0。其他多项 Agent 测试里，中国模型也依然领先。Beam 更值得讨论的卖点是推理效率。

但发布当天，AWS、Google Cloud、微软 Azure、NVIDIA、Cloudflare、CoreWeave、Dell、HPE 等 40 多家合作伙伴已经就位，从云端推理到企业私有部署，几乎全部覆盖。

今年 5 月，Reflection CEO Misha Laskin 在华盛顿游说时就公开讲过，中国正在大幅领先开源 AI，而这构成了美国的国家安全威胁。Reflection 当时已经拿到了 250 亿美元的估值。

他的逻辑其实很清楚。当一个国家的政府或一家大型企业决定把 AI 部署进自己的基础设施里，模型的国籍、监管归属、供应链控制权都会进入采购决策。

所以 Reflection 的商业机会非常微妙。它可以在性能尚未达到中国头部模型水平的时候，先争取那些愿意为了供应链安全和政治确定性付费的客户。技术上的差距可以慢慢追，企业采购中的信任壁垒却可能提前建立。

中国开源模型接下来真正需要面对的，是一个相当残酷的商业问题。

我们把模型性能做到了世界前列，把推理成本压了下来，也让全球开发者从中国的技术创新中获益。可这些技术一旦成为全行业共享的基础，美国公司完全可以在此之上继续开发，再利用本土身份、资本和政府关系，去争取利润更高的企业合同。

最讽刺的是，这整个过程完全符合开源精神。

开源可以让技术成果跨越国界，却无法保证创造这些成果的公司最终获得相应的商业回报。

中国模型已经证明自己有能力影响全球 AI 的技术路线。至于能从中赚到多少钱，我觉得现在还远远没到可以庆祝的时候。

After the early success of Pudgy Penguins, every project copied their playbook and tried to build a business outside core crypto, but the reality is that (with a few exceptions) no one cares, and there's no market or revenue for them.

Even the "successful" ones still sell most of their products to their crypto user base (NFT holders), but interest there is now also declining sharply, as those users get increasingly neglected in the push to find new non-crypto ones.

I am leaving Cambridge after a few days spent for a workshop on fast finality, concurrent with other workshops on post-quantum crypto and formal verification. Quick takeaways

- Faster finality is coming, the research is mature, even as new ideas have come in during the week, the handoff to specifiers and implementers feels well underway. Next catalyst event will be at devcon in a few weeks, with core devs
- The performance numbers for post-quantum finality are improving massively, and this is the worst that they’ll ever be. This is significant, it means the penalty from moving to more complex crypto would not require, in my opinion, if the numbers hold up, a deep rearchitecting to move to PQ-secure consensus, in particular when it comes to incentives
- The biggest opportunity imo remains networking. Simulations and live experiments are exploring both the current pre-PQ setting, where networking is clearly the bottleneck, and the post-PQ setting, where compute remains the bottleneck. But with PQ compute numbers improving, I wouldn’t be surprised if once again networking becomes the bottleneck

All of this is making me extremely bullish that we’ll achieve PQ-secure and faster finality even faster.

Many thanks to @yannvon @benjaminion_xyz and @robsaltini for the workshop, and to @corcoranwill and @drakefjustin for hosting us in Cambridge!

text:
扎克伯格（@finkd）刚刚晒出自己的办公桌：

没有天价 H200 机柜，只用两台并排的新款 Mac Studio，

就在本地跑起了今天刚开源的 816B 旗舰大模型 

Muse Spark Open

苹果 CEO John Ternus（@johnternus）也在评论区互动，短短几小时浏览量破百万。

816B 总参数、42B 激活参数，靠 MoE 稀疏架构和苹果统一内存，让桌面设备也有机会挑战超大模型。

硬件门槛、部署命令、避坑指南，一文看懂。

一、硬件门槛

1TB 内存：双 Mac Studio，MLX oQ4e，约 476GB 权重

512GB 内存：单台 Mac Studio，MLX oQ3e，约 340GB 权重

256GB 内存：Unsloth UD-Q2_K_XL 或 GGUF Q2_K，约 210GB 权重

700GB 以上显存：4×B200 或 8×H200，部署 NVFP4 版本

以上为原方案中的估算值，实际需求取决于模型版本、运行框架和上下文长度。

二、一键部署

Mac 单机：

uv tool install mlx-lm
mlx_lm.server --model "mlx-community/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-oQ3e" --port 8080

256GB 工作站：
llama serve -hf ggml-org/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-GGUF:Q2_K

企业级 GPU：

VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 1048576

运行前请确认模型仓库、权重格式、框架版本及启动参数均真实可用。

三、三个关键注意事项
采样参数：原方案建议 temperature=1.0、top_p=1.0，关闭 top_k，具体应以模型官方配置为准。

推理强度：确认框架支持的 reasoning_effort 参数后，再选择适合任务的推理等级。

多模态：图像、视频和音频的输入规格应以模型实际支持的配置为准。

从大型 GPU 集群到桌面工作站，超大模型的本地部署正在拓展更多可能。

你的主力机有多少内存？256GB、512GB，还是准备挑战双 Mac Studio？

欢迎评论区晒配置、交流部署经验。

text:
현재 코스피를 떠나서 대한민국의 미래가 진짜 어두운 이유.

최근 일론 머스크가 X(트위터)에 연달아 던진 두 마디가 한국 반도체의 본질을 정확히 관통함.

1) "마이크론의 메모리 가격은 합리적인 반면, 다른 기업들(삼성·하이닉스)은 터무니없는 폭리(extortionate)를 취하고 있다. 고객들은 오늘을 절대 잊지 않을 것이다."

2) (중국 창신메모리 급성장 기사를 인용하며) "2028년이면 중국이 엄청난 양의 램(RAM)을 찍어낼 것이다."

이게 도대체 무슨 의미일까?
머스크의 두 발언을 합치면 빅테크들의 서늘한 속내가 그대로 읽힘.

과거 애플이 아이폰 원가를 낮추려고 중국 YMTC·CXMT 메모리 도입을 추진했던 것처럼, 글로벌 빅테크들에게 한국 반도체는 '영원한 대체 불가 파트너'가 아니라는 거임.

지금은 AI 붐으로 울며 겨자 먹기로 비싼 한국산 메모리를 쓰지만, 중국이 스펙만 적당히 맞추고 싼값에 물량을 쏟아내는 순간 언제든 한국산을 가차 없이 갈아치울 준비가 되어 있다는 뜻임.

지금껏 우리는 이 피눈물 나는 역사를 수없이 목격해 왔음.

- LCD 디스플레이: 삼성·LG가 세계 1위를 독점했지만, 중국 BOE가 정부 보조금으로 패널을 똥값에 덤핑하자 결국 백기 투항하고 사업 철수.
- 태양광 & 석유화학 & 철강: 중국이 무제한 보조금으로 글로벌 판가를 원가 이하로 초토화시키며 국내 기업들 줄도산 및 구조조정.
- 배터리: K-배터리가 삼원계(NCM)로 버티는 사이, 중국이 압도적 가성비의 LFP로 글로벌 완성차 시장을 잠식.

그리고 그 악명 높은 ‘국가 주도 박리다매 치킨게임’의 마지막 타깃이 바로 한국 수출의 생명줄인 [메모리 반도체]임.

머스크의 경고대로 2028년 전후 창신메모리(CXMT)가 중국 정부의 천문학적 보조금을 등에 업고 물량을 융단폭격하기 시작하면 범용 D램 판가는 순식간에 무너짐.

"우린 HBM(고대역폭메모리)이 있으니 괜찮다"?고 말할수도 있지만, 전체 매출과 현금 창출의 기둥인 범용 D램이 적자로 돌아서면, 차세대 HBM에 투자할 실탄 자체가 마름. 심지어 중국은 이미 DDR5를 넘어 HBM까지 턱밑 추격 중임.

더 끔찍한 건, 메모리가 무너졌을 때 대한민국 경제를 받쳐줄 '다음 타자'가 단 하나도 없다는 사실임.

왜 다음 타자가 없을까?
한국이라는 국가 시스템 전체가 미래 경쟁력과 정반대 방향으로 설계되어 있기 때문임.

1. 최고 두뇌들의 ‘의대 블랙홀’

- 고등학교에서 전교 1등 하는 이과 수재 100명이면 100명 전원이 공대를 버리고 의대로 직행함.
- 미국·대만·중국은 최고 천재들이 AI, 반도체 랩으로 달려가 엔비디아, TSMC, 딥시크의 핵심 엔진이 되는데,
- 한국은 국가의 가장 귀한 브레인들이 전부 피부과, 성형외과, 개원의로 수렴하는 기형적인 구조가 고착화됨.

2. “공대 가면 바보”를 만드는 기형적 처우

- 왜 똑똑한 애들이 의대로 도망칠까? 한국의 연구직 보상 체계가 철저히 무너졌기 때문임.
- 삼성전자만 봐도 5~10년 뒤 미래 기술을 연구해야 할 핵심 조직(반도체연구소·SAIT)이 당장 돈 버는 메모리사업부 성과급의 70% 수준만 받는다는 블라인드 성토가 쏟아질 정도임.
- 원천 기술을 파는 석·박사 고급 인력들을 “당장 올해 매출 못 냈다”며 홀대하는데, 어느 미친 천재가 공대에 남아 인생을 갈아 넣겠음?
- 엔비디아 같은 미국 빅테크는 핵심 엔지니어들에게 수억~수백억대 주식(RSU)을 안겨주고, 중국조차 연봉 3~5배를 부르며 한국 엔지니어들을 빼가는데, 한국만 연구자를 ‘소모품 부품 1’ 취급하니 의대로 런하는 게 가장 합리적인 생존 전략이 된 거임.

3. "3대만 넘어가면 기업이 공중분해되는 구조"

- 여기에 기업의 숨통을 끊어놓는 ‘세계 1위 징벌적 상속세’까지 결합되면 상황은 완전히 절망적임.
- 이건희 회장 별세 당시 삼성 일가가 내야 했던 상속세만 무려 12조 원이었음.
- 한국의 상속세 최고세율은 50%, 여기에 최대주주 할증(20%)까지 붙으면 실효세율이 무려 60%에 달함 (OECD 압도적 1위, 평균은 26% 수준).
- 이게 얼마나 잔인한 산수냐면:
  1세대 지분 100% ➔ 2세대 40% ➔ 3세대 16%로 쪼그라듦.
- 2~3대만 넘어가도 지분의 84%가 세금으로 뜯겨나가 기업이 자연 해체되는 구조임.
- 결국 상속세 수조 원을 현금으로 마련하려고 오너 일가는 주가를 누르거나 주식을 헐값에 블록딜 매각하고, 그 틈을 타 외국계 투기자본이나 사모펀드가 경영권을 흔듦.
- 수십 년간 세계 1위 기술을 축적한 알짜 중소·중견기업들(쓰리세븐, 락앤락, 한샘 등)도 결국 세금을 못 버텨 사모펀드에 팔려나가거나 문을 닫아버림.

4. 기업가들의 한국 탈출 (본사 엑소더스)

- 상황이 이렇다 보니, 요즘 똑똑한 스타트업 창업자들은 애초에 한국에 본사를 두지 않음.
- 쿠팡을 시작으로 요즘 유망한 AI·테크 스타트업들은 설립 초기부터 미국(델라웨어)이나 싱가포르로 본사를 옮기는 ‘플립(Flip)’이 기본 공식이 됨.
- “한국에서 청춘 바쳐 기업 키워봤자, 전 세계에 유례없는 배임죄로 감옥 갈 리스크만 높고, 나중에 상속세로 국가에 회사 뺏기는데 왜 한국에 법인을 두냐”는 아주 냉정한 계산임.

결국 이 모든 게 하나로 맞물려 돌아가고 있음.

지금 당장은 삼성전자, SK하이닉스가 역대급 매출과 영업이익을 찍으며 잘 나가는 것처럼 보임.

하지만 중국이 과거 LCD나 배터리를 집어삼켰던 것처럼, 메모리 시장에서도 점유율을 야금야금 높이며 파이를 뺏어 먹기 시작하면 그땐 진짜 미래가 없음.

생각해 보면, 한국 반도체가 세계 1위 매출을 찍어도 그 가치가 주가(밸류에이션)에 제대로 반영되지 않는 진짜 이유도 바로 여기에 있음.

엔비디아처럼 누구도 넘볼 수 없는 독점 생태계(해자)를 가진 게 아니라, 언제든 값싸고 스펙 비슷한 대체재가 나오면 가차 없이 갈아치워질 수 있는 ‘규격화된 부품 시장’이기 때문임.

주가는 당장의 실적(펀더멘탈)도 중요하지만, 결국 ‘미래 가치와 지속 가능성’에 훨씬 더 큰 점수를 주는 생물임.

글로벌 자본시장은 이미 알고 있는 거임.

유일한 캐시카우인 메모리는 중국의 물량 공세 앞에 유통기한이 켜졌고,
그 뒤를 이을 천재들은 전부 의대로 블랙홀처럼 빨려 들어가고,
남아있는 연구자들은 홀대받고,
기업은 징벌적 상속세에 팔려나가고,
새로운 창업자들은 해외로 탈출하고 있다는 걸.

화려한 '역대 최대 매출' 뉴스 뒤에 가려진 이 서늘한 구조적 결말이, 지금 대한민국의 미래가 진짜 어두운 이유임.

quoted_text:
这两天不少人私信问我 @safetrade 上的低市值“欢乐豆”，干脆把我了解的项目整理一下：主网上线时间较新、体量较小，主要在 SafeTrade 能交易。

涨跌别问我，我也不知道。我只知道，Safetrade上币都是免费的，既然他们选择list，那或许会有一些亮点，而在研究后，我知道这些项目谁在背后，这些信息或许对你有帮助，但只是研究线索，绝对不是投资推荐。

1｜Qubitcoin qubitcoin-2:native @qubitcoinx

做量子电路模拟挖矿的 BTC 分叉。创始人 @MYShalaginov 有 MIT 博士后及量子光学、纳米光子学研究经历，科研背景很不错。

不过，我对他在项目上的持续投入经历抱有疑问。我看过的他自己主持的播客，没见过他提自己的项目。创始人背景这么好，如果能把更多精力放在建设上自己的项目就更好了。

流通市值约 $1.54M｜最大供给口径 FDV 约 $14M

2｜Parano1d $NOID @Parano1dComm

通过递归证明验证链状态，以 PoW 确定顺序，尝试减少新节点对完整历史重放的依赖。

开发者 @ignotus_nemo 未实名，但从公开文章和以太坊论坛的讨论看，我个人觉得是想认真做事的，技术方向也有些意思。

我的个人经历比较惨：早期挖过几万个，低位也买过一点，结果 0.01 多就卖了，最近看着上涨，拍断大腿。

流通市值750K｜无固定发行上限，需结合排放计划评估后续稀释与抛压

3｜NeptuneCash $NPT @NeptuneCash

主打隐私和抗量子方向的 PoW 公链，核心设计包括 STARK 零知识证明和 Mutator Sets。

核心开发者包括 @aszepieniec、@ThorkilVaerge。经历25年社区分叉后，项目仍在持续建设，我一直比较关注它的技术路线，技术开发依然活跃。

流通市值560K｜最大供给口径 FDV 约 $5.5M

4｜Neptune Privacy neptune-privacy:native @NeptunePrivacy

2025 年从 NPT 社区分叉出来的项目，分歧主要围绕代币发行模型和发展路线。

开发方向包括 L2“利维坦”，实际交付还需继续跟踪。就我的观察，社区在传播和推广上更积极，也已经上了 MEXC。

流通市值约 $625K｜无固定发行上限，需结合排放计划评估后续稀释与抛压

5｜Compute Substrate $CSD

一个挺有个性的“链上公共建议箱”：让人或程序提交想法、表达支持，形成可复核的排行榜。

链只记录支持，不判断观点真假，也不替参与者执行决定。更像一个协调与公共记录的应用协议实验，而不是又一条泛用公链。

协议发起者 @matsjulner，也可以关注 @Cairn_substrate、@0xInverse 生态开发者账号。

流通市值约 $17K｜最大供给口径 FDV 约 $300K

6｜Midstate $MDS @cypherpunkgold

以 BLAKE3、哈希签名和顺序 PoW 为基础，走抗量子电子现金方向。

可关注 @phraudsta 的公开内容，以及他的播客 https://t.co/KmNeYBkI2C。Dev行文有密码朋克色彩，但真实职业履历仍未确认，推特号倒是粉丝不少，有一些加密OG关注和互动。

流通市值约 $21K｜FDV约 $68K

7｜Parallax $LAX @prlxchain

ETN 生态开发者 @andre_patta 发起的新项目，采用 XHash PoW，支持 EVM 智能合约。

这个在我这里更偏“欢乐豆”观察仓：先看开发者有没有持续交付，以及网络和生态能不能慢慢做起来。

行情站流通市值约 $12K｜最大供给口径 FDV 约 $86K

另外还有 @Kvanta5_QR，也是抗量子方向，但开发者身份和项目沿革仍有待核实，据说是 @BitcoincashII 的同一个人 ，不知道Safetrade觉得他哪方面有亮点，还不清楚。

以上就这些，全部免费分享，祝你们好运。

text:
Nullmask / $MASK: the most underrated privacy coin of the cycle

$MASK is currently sitting at around $23.5m market cap ($40m FDV, with 40% of supply out of circulation and 2.16% already burnt)

i believe Nullmask is by far the most underrated privacy coin in all of crypto, and i'll explain why in this thread

let's start by looking at the top privacy coins and their market caps:

• ZCash / $ZEC: $21 BILLION market cap
• $NEAR: $6.8 BILLION market cap

these two have been by far the biggest gainers in the top 50 cryptocurrencies over the past year, and it's not even close!

if it isn't already obvious, both have run hard (and continue to run) on the PRIVACY narrative

but what's impressive isn't just their gigantic market caps

it's how much they've added in the past year alone:

• ZCash added $18 BILLION to its market cap
• NEAR added $4.3 BILLION to its market cap

all before the bull run has properly started

so how does this affect Nullmask / $MASK?

the incredible runs ZEC, NEAR, and other privacy coins have had have established beyond reasonable doubt that this is the privacy cycle

and i believe Nullmask is going to win big because it sits right at the heart of this narrative, with several key advantages that many much bigger privacy coins don't have

let's start with the PRODUCT

Nullmask makes private transactions possible across EVM chains and Solana in the most normie-friendly way imaginable

you can use your existing wallets (MetaMask, Rabby, Phantom, etc.) the same way you normally would, while enabling private transactions across major ecosystems like Ethereum, BNB, Base, Robinhood, and Solana

yes, you read that right

you don't need to learn how to use a new wallet, create a new seed phrase or private key, learn to navigate a complicated new blockchain, or deal with any of that nonsense

you can activate Nullmask's privacy capabilities on your existing crypto setup in just a few clicks

all you need to do is activate Nullmask's custom RPC and let its 'virtual private network' shield your transfers using zero-knowledge proofs

i'm simplifying the technical details to make this as normie-friendly as possible, but that's the gist of it

and this isn't just speculative stuff: Nullmask is already LIVE & WORKING on Ethereum, BNB, Base, and Robinhood

you can actually use the product and verify that it works!

but i'm bullish on $MASK for more than just the product

TOTAL ADDRESSABLE MARKET (TAM)

what makes Nullmask so incredibly bullish and underrated isn't just how impressive the product is, but the size of its total addressable market

i've never used the ZCash or NEAR blockchains, and the same is true for tens of millions of users across Solana, Robinhood, Base, BNB, and Ethereum

yet ZCash and NEAR have market caps of approximately $21 BILLION and $7 BILLION, respectively

the average crypto user may never touch the ZCash or NEAR blockchains, but they're already using Ethereum, Robinhood, BNB, Solana, and Base

and Nullmask caters to those users

this begs the question:

what is fair value for Nullmask when ZCash and NEAR are both trading at multibillion-dollar valuations?

LET'S TALK ABOUT THE TEAM

when a protocol promises something as ambitious as Nullmask does, you obviously want to know who's building it and whether they're capable of delivering

Nullmask is built by several ZCash contributors, led by Tomas Krnak

Tomas Krnak helped build shielded ZCash transactions for hardware wallets. his work was funded by the ZCash Foundation and merged into the main ZCash protocol itself

i should also add that the lead dev is doxxed and regularly participates in live interviews!

PARTNERSHIPS & INTEGRATIONS

we've established that the team has serious credentials in the privacy space and that the product is already live and working

but what about partnerships, integrations, and endorsements?

here's a list of industry players Nullmask has collaborated with in some form since launching:

• NEAR Protocol ($11.3 BILLION ATH)
• THORChain ($4.4 BILLION ATH)
• Dashpay
• Beldex
• Quai Network

the team also revealed in a recent AMA that it's in discussions with major wallet providers, including MetaMask, about potentially integrating Nullmask as an additional privacy layer

all of this for a product that isn't even a month old, by the way!

METRICS & REVENUE

Nullmask looks incredibly strong from a fundamentals perspective, but the key question is:

what do the metrics actually look like?

since the protocol launched a little over two weeks ago, Nullmask has generated:

• $37.8 MILLION in total protocol volume, averaging $2.36 million per day
• $833k in total revenue, averaging $52k per day

it has also burnt 2.16% of supply and distributed $1.4 MILLION in $ZEC rewards to holders since the token launched approximately three weeks ago (token launched a week before the protocol)

and here's the important part:

all these adoption metrics were recorded before the protocol is live on Solana, which is expected to happen next week, and mostly before it went live on Robinhood and BNB just a few days earlier

the team also has 20% of the token supply allocated to a long-term incentives campaign designed to encourage people to use the protocol and accelerate adoption

i should also add that Nullmask is now ranked #1 among ALL privacy protocols for both 7-day and 30-day revenue, according to DeFiLlama, barely two weeks after its protocol went live, and by a clear margin

this is despite the fact that 

-it only went live on Robinhood and BNB a few days earlier
- it is yet to launch on Solana
- its incentives program aimed at accelerating adoption is yet to launch

the speed of adoption Nullmask has witnessed is impressive for any privacy protocol

TOKENOMICS

20% of the token supply is allocated to the team and locked for two years, meaning these tokens won't start entering circulation until at least two years after token launch

another 20% is reserved for an incentives campaign aimed at accelerating protocol adoption

the remaining 60% of supply is circulating

this means approximately 60% of the supply is currently in circulation, while the bulk of the rest won't enter circulation anytime soon

ROADMAP

• Launch on Ethereum, Robinhood, BNB, and Base (LIVE)
• Cross-chain bridge (LIVE)
• Unshield directly to ZEC wallets (October 2026)
• Launch on Solana (Q4 2026)
• NullMask SDK (Q4 2026)
• Privacy Perpetuals (Q4 2026)

TO CONCLUDE

i know Nullmask might sound too good to be true right now, and it's crazy to me that it's sitting at such a ridiculously low market cap

but believe it or not, all of the facts in my thesis above can be independently verified

i'm not going to ask you to buy Nullmask

i'm simply laying out my thesis and thought process for this trade, and explaining why i believe it could be a big one

i objectively believe $MASK will become a multibillion-dollar token before the end of the bull run, and i expect it to be yet another kingmaker trade for me

nothing in this thesis is financial advice

AI is making Ethereum more ambitious.

You might have heard about the challenges that blockchains face in a post-AI world, and while security assumptions will surely be stress-tested in the coming months and years, there is another side to it. I believe AI will let us speedrun towards a world that's both more secure and feature-rich.

As we look towards Ethereum's first post-AI upgrade, Hegotá, the R&D community is asking itself what increasingly powerful tools could help us do differently:

> How far can we push both security and iteration speed?
> How much of the design space can we examine before committing to one?
> How easily can we test the interactions between complex features?

My recent formal verification work @ethlabs_org has given me some reasons to be optimistic about these, as work that would have previously not even been attempted is now being done by agents in days. In September, I posted about using formal verification as part of designing a new consensus protocol. This time, I want to tell you about formally verifying something already fully specified and in production: Ethereum's Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR).

If you are not familiar with FCR, it lets applications confirm Ethereum blocks in seconds, roughly 30x faster than waiting for finality, under additional assumptions (from waiting 13 minutes to 24 seconds!). It also further solidifies Ethereum L1's case as an asset hub and center of gravity for the onchain economy. FCR now has a safety proof in Lean, closely modeling the rule in the consensus specs, which is the source of truth for Ethereum's consensus clients.

Some takeaways:

> FCR is safe! Under its assumptions, confirmed blocks remain canonical. On top of the manual proofs from the paper, we now have Lean proofs of this for the actual spec, additional evidence for applications considering FCR!

> The bulk of the formal verification work took just a 4-5 days (check out the animation!), with agents working mostly unsupervised. We should be very ambitious about using this as a tool at scale.

> After verifying the current rule, it was easy to adapt the model to the upcoming Gloas changes. Immediately, this surfaced a subtle bug caused by changes to fork choice. The problem was in the spec itself and not a gap in the model. The safety proof would not go through, and the agents could precisely pinpoint what was causing it to fail. The bug is now fixed, and formal verification of the corrected protocol goes through.

Iteration is never quite over, even for "finished" features like FCR, because the protocol keeps evolving around them. A formal model lets us ensure that key properties keep holding throughout the evolution of the protocol. With these capabilities, Ethereum can and should keep upgrading faster, tightening fork timelines and exploring more ambitious features, while still raising the security bar.

This picture has been getting much clearer over the past few months, and the past week confirmed it for me, as @drakefjustin and @corcoranwill brought together 100+ Ethereum researchers, cryptographers and formal verification experts in Cambridge for six days of workshops on post-quantum cryptography, formal verification and fast finality. Beyond its own workshop, formal verification was the omnipresent star of the week: everyone is using Lean and doing amazing things with it! Piece by piece, Ethereum's technological core is being rebuilt for the post-AI age.

The excitement was palpable, the sense of optimism was pervasive, and every talk and conversation carried a level of ambition I'd never seen before. The Ethereum R&D machine is upgrading itself, and we will see the outcome of that on the network sooner than you think.

text:
推荐一下 @flock_io 

比较值得注意的是，他们把 AI Agent 里的「决策」单独拆出来做成了一个小模型。

THIS / THAT 基于 Qwen3.5-2B，专门处理工具选择、任务分配、下一步动作这类判断。按照团队公布的数据，在 1710 道复杂决策题里，1.2 版本成功率做到 87.8%，高于 Claude Opus 5 的 83.4% 和 GPT-5.6 的 81.6%。

技术上，它只有约 18.8 亿参数，可以本地运行，单次决策大约 31ms，也不需要生成一大段输出 Token。

我觉得这背后更值得研究的是一个趋势：

AI Agent 下一阶段的竞争，可能会从“谁更会回答”，慢慢走向“谁更会做决定”。

真正进入交易、自动化和企业工作流以后，很多关键节点其实根本不需要一个最大的模型。

需要的是：低延迟、低成本、稳定地把一个判断做对。

再往后看，我觉得 Agent 这条线会慢慢拆成几层：

Decision
Execution
Permission / Risk
Verification
Memory / Identity

也就是说，谁负责判断，谁负责执行，谁限制权限，谁处理争议，谁保存长期上下文。

当这些层开始独立长出产品，Agent 才算真的从“会聊天”走向“会工作”。

所以我现在看这类项目，会更关注几个问题：

它解决的是哪一个决策环节？
为什么一定需要专用模型？
相比通用模型，准确率、延迟、成本到底改善多少？
做错一次的代价是什么？
最后有没有真实资金或业务结果？

@Alibaba_Qwen 和 @alibaba_cloud 这次也有公开支持，训练跑在阿里云上，再加上 FLock 自己在 ACL 2026 的研究成果，这条路线至少已经开始有比较扎实的东西可以验证。

如果 Agent 下一阶段真的从「会回答」走到「会执行」，那决策层会是我很关注的一层基础设施。

$FLOCK 可以继续保持关注，等风来！

如果你也在做 Agent Decision / Execution / Risk / Verification 这一类产品，欢迎来找我交流。
