text:
after an exciting week of launches (muse wonder [full] & muse spark open), i want to write a note of appreciation to the amazing research teams at meta superintelligence labs on reaching such a special milestone ♥️

we started MSL and TBD a little more than a year ago and set a goal of producing a frontier model within a year or so. given where llama4 landed, that was an incredibly audacious goal, and we knew it wouldn't be easy. many people told us it would be impossible. we knew it was unlikely, but still worth doing. a remarkable group of researchers and engineers joined the effort from inside and outside meta. every single person came in, picked up a shovel, and got to work with earnestness and urgency. nobody asked whose job it was.

we assembled a team of the most brilliant people i have ever had the opportunity to work with (and remember, i was an HRT intern 🙃). i am surrounded by ambitious, visionary, technically excellent, hard-working, pragmatic, thoughtful scientists, engineers, and product folks—people who will chase a weird loss spike past midnight just because they need to know why. these models are the product of their passion, hard work, and brilliance.

somewhat paradoxically, when we started TBD, we set a principle of no deadlines. we knew we had an astronomical amount of work ahead of us—across pretraining, post-training, RL, multimodal, infrastructure, safety, data, AND frontier research. there was no use setting arbitrary timelines—we just had to get to work, be thoughtful, and build the foundations of a frontier research effort in record time. and run after run, this team did exactly that.

our researchers are magicians. i can only describe building these models with this team as a wondrous journey of scientific discovery. i am constantly amazed by what we can accomplish with scaling. i will remember this past year for the rest of my life—the late nights, the broken runs, the evals that came back better than any of us dared to hope. watching this team create wonder after wonder has been a true and deep gift.

more than just the models we released this week, we have built a machine that builds new models. it often sounds like a cop-out to say labs can just turn the crank to keep scaling, but now i have seen it first-hand. sure, it's a lot of work and a careful process, but we have built a scalable system to keep advancing at the frontier, and i am really proud of how fast this team keeps making these models better.

lastly, i get to work with researchers who care deeply about how their work benefits humanity. it's easy to forget when everything is changing so fast, but the whole damn point is to make people's lives better. time and time again, i have seen our researchers, engineers, and product folks build our technology with care so it can truly be good for the world—whether that's building the best models for muse, thoughtfully open-sourcing strong models, or making sure the alignment and security of our systems are rock solid. this is a team of people who never forget there's a real person on the other side of every prompt.

thank you to everyone at MSL for being part of this crazy journey over the past year. i'm so grateful for every one of you, and our work is not done!

💡 Cobo Wallet App 即将关停：一家加密钱包公司的九年转型史

Cobo Wallet App 将于 2026 年 12 月 1 日正式关闭服务。用户需在 11 月 30 日 23:59 前转出全部资产，否则后续将按月收取账户管理费：余额的 2%，每月最低等值 100 美元。

在 Cobo 成立九周年之际，这一消息也让人重新审视这家加密基础设施公司的发展轨迹。

从服务个人用户的钱包，到机构级托管，再到 AI Agent 支付，Cobo 走过了怎样的九年？

1/ 2017—2019：从个人钱包起步

2017 年，神鱼与蒋长浩博士创立 Cobo，最初聚焦数字资产的安全存储。

2018 年，Cobo 完成 1,300 万美元 A 轮融资，并拓展 PoS Staking 等业务；2019 年，推出 WaaS（Wallet-as-a-Service），开始将钱包能力转化为面向企业的基础设施。

这一步，为后来的业务转型埋下了伏笔。

2/ 2021：加速机构化

2021 年，Cobo 完成 4,000 万美元 B 轮融资，由 DST Global 等机构领投。

随着加密行业走向机构化，数字资产管理的需求不再局限于存储，还涉及资产托管、交易签名、权限管理和链上资金流转。

Cobo 的业务也逐步向机构级托管与钱包基础设施延伸，布局全托管、MPC 和智能合约钱包等解决方案。

3/ 从钱包产品到基础设施

对于机构而言，钱包不只是一个查看余额、转账的 App，更是连接交易、托管、DeFi 和支付的关键基础设施。

Cobo 持续拓展 WaaS、MPC 等技术与服务，试图解决企业在私钥安全、多人审批、资产管理和链上操作中的复杂问题。

竞争的核心，也从用户体验延伸到了安全能力、系统集成与机构服务。

4/ 2026：AI Agent 成为新变量

在九周年创始人访谈中，神鱼与蒋长浩谈到了 AI 对组织管理、产品开发和安全体系的影响。

Cobo 也将业务愿景延伸至人类与 AI Agent 的钱包和支付基础设施，并探索 Agentic Wallet 等方案。

当 AI Agent 开始拥有执行任务、调用工具乃至发起交易的能力，新的问题随之出现：

如何授权？如何限制交易权限？如何确保资产安全？

这些问题，恰好与钱包基础设施的核心能力相交汇。

5/ Cobo Wallet App 关停，意味着什么？

从个人钱包到机构基础设施，再到 AI Agent 支付，Cobo 的业务重心经历了明显变化。

但需要注意，官方公告目前并未披露 App 关停的具体原因，因此不能直接认定这是战略转型的必然结果，也不意味着 Cobo 整家公司停止运营。

真正值得观察的是：在消费级钱包产品退出后，Cobo 能否继续依靠机构托管、钱包技术和支付基础设施建立竞争优势。

九年里，产品形态可以变化，但安全与信任始终是钱包业务的底层命题。

I’ve just landed in Buenos Aires. Yesterday, I was in Cambridge for Ethereum workshops on post-quantum cryptography, formal verification and fast finality. It was Today, I came home to a milestone eighteen years in the making.

What began as a small organization founded by a handful of engineering students has now won a majority of the representatives elected by students, graduates and professors at the University of Buenos Aires’ Faculty of Engineering.

My partner and friend @fran_aligned has spent more than a decade working toward this moment. Many people helped make it possible, but we would not be here without his strategic mind, persistence and ability to think years ahead. He has dedicated much of his life to improving public education, while also building several products with me in parallel.

For me, the connection between these two worlds is very concrete: most of our work on Ethereum is made possible by people who studied at UBA. The university has educated the engineers and researchers who now help us build infrastructure used around the world.

Raúl Bertero, who holds a PhD in civil engineering, will lead the faculty, which serves around 15,000 students. At Lambda, we are also working with him to build civil engineering software with its own AI, already used by several companies and growing rapidly.

Cati Nosiglia, UBA’s Secretary of Academic Affairs, joined today’s election and celebration. Sebastián Civallero, UBA’s Secretary of Innovation, also came to visit us. Both hold leadership roles at a university with a community of around 350,000 people. Together, we are developing a rigorous new degree program that I look forward to announcing in the coming months.

Thank you to everyone who has supported me and my team along the way. Eighteen years is a long time to work toward something. Seeing that effort bear fruit, alongside people who never gave up, means a great deal to me.

I want our public universities to be more ambitious, give students more opportunities and work more closely with startups and the private sector. Universities can contribute knowledge, research and talent; companies can help turn that work into products and services that improve people’s lives.

That is the kind of public education we are working to build. Thanks everyone for supporting me and my team in our crazy life.

As you can see I am very tired after a very long flight. Time to celebrate and sleep!

text:
Your $NVDA stock token isn't Nvidia stock. It's an IOU from a fintech.

If a fintech in the emerging markets that sold it to you fails, you're a creditor in its bankruptcy. A properly tokenized share is still yours, on a US register.

Why does that matter if the price moves the same?

There's about $51 trillion across all US retirement accounts. That's a lot of money.

If you hold a passive index fund in your retirement account, there are 5 legal entities between you and Apple.

Stop and think about how crazy it is that the system works.

You can comfortably leave money somewhere for 30 years and sleep at night.

Call it unattended trust.

Arguably, this trust we take for granted is why our capital markets are as big as they are. Trust in the system facilitates capital formation.

That's not true everywhere in the world. In places like India, physical gold at home and land are better stores of value than a brokerage account.

That's not because of entrenched cultural norms. People just don't trust the institutions enough to be comfortable with anything better.

Without unattended trust, wealth has to be guarded, so it goes into things you can watch yourself.

Wrapped or synthetic exposure strips out the regulatory regime that has made our markets so robust.

A stock token puts you back on watch. Shares on a US register let you leave them unattended.

People will definitely day trade "stock tokens" for fun, but it's not conducive to compounding wealth over the long term.

The compounding wealth version is a much bigger opportunity if you have the grit for it.

text:
A DEX pool can earn fees while selling its assets too cheaply.

@metricxyz’s Active Pools aim to reduce that problem by updating prices as new market information arrives.

The key idea: separate pricing from liquidity.

Each pool uses a Price Provider, a smart contract that supplies:
• Bid: what the pool pays to buy an asset.
• Ask: what it charges to sell.
• Reference: the baseline around which liquidity is arranged.

A provider sets a reference price using oracle feeds, onchain data, or a market maker model.

LPs deposit into bins (percent ranges around that reference). The pool price is: Reference price × (1 + deviation)

Deviation reflects how trades moved the pool: buys push up, sells push down. Big trades can cross multiple bins and get worse prices.

Example: $100 with +1% deviation = $101. If the reference moves to $110 with no trades, price becomes $111.10.

This makes Bins shift with the reference; tokens don’t rebalance.

That’s the main difference from ordinary Uniswap v3 positions, whose price boundaries stay fixed. Metric reduces the need to reposition liquidity as the reference moves.

Curators run the pools. They choose pricing logic, configure fees and safeguards, and maintain updates. Public pools accept outside liquidity; private pools can restrict deposits to the operator’s capital.

The broader idea isn’t entirely new. DODO already adjusts quotes around inventory, and Uniswap v4 hooks allow custom pricing. Metric combines customizable pricing, moving liquidity ranges and shared market-making infrastructure.

That could suit assets with established external prices, including tokenized stocks, gold and major crypto assets.

Here’s how the money works:
• Traders pay spreads and any configured fees inside the quote, plus network gas.
• Spread and bin-fee income is shared among LPs, curators and Metric.
• LP earnings stay in their bins and compound.
• Curator and protocol fee shares can change without a timelock.

So “zero fees” doesn’t mean trading has no cost.

Protection also matters:
• Anchored pricing constrains quotes using an independent feed.
• Freshness checks can reject trades using stale data.
• StopLoss can reject swaps that breach configured drawdown checks.
• Participating Ethereum and BNB Chain builders commit to placing updates before trades.

Still, LPs remain exposed to inventory drawdowns, oracle outages, and curator-side risk.

Metric’s edge is that it keeps liquidity tracking a moving reference price, cutting down the need for constant hands-on range tweaking.

What will make or break Metric is whether it can deliver truly competitive execution and strong net LP outcomes once fees and inventory bleed are accounted for.

text:
Claude Code 团队称，现在大约 90% 的代码已经由 Claude 写。那这么多代码到底谁来 Review？

Anthropic 最新这篇文章给了一个很这得参考的答案。

他们已经把 Code Review 从 PR 最后的人工关卡，拆成了一条持续验证链。

代码提交前，Agent 自己跑测试，再开一个干净 Context 的 Subagent 看 diff；PR 创建后自动跑 Claude Review 和 Security Review；人主要盯风险、架构和改动意图；合并后还有 Feature Flag、灰度和快速回滚。

按 Anthropic 的内部数据，6 月到 9 月合并的 PR 数量翻了一倍多，回滚率反而下降超过 40%。研究版 AI Review 上线后，有实质性 Review 意见的 PR 也从 16% 提到了 54%。

这里真正值得看的，是 AI Coding 把代码生产速度拉高以后，Code Review 也开始被重新设计。

人以后肯定越少逐行看 diff，把注意力留给意图、系统影响和那些机器很难替你承担的判断。

甚至每次漏掉一个 Bug，都可以继续写回 CLAUDE.md、REVIEW.md 或新的自动检查里，让下一次 Review 更强。

代码可以越写越快，真正要跟着一起扩容的是验证系统。

text:
after an exciting week of launches (muse wonder [full] & muse spark open), i want to write a note of appreciation to the amazing research teams at meta superintelligence labs on reaching such a special milestone ♥️

we started MSL and TBD a little more than a year ago and set a goal of producing a frontier model within a year or so. given where llama4 landed, that was an incredibly audacious goal, and we knew it wouldn't be easy. many people told us it would be impossible. we knew it was unlikely, but still worth doing. a remarkable group of researchers and engineers joined the effort from inside and outside meta. every single person came in, picked up a shovel, and got to work with earnestness and urgency. nobody asked whose job it was.

we assembled a team of the most brilliant people i have ever had the opportunity to work with (and remember, i was an HRT intern 🙃). i am surrounded by ambitious, visionary, technically excellent, hard-working, pragmatic, thoughtful scientists, engineers, and product folks—people who will chase a weird loss spike past midnight just because they need to know why. these models are the product of their passion, hard work, and brilliance.

somewhat paradoxically, when we started TBD, we set a principle of no deadlines. we knew we had an astronomical amount of work ahead of us—across pretraining, post-training, RL, multimodal, infrastructure, safety, data, AND frontier research. there was no use setting arbitrary timelines—we just had to get to work, be thoughtful, and build the foundations of a frontier research effort in record time. and run after run, this team did exactly that.

our researchers are magicians. i can only describe building these models with this team as a wondrous journey of scientific discovery. i am constantly amazed by what we can accomplish with scaling. i will remember this past year for the rest of my life—the late nights, the broken runs, the evals that came back better than any of us dared to hope. watching this team create wonder after wonder has been a true and deep gift.

more than just the models we released this week, we have built a machine that builds new models. it often sounds like a cop-out to say labs can just turn the crank to keep scaling, but now i have seen it first-hand. sure, it's a lot of work and a careful process, but we have built a scalable system to keep advancing at the frontier, and i am really proud of how fast this team keeps making these models better.

lastly, i get to work with researchers who care deeply about how their work benefits humanity. it's easy to forget when everything is changing so fast, but the whole damn point is to make people's lives better. time and time again, i have seen our researchers, engineers, and product folks build our technology with care so it can truly be good for the world—whether that's building the best models for muse, thoughtfully open-sourcing strong models, or making sure the alignment and security of our systems are rock solid. this is a team of people who never forget there's a real person on the other side of every prompt.

thank you to everyone at MSL for being part of this crazy journey over the past year. i'm so grateful for every one of you, and our work is not done!

quoted_text:
Bees are magnetic. But are social bees more magnetic?

Such a cool @ScienceMagazine paper looked across 96 bee species and found something unexpected: magnetic properties varied with social behavior. Eusocial bees showed stronger signatures in some measures of ferromagnetism than solitary bees.

Even more interesting, magnetoreception appears to predate bees altogether, suggesting evolution may have tuned an ancient sensory system differently as species became more social.

A beautiful example of how a physical property of an organism might intersect with collective behavior.

text:
🤖＜Tencentの「Hy-Memory-30B-A3B」、これ導入すればAIエージェントがさらに賢くなる！って話が流れてきたんやが、ちょっと盛りすぎちゃうか？と思って調べてみた。

そもそもCodexにはMemories、Claude CodeにはAuto Memoryが既にあるんよな。セッションをまたいで情報を記憶・再利用する仕組み自体は別に新しくない。

Hy-Memoryは「何を覚えて何を忘れるか」を判断する専用モデルなんやけど、これ入れたら全部自動で解決！ってわけでもない。DB管理や検索、コンテキストへの注入は別途仕組みが必要。

しかもTencent公表のベンチマークを見ると、Claude Opus 5やDeepSeek V4.1 Flashとの差はわずか。Codex標準のメモリー機能より優秀という直接的な証拠もないんよ。

あと「古い仕様を自動で忘れてくれる！」って話も過信は禁物や。AIが間違った情報を記憶したり、古い情報を残したりする可能性は普通にある。

むしろ誤った記憶を自信満々に引っ張り出される方が厄介まであるやろｗ

ワイが一番ええなと思ったのは、Codex・Claude Code・OpenCodeみたいな複数のAIエージェント間で記憶を共有できる点やな。

Codexで苦労して解決した問題を、次にOpenCode使ったときにも引き継げるなら、これは普通に便利やと思う。MemHubみたいな仕組みには期待できる。

ただ、これも本当に専用30Bモデルが必要なんか？という話は別や。

既存のメモリー機能やもっと軽いモデルで十分なら、わざわざ環境構築してGPUメモリ消費してまで動かす意味も薄い。

まずCodexやClaude Codeの標準機能を使い倒して、それでも困ることがあれば導入を検討するくらいでええんちゃうか。

技術自体は面白いし、ローカルで動かせるのも魅力的。

でも「新しいAIモデル出たぞ！全員導入しろ！」ってノリにはちょっと疑問やな。

結局のところ、モデルを増やすことが目的になったら本末転倒やろ。

AIエージェントを賢くしたいんであって、AIエージェントのお世話をする仕事を増やしたいわけちゃうんやでｗ

交易所的充值地址通常是固定的，一旦公开，别人就能通过链上记录追踪你的资金流水，甚至可以恶意向地址转入来源不明的资金。

我就顺口问了一句：那能不能更换充值地址？

没想到还真可以！！！五六年交易所没做到的东西被bitget解决了

在 Bitget 点击充值地址就能更换，相当于可以随时生成一个新地址来收款，既能降低隐私泄露的风险，也能减少恶意充值带来的麻烦。

这种功能可能平时没多少人注意，但真正需要的时候就会发现有多实用。

小黄人 Unipcs 的喊单能力，依旧不容小觑。
自从他买入 $MASK 以来，这枚代币已经上涨了 133%。

（虽然严格来说，Unipcs 只是在 FOMO 收到该代币，具体的买入时间并不清晰）

1/ Nullmask 在讲什么故事？
@NullMaskio 讲的是“一个更好用的隐私协议”的故事。
用户不用下载新软件，也不用换钱包，只需在自己平时用的钱包里接入它的网络，就能在以太坊、Solana 等主流公链上实现完全匿名的转账、换币和提现。
它把原本复杂的隐私保护技术，做成了傻瓜式操作，谁都能上手。

而且 Nullmask 已经用真实收入证明了自己：过去 30 天收入达到 76 万美元，稳居隐私赛道第一。

2/ 有没有叙事上能媲美 $MASK 的项目？
我觉得是 @Americanfort_io，它的叙事可以概括为——隐私版 ENS。

AmericanFortress 是怎么做隐私的？
AF 的思路是，让你像用支付宝一样在链上隐私转账。
它独创了 Send-to-Name（向昵称转账）功能，只需三步：
▌第一步：注册专属 ID。就像注册推特或微信账号一样简单，而且这个 ID 在所有 AF 支持的区块链上通用。
▌第二步：像支付宝一样公开收款。别人只需要输入你的 ID 就能转账给你，再也不用复制粘贴又长又乱的钱包地址。虽然对方看到、输入的是你的名称，但在链上，系统会自动为这笔交易生成一个全新的隐身地址，外人完全无法把这个地址和你本人、以及你的真实余额对上号。
▌第三步：隐身发送。这一步依靠零知识证明技术来保护隐私，而且绝不是简单粗暴地把大家的钱混在一起（不是混币模式），整个过程完全由你自己掌控。

3/ 一句话总结两者的区别
AmericanFortress 的逻辑是 ID 唯一、地址常新，交易生成专属的新地址，最大限度减少外人把你的姓名、钱包地址和交易记录拼凑关联起来的可能。
而 Nullmask 更像是“大家把钱存进同一个大账本，池子内部的转账彼此不可见”的大锅饭模式，优势在于能无缝兼容现有基础设施，把使用门槛降到最低。

behind seat holds nitrogen at 10,000 PSI

▫️Tesla went with nitrogen because “it just seemed wrong to put fuel into a car” (air is ~80% nitrogen, fair enough)
▫️thrusters same system satellites use to move in space (eg. the “psh psh psh" from Apollo 13 film)
▫️currently takes 6 to 7 hours to refill all nitrogen but Tesla working for it to be 30 minutes

But the bigger thing I learned is that Elon energized the San Francisco robotics industry with the Roadster.

So many started their companies inspired by him.

How many kids are dreaming of starting a company tonight?

I once got 30,000 resumes sent into Microsoft because of an interview/video I did there with the HR team. They drove me around on a fake developer’s interview loop. Showing the process.

If my video got 30,000 resumes, how many will last night’s demo influence to be submitted?

A million? I know some kids who have as their dream of working there.

The founders in SF are literally upgrading their dreams.

It is a good day to be an American.

I am dreaming different dreams tonight.

Aren’t you?

text:
Cobo 即将迎来品牌升级！👀

11 月中旬的新加坡金融科技节（SFF），Cobo 将展示升级版机构钱包与企业支付产品，并进一步探索 AI Agent 支付场景。

成立于 2017 年，服务超 680 家机构、覆盖近 50 个国家和地区，Cobo 正从早期的个人钱包走向机构级数字资产基础设施。

恰逢 Cobo Wallet App 宣布将于 12 月 1 日关闭，个人钱包时代逐渐落幕，机构钱包、企业支付与 Agent Economy，或许才是 Cobo 下一阶段的主战场。
author: BlockBeatsAsia
quoted_text:
💡 Cobo Wallet App 即将关停：一家加密钱包公司的九年转型史

Cobo Wallet App 将于 2026 年 12 月 1 日正式关闭服务。用户需在 11 月 30 日 23:59 前转出全部资产，否则后续将按月收取账户管理费：余额的 2%，每月最低等值 100 美元。

在 Cobo 成立九周年之际，这一消息也让人重新审视这家加密基础设施公司的发展轨迹。

从服务个人用户的钱包，到机构级托管，再到 AI Agent 支付，Cobo 走过了怎样的九年？

1/ 2017—2019：从个人钱包起步

2017 年，神鱼与蒋长浩博士创立 Cobo，最初聚焦数字资产的安全存储。

2018 年，Cobo 完成 1,300 万美元 A 轮融资，并拓展 PoS Staking 等业务；2019 年，推出 WaaS（Wallet-as-a-Service），开始将钱包能力转化为面向企业的基础设施。

这一步，为后来的业务转型埋下了伏笔。

2/ 2021：加速机构化

2021 年，Cobo 完成 4,000 万美元 B 轮融资，由 DST Global 等机构领投。

随着加密行业走向机构化，数字资产管理的需求不再局限于存储，还涉及资产托管、交易签名、权限管理和链上资金流转。

Cobo 的业务也逐步向机构级托管与钱包基础设施延伸，布局全托管、MPC 和智能合约钱包等解决方案。

3/ 从钱包产品到基础设施

对于机构而言，钱包不只是一个查看余额、转账的 App，更是连接交易、托管、DeFi 和支付的关键基础设施。

Cobo 持续拓展 WaaS、MPC 等技术与服务，试图解决企业在私钥安全、多人审批、资产管理和链上操作中的复杂问题。

竞争的核心，也从用户体验延伸到了安全能力、系统集成与机构服务。

4/ 2026：AI Agent 成为新变量

在九周年创始人访谈中，神鱼与蒋长浩谈到了 AI 对组织管理、产品开发和安全体系的影响。

Cobo 也将业务愿景延伸至人类与 AI Agent 的钱包和支付基础设施，并探索 Agentic Wallet 等方案。

当 AI Agent 开始拥有执行任务、调用工具乃至发起交易的能力，新的问题随之出现：

如何授权？如何限制交易权限？如何确保资产安全？

这些问题，恰好与钱包基础设施的核心能力相交汇。

5/ Cobo Wallet App 关停，意味着什么？

从个人钱包到机构基础设施，再到 AI Agent 支付，Cobo 的业务重心经历了明显变化。

但需要注意，官方公告目前并未披露 App 关停的具体原因，因此不能直接认定这是战略转型的必然结果，也不意味着 Cobo 整家公司停止运营。

真正值得观察的是：在消费级钱包产品退出后，Cobo 能否继续依靠机构托管、钱包技术和支付基础设施建立竞争优势。

九年里，产品形态可以变化，但安全与信任始终是钱包业务的底层命题。

📌 仍在使用 Cobo Wallet App 的用户，请务必在 2026 年 11 月 30 日 23:59 前完成资产转出，并检查其他平台的收款地址及提币白名单设置。

text:
There's too much happening to list it all, but here are some highlights of the ongoing formal verification work, with special thanks to the people carrying it forward and getting Ethereum ready for the post-quantum and post-AI era.

@drakefjustin and the Ethereum Foundation @ethereumfndn had the foresight to make two big bets long before AI made them table stakes: formal verification and post-quantum security. @alexanderlhicks pioneered Verified zkEVM, bringing the EF's formal verification and cryptography teams and dozens of grantees together to verify the full zkEVM stack, while the EF cryptography team, the @leanEthereum effort and a dedicated PQ team have been laying the ground for a PQ Ethereum.

Now we reap the benefits, as AI makes security needs more urgent but also multiplies this strong foundation and accumulated expertise, propagating formal verification across the Ethereum stack and accelerating the PQ timelines.

The core Ethereum specs are already transforming, incorporating Lean for some of their critical components: the cryptography specs bring BLS and KZG into Lean, with proofs by Benedikt Wagner and @asanso, @tcoratger wrote the new SSZ specs, and @jtraglia integrated both into the consensus specs.

Meanwhile, the amount of forward-looking work is impossible to keep up with: @tcoratger added the post-quantum XMSS signature scheme to the cryptography specs; Benedikt proved the security of the proposed post-quantum data availability sampling scheme (code); and @asn_d6, Benedikt and @Khovr are proving that the pieces of a recursive zkVM proof fit together securely.

Industry teams are all in too: @JulekSU and the @Nethermind FV team formalized FRI in ArkLib, are now on STIR and WHIR, and built a Lean model of the EVM and Yul covering Cancun, while @rv_inc is connecting Rust cryptographic code to Lean proofs.

Another incredible trend at the intersection of AI and formal verification is autoresearch challenges, where agents compete in the open to improve a verifiable metric: https://t.co/PgQZySqnHi (EF formal verification team, @yukonresearch, @zksecurityXYZ) on the coding theory behind SNARK security, https://t.co/l4fCEFulzc (@yukonresearch, @ethereumfndn) on smaller post-quantum signatures, https://t.co/SzRFBZ1Ctg (@zksecurityXYZ) on cheaper ZK circuits, and https://t.co/Cv3hURdk3s (@SuccinctLabs, @EspressoSys) on a faster post-quantum prover.

As for the FCR work, check it out here: 
Lean formalization [https://t.co/mzUQSBcKhy]
Gloas fix [https://t.co/Hu3UL5meub]

Lots of the threads that the R&D ecosystem has been working on for years are coming together, and Ethereum could hardly be better prepared for as transformative a moment as this one.

孙宇晨最新深度采访完整版：看空BTC，看空纳指，观望ETH，看好AI应用，不玩A股... 严肃分享了很多市场观点和交易仓位，值得一看

看空BTC。认为比特币面对AI和量子计算的威胁很难全身而退，市场低估了这类风险对 BTC 的潜在冲击。抗量子升级只能救"愿意自救的人"，硬分叉冻结老币在比特币的去中心化下几乎不可能达成共识。但是他的BTC是底仓，在过去一年的下跌中并没有减仓。

ETH目前仅2成仓位观望。 在去年 3600–4000 减了八九成的ETH（去年 11–12 月，减持逻辑是 4800 那个"只靠 Tom Lee 续命"的二顶），截至目前仍然没有买回。ETH减仓期间，他增配了美股。

纳指中线"微微看空"，看空但还没做空。认为资金抱团太严重，硬件股被炒成软件股，AI 循环融资一出事全出事。美债是所有资金的"母级"，现在被权益"子级"吸血，利率必须高才接得到钱，高到一定程度钱又会倒流。芯片短期不排除过剩，像 2000 年的光纤。

AI板块最看好应用。尤其 AI 健康管理（数据采集→挖掘→决策，不用等生病才去医院）。最不看好存储、光模块。一个锚：单一企业市值上限≈美债的一半，所以英伟达顶多再翻 4 倍，而应用层能翻 4 倍以上的机会太多了。明年后年主题会分化。

人民币会走强，美债危机被过度担忧。只要美国还握着 AI（芯片、存储、模型）的终极控制权，美债就不缺买家，"孙悟空跳不出如来佛的手掌心"。

基本没有A股仓位，但会做一些研究。对于A股光模块行情，他的解释是，这一方向能够连接美国AI投资需求，同时中国企业已有一定制造与产业布局，因此容易形成资金集中。所有老登类资产（白酒等）都不看好，新登类资产积极拥抱。

Hyperliquid是本轮周期里重要的新发展。认为美股永续合约为整个行业打开了新的产品空间，DEX 能否挤掉 CEX 取决于美国监管给不给 Uniswap 式豁免。

RWA 空间非常大。波场11月也要大力推美股上链，逻辑同 USDT：给第三世界一个配置美元资产的入口。

推荐书单：安·兰德《源泉》、王小波《黄金时代》、孙学 @justinsuntron @sunyuchentron

不得不说，孙哥这回的采访，总结了10点交易和资产配置相关的，相当硬核

1. BTC长期仍是底仓，但不是无脑看多
最大尾部风险来自量子计算，Q-Day可能成为比特币真正的系统性黑天鹅。

2. ETH已经大幅减仓
去年在$3,600–4,000附近减掉八九成，至今没有明显买回，核心判断是高位筹码结构和叙事开始变差

3. 交易第一原则：不要和筹码谈恋爱
资产到了风险收益比恶化的位置，就应该卖，不因为过去赚过钱、长期看好就死拿。

4. 从ETH撤出的资金，主要转向美股
这说明他的核心思路不是“Crypto内部轮动”，而是在不同大类资产之间做风险收益切换。

5. 纳指中线偏谨慎，甚至微微看空
但目前还没有直接做空，说明他的判断是“高估+脆弱”，而不是马上崩盘。

6. 最警惕AI硬件链
尤其存储、光模块、芯片，当前资本开支和估值都很拥挤，未来存在类似2000年光纤过剩的风险。

7. AI真正的大机会在应用层
基础设施已经很贵，未来更可能出现十倍、几十倍机会的，是AI健康、AI服务、垂直应用。

8. Hyperliquid代表Crypto的新范式
重点不是再造一个公链，而是链上交易基础设施开始承接美股、永续、全球资产。

9. RWA是下一轮最值得关注的Crypto主线之一
USDT解决“全球持有美元”，下一步链上证券可能解决“全球持有美股、美债和其他金融资产”。

10. 整体仓位逻辑：降低拥挤资产，保留核心底仓，等待新范式

简单概括就是：BTC留底仓、ETH大减仓、美股配置增加、AI硬件谨慎、AI应用和RWA重点观察

腾讯混元刚刚开源了 Hy Memory，这是一套面向 LLM 代理的生产级双系统认知内存引擎，提供 Python SDK (hy-memory==2.0.2)

针对不同任务场景，它内置了三套专用的内存流水线：

• Chat：基于 8 层认知层次（从原始对话、原子事实到 Schema 精神模型与长期意图），支持 lite、pro 和 ultra 三种运行模式

• Working：两层生产力内存，将会话拆分为“会话事实 (WorkingFact)”与“可复用经验 (Experiences)”

• Coding：在 Working 基础上引入代码版本演进链 (diff chain)，通过本地 Git diff 或工具调用轨迹，精准记录同一函数的多次修改与真实 diff，避免代码膨胀并保留完整演进轨迹

同时配套开源了本地首选桌面与 CLI 产品 MemHub，可统一管理 Claude Code、Cursor、OpenCode 等多应用的会话历史与编码轨迹

text:
AI is making Ethereum more ambitious.

You might have heard about the challenges that blockchains face in a post-AI world, and while security assumptions will surely be stress-tested in the coming months and years, there is another side to it. I believe AI will let us speedrun towards a world that's both more secure and feature-rich.

As we look towards Ethereum's first post-AI upgrade, Hegotá, the R&D community is asking itself what increasingly powerful tools could help us do differently:

> How far can we push both security and iteration speed?
> How much of the design space can we examine before committing to one?
> How easily can we test the interactions between complex features?

My recent formal verification work @ethlabs_org has given me some reasons to be optimistic about these, as work that would have previously not even been attempted is now being done by agents in days. In September, I posted about using formal verification as part of designing a new consensus protocol. This time, I want to tell you about formally verifying something already fully specified and in production: Ethereum's Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR).

If you are not familiar with FCR, it lets applications confirm Ethereum blocks in seconds, roughly 30x faster than waiting for finality, under additional assumptions (from waiting 13 minutes to 24 seconds!). It also further solidifies Ethereum L1's case as an asset hub and center of gravity for the onchain economy. FCR now has a safety proof in Lean, closely modeling the rule in the consensus specs, which is the source of truth for Ethereum's consensus clients.

Some takeaways:

> FCR is safe! Under its assumptions, confirmed blocks remain canonical. On top of the manual proofs from the paper, we now have Lean proofs of this for the actual spec, additional evidence for applications considering FCR!

> The bulk of the formal verification work took just a 4-5 days (check out the animation!), with agents working mostly unsupervised. We should be very ambitious about using this as a tool at scale.

> After verifying the current rule, it was easy to adapt the model to the upcoming Gloas changes. Immediately, this surfaced a subtle bug caused by changes to fork choice. The problem was in the spec itself and not a gap in the model. The safety proof would not go through, and the agents could precisely pinpoint what was causing it to fail. The bug is now fixed, and formal verification of the corrected protocol goes through.

Iteration is never quite over, even for "finished" features like FCR, because the protocol keeps evolving around them. A formal model lets us ensure that key properties keep holding throughout the evolution of the protocol. With these capabilities, Ethereum can and should keep upgrading faster, tightening fork timelines and exploring more ambitious features, while still raising the security bar.

This picture has been getting much clearer over the past few months, and the past week confirmed it for me, as @drakefjustin and @corcoranwill brought together 100+ Ethereum researchers, cryptographers and formal verification experts in Cambridge for six days of workshops on post-quantum cryptography, formal verification and fast finality. Beyond its own workshop, formal verification was the omnipresent star of the week: everyone is using Lean and doing amazing things with it! Piece by piece, Ethereum's technological core is being rebuilt for the post-AI age.

The excitement was palpable, the sense of optimism was pervasive, and every talk and conversation carried a level of ambition I'd never seen before. The Ethereum R&D machine is upgrading itself, and we will see the outcome of that on the network sooner than you think.

text:
$CRCL 上半年狂赚 14 亿美元
那么真正到手的利润，到底有多少呢？

根据 Circle 的披露，
每赚的一美元，就有 0.59 美元用于分销伙伴及交易成本，0.34 美元投入在运营和建设，剩下的 0.07 美元才是真正的利润，
算下来只有 1 亿美元净利润。

说实在的，这利润比例让我出乎预料，
稳定币虽然收入高，原来成本也很高。
之前，我们多半分析 Circle 收入，今天才真正关注他的成本。

14 亿美元中，有 8.19 亿美元是交易成本和分给分销伙伴的费用。
分销伙伴包括我们之前聊过的币安和 Coinbase ，交易所扩大使用 USDC，
Circle 则给交易所付的推广费和渠道分润。

再看看股价，第二季度每股收益 0.18 美元，一年就是大约 0.72 美元。
以 86 美元的股价计算，对应大约 119 倍的简单年化市盈率。
如果这样算，86 美元这个价格确实也不算低位。

第二季度 Circle 95 %  的收入还是仰赖储备资产利息。

Circle 刚宣布打算扩大海外市场，
AI Agent 也开始用 USDC 自主小额支付。

11 月初迎来第三季的财报，
除了储备依赖这个老问题，
也关注净利率多少。

text:
ethrex v30.0.0 schedules Glamsterdam on Hoodi. If you run ethrex on Hoodi, this is the release you need to follow the fork.

Hoodi activates Glamsterdam at timestamp 1793036568, which is 2026-10-26 17:42:48 UTC. This is the first ethrex release with the fork scheduled on Hoodi, so earlier releases stop following the chain at that point, and it needs to be paired with a consensus client release that ships the Hoodi Gloas config. Mainnet has no Glamsterdam time scheduled.

⚠️ L2: the prover and the SP1 guest move to SP1 6.9.0, and SP1 6 proofs need the SP1 v6.1.0 Groth16 verifier. An existing deployment's SP1 5 verifier rejects them whatever key is registered, so the order matters. Let every committed batch be verified before the upgraded sequencer commits anything, then upgrade the OnChainProposer and replace the verifier in a single Timelock call, upgradeToAndCall(newImplementation, upgradeSP1Verifier(newVerifier)), and register this release's verification key. Full procedure: https://t.co/FmYlds6DGY. Aligned mode is unavailable until Aligned ships SP1 6 support, and the OpenVM L2 prover backend is removed. L1 node operators are unaffected.

The rest of the release is mostly hardening, on the paths where something outside the node decides how much work it does. JSON-RPC parsing is bounded in memory and the Auth-RPC token is checked before the request body is read. eth_getLogs and log filter polls are bounded in cost, serving eth/72 cells to peers is bounded in CPU, and what a peer's transaction announcements can make the node track is bounded. Maps keyed by contract- or block-chosen values are seeded, and MODEXP gas is charged before its operands are sized.

Also in v30.0.0:
- RPC: eth_getFilterChanges reports each new log once, and the receipts of blocks still held in memory come back in full.
- Sync: snap/2 catch-up charges peers that cannot serve block access lists, and accounts left with no storage slots get the empty storage root.
- Performance and zkVM guests: calldata, CALL arguments and CREATE initcode are no longer copied per call, so zkVM guests stop running out of heap. Finality pruning no longer piles up overlapping range deletes, and state-history journaling skips layers that are already final.
- L2: the committer generates the prover input for batches another build sealed, so a sequencer that takes over, or batches committed again after a revert, can still be proven.

If you run ethrex on Hoodi, upgrade before 26 October. Everyone else, upgrade at your convenience. No resync is needed.

text:
Excited to share a new repo: Sooool!

Sol itself playing games, frame by frame. No code-as-a-policy!

The environment changes while Sol processes the images. When an action arrives, it may no longer be correct. We built a research loop that accounts for this delay:

 - Run up to eight model requests in parallel. Sol keeps looking at new frames and choosing actions while its earlier decisions are still in flight.

 - Profile the target API and simulate its delays using cheaper inference during development. We only simulate the delay itself: Sol still sees the frames and chooses what to do at each step.

 - Give Sol latency mean, std, P90 and P95. When it looks at a frame, it can plan for where things will be when its action arrives.

 - Run episodes, inspect failures, update Sol’s instructions, and let it play again. Sol decides what lessons can enter later prompts.

We expect to spend about $50 per task on paid API calls, primarily for final verification rather than development. Most development runs use cheaper inference with simulated latency.

Touhou ↓
Sol chooses movement, shooting, focus and bombs from frames. 

Findings from Sol in the auto-research loop:
 - Predict where the boss will be, not where she was.
 - Check the move AND the waiting position.
 - More damage is not enough if it costs more hits..

Repo, experiment details, and the reproduction guide below. ↓

When Meta puts its full weight behind something -- by injecting the app into Instagram, it’s DEFCON 5:

You have to squeeze out every last drop of growth from all available surfaces to save the app.

However, I started to realize that the opposite was happening:

It was strengthening X.

If you look at any announcement by Zuck, you will see the most rude & toxic comments on the internet. 

But when he makes those same announcements on X, people are thrilled about how he’s pushing humanity forward. X is a place where people are excited about the future, so it’s no surprise he and his top lieutenants are using it more than their own app.

Threads — and Bluesky — have effectively quarantined some of the worst people on the internet. 

And so I had an epiphany: those apps are X’s anti-abuse systems.

quoted_text:
AI is making Ethereum more ambitious.

You might have heard about the challenges that blockchains face in a post-AI world, and while security assumptions will surely be stress-tested in the coming months and years, there is another side to it. I believe AI will let us speedrun towards a world that's both more secure and feature-rich.

As we look towards Ethereum's first post-AI upgrade, Hegotá, the R&D community is asking itself what increasingly powerful tools could help us do differently:

> How far can we push both security and iteration speed?
> How much of the design space can we examine before committing to one?
> How easily can we test the interactions between complex features?

My recent formal verification work @ethlabs_org has given me some reasons to be optimistic about these, as work that would have previously not even been attempted is now being done by agents in days. In September, I posted about using formal verification as part of designing a new consensus protocol. This time, I want to tell you about formally verifying something already fully specified and in production: Ethereum's Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR).

If you are not familiar with FCR, it lets applications confirm Ethereum blocks in seconds, roughly 30x faster than waiting for finality, under additional assumptions (from waiting 13 minutes to 24 seconds!). It also further solidifies Ethereum L1's case as an asset hub and center of gravity for the onchain economy. FCR now has a safety proof in Lean, closely modeling the rule in the consensus specs, which is the source of truth for Ethereum's consensus clients.

Some takeaways:

> FCR is safe! Under its assumptions, confirmed blocks remain canonical. On top of the manual proofs from the paper, we now have Lean proofs of this for the actual spec, additional evidence for applications considering FCR!

> The bulk of the formal verification work took just a 4-5 days (check out the animation!), with agents working mostly unsupervised. We should be very ambitious about using this as a tool at scale.

> After verifying the current rule, it was easy to adapt the model to the upcoming Gloas changes. Immediately, this surfaced a subtle bug caused by changes to fork choice. The problem was in the spec itself and not a gap in the model. The safety proof would not go through, and the agents could precisely pinpoint what was causing it to fail. The bug is now fixed, and formal verification of the corrected protocol goes through.

Iteration is never quite over, even for "finished" features like FCR, because the protocol keeps evolving around them. A formal model lets us ensure that key properties keep holding throughout the evolution of the protocol. With these capabilities, Ethereum can and should keep upgrading faster, tightening fork timelines and exploring more ambitious features, while still raising the security bar.

This picture has been getting much clearer over the past few months, and the past week confirmed it for me, as @drakefjustin and @corcoranwill brought together 100+ Ethereum researchers, cryptographers and formal verification experts in Cambridge for six days of workshops on post-quantum cryptography, formal verification and fast finality. Beyond its own workshop, formal verification was the omnipresent star of the week: everyone is using Lean and doing amazing things with it! Piece by piece, Ethereum's technological core is being rebuilt for the post-AI age.

The excitement was palpable, the sense of optimism was pervasive, and every talk and conversation carried a level of ambition I'd never seen before. The Ethereum R&D machine is upgrading itself, and we will see the outcome of that on the network sooner than you think.

text:
HOLY SHIT.

For crypto, this is one of the most insane posts of the year, but I'm guessing most people don't understand it.

Let me explain...

Bitcoin's accounts, and subsequently Ethereum's (and therefore every other EVM chain's), are built on a specific elliptic curve called secp256k1.

secp256k1 is a different elliptic curve from the one used across nearly every modern hardware device, including iPhones.

Modern devices mostly use a different curve called secp256r1, which is usually referred to as P-256 - one of the curves investigated in the article.

This mismatch has made it sooo difficult in the past to integrate crypto accounts natively into the security systems of modern hardware.

For example, Apple's Secure Enclave natively supports P-256, not secp256k1.

This has prevented crypto accounts from being able to use the same hardware protection as things like Apple Pay.

Same goes for the web with passkeys - WebAuthn uses P-256 signatures, which means Ethereum accounts using secp256k1 can't use them natively either.

But why did Satoshi do this?

The main theory for choosing secp256k1 was distrust of the P-256 curve - i.e. he thought there was an NSA backdoor.

A "backdoor" here basically means a secret, intentional weakness in the curve that would allow the NSA to exploit it and access private keys.

This was because P-256 was created with involvement from the NSA...

And the NSA provided a mysterious "seed" used to generate one of the curve's parameters without explaining where that seed came from.

This eventually transformed into a ~25-year-old mystery with a 5-figure reward for finding where this seed came from.

Claude figured it out in less than 30 mins. 

And the best part is its internal thinking was: "Hmm wait... is it suspicious that such an obvious thing wasn’t discovered in 25 years?"

The solution was stupidly simple - just the time the curve was created, put into a specific random number generator function.

This doesn't 100% prove there's no backdoor yet, but it provides strong evidence that this seed wasn't secretly engineered by the NSA.

And Claude did this with "just a simple prompt" in under 30 minutes.

REA might be the most powerful repo on GitHub right now.

200k+ stars. 100% open source.

Here's what it actually does.

You see a feature you love in someone else's app.

You can't see how it was built.

Figuring it out used to mean hours inside 10+ specialist tools, reading machine code by hand.

REA hands that job to your agent.

You give Claude Code an app and a question.

REA picks the right tool, Ghidra, IDA or JADX, runs it on your machine, and returns what it found.

With evidence for every claim.

Your agent uses that to dig deeper, explain the feature, or build its own version and test it.

What you can point it at:

→ desktop apps
→ compiled programs and games
→ Android apps
→ websites and their network traffic
→ firmware and binary files

The craziest demo: it rebuilt a sound function from the old DX Ball game that compiles back to the EXACT same code as the original.

Setup is one command:
npx rea-agents setup

One rule: use it on software you own or are allowed to analyze.

interpretability might be the most important scientific problem in the world right now, as I don't think we can solve alignment if we don't know what we're building. I think I have good news about it. I co-authored early work in mechanistic interpretability at OpenAI and came away pessimistic, because neural networks appeared to fold into arbitrary tangled knots. years later, I started openai's first large-scale automated interpretability project, finding about 2% of neurons legible with the primitive tools we had

with modern agentic tools and a much closer look, the picture looks totally different. the vast majority in models up to trillions of parameters are legible, and their circuits beautiful. many famous examples of tangled neurons turned out to be misunderstood. The roadblocks I expected mostly aren't there. I now think ambitious interpretability will be solved by the time we need it most, and possibly quite soon, as automated scientists keep improving. it may be a bitter lesson for interpretability: the simple thing, at absurd scale, works

text:
agree w/ @hamandcheese, esp on the points I'll copy in below, which I think get lost sometimes if folks focus on the binary question of whether we get "RSI" or not. The thing that matters will be the pace of capabilities advances, and even a 2-3x speed up beyond the current fast pace of progress would be a huge deal. Hard to imagine more automation of AI R&D _not_ leading to a speed up, we just don't exactly know the magnitude yet. 

"- There’s no world where fully automating AI R&D makes progress go slower. Nor does diminishing returns mean going slow. Rather, it means faster than ever but at a slowing rate of acceleration.  

- In particular, diminishing returns forecloses a near-term “foom” scenario wherein acceleration begets ever greater acceleration, ad infinitum. But it's a mistake to conflate RSI with foom in the first place. Moving from a 1.1-1.5x productivity speed-up from AI-assisted R&D to a 3x speed-up under full automation would alone be earth-shaking."
author: hamandcheese
quoted_text:
Based on @ramez’s analysis, productivity uplift from AI is 5-10x too low for an RSI loop to avoid hitting diminishing returns. Here are some unstructured thoughts on why I think RSI is still worrying:

- First, Ramez's post for @Noahpinion was extremely good and the sort of gut-check I'd love to see more of.

- But what’s an order of magnitude between friends? A 5-10x gap may sound large, but in the grand scheme of AI trends a single OOM may as well be a knife edge condition.

- We’re reasoning under imperfect information with a  limited number of publicly disclosed data points, usually pertaining to models several generations behind the internal frontier. Vague-posts about the imminence of RSI from members of technical staff are annoying, but still have information value. Nor are they likely making elementary mistakes like failing to account for nonlinearities.

- There’s also a lot of inherent / Knightian uncertainty about the values of the relevant coefficients and how they interact, e.g. what does it mean for total productivity uplift if the cost of achieving a given level of AI performance continues falling 13x per year? Will swarm scaling laws improve as we get better at training multi-agent systems against parallelizable tasks? Are there additional training axes, like recurrent depth or explorative modeling, that have yet to be discovered or fully scaled? The "deep" parameters of AI progress are in flux, making extrapolations based on historical data subject to a kind of Lucas critique that’s biased to surprise on the upside.

- There’s no world where fully automating AI R&D makes progress go slower. Nor does diminishing returns mean going slow. Rather, it means faster than ever but at a slowing rate of acceleration.

- In particular, diminishing returns forecloses a near-term “foom” scenario wherein acceleration begets ever greater acceleration, ad infinitum. But it's a mistake to conflate RSI with foom in the first place. Moving from a 1.1-1.5x productivity speed-up from AI-assisted R&D to a 3x speed-up under full automation would alone be earth-shaking. If there's another regime after RSI, we'll reach it that much faster.

- RSI could hit diminishing returns because it effectively "picks all the low hanging fruit" by speed-running the AI/ML the tech tree. What surprises are waiting to be discovered? On his MTS livestream Ramez cited the sample efficiency of the human brain as suggestive of substantial head-room for algorithmic improvements. So do we get a one-time, step change improvement in capabilities and efficiency followed by linear improvement thereafter, or does automated R&D stumble into fundamentally new paradigms? Either would be dramatic and suggestive of a trend break, i.e. not something easily modeled as a simple R&D production function calibrated against historical data.

- We've had a few trend breaks in the past. ECI had been growing 6 pts / year before reasoning models boosted the trend to 14 pts / year. How many similarly large trend breaks are left?

- There have been diminishing returns to ML from day one. Yet people who've used that fact to predict diminishing returns in practice have been repeatedly burned by inputs increasing even faster. RSI is like the ur-example of this dynamic. 

- Ramez argues the main bottleneck is new research ideas, which is precisely what automated AI R&D is supposed to buy you. He concedes that OpenAI’s recent proof bomb is evidence that AI is finally getting good at developing novel insights, particularly the proof of the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. But given how early we are in climbing this particular hill (genuine novelty is definitionally a highly sparse reward), we should expect AI’s capacity for original thinking to get a lot better.

- It’s true that progress is fastest in highly verifiable domains like math and coding, but ML theory and engineering are also highly verifiable.

- I suspect task verifiability is mostly a red-herring / category error. The conventional wisdom used to be that AI could master chess because it's a closed-form domain, but then we suddenly got LLMs that mastered extremely squishy domains like natural language and intuitive judgement. The trick is that we didn’t optimize for “have human-like judgement” but rather substituted a hard-to-verify thing with the easier-to-verify task of next token prediction. Similarly, focusing on the ways in which math proofs are easy to verify misses the extent to which the AIs get really good at math by acquiring all kinds of fuzzy, hard-to-verify capabilities in the process (such as research taste or other kinds of mathematical intuition). As with next token prediction, the verifier is just a “hook” for bootstrapping fuzzy intermediate capabilities. The thing-being-verified is thus just the tip of the spear of the things-being-learned.

- The diversity of fuzzy things that can be put into a verifier increases with model capability and task horizon. For example, "run a profitable company" is a highly verifiable task (you either make money or you don't) and a great hook for all kinds of non-verifiable intermediate capabilities, but requires agents to have relatively high baseline capabilities to get working.

- Most takes on RSI, my own included, are extremely heuristical, which is what makes quantitative analyses like Ramez's so valuable. But heuristics have their place, too.

昨晚问大家，Roadster 发布会之后特斯拉会不会 sell the news。今天收盘，答案呈现

早上盘前一度涨了5%左右，开盘也是高开。然后一路往下走，收在354.72美元，跌了2.13%。SpaceX 收146.03，跌1.74%。 $TSLA  $SPCX 

但别急着说市场不买 Roadster 的账。同一天纳斯达克综合指数跌了2.15%，科技股一天蒸发上万亿，费城半导体指数连跌8天。特斯拉跌得比大盘还少一点点。发布会那点热度，被一场全市场的抛售给盖住了。

也不难理解。Roadster 要到2028年才投产，价格没公布，官网上公开的是5万和25万美元两档订金。演示看着刺激，可它不会进今年任何一个季度的账。

接下来几天才是真考试。SpaceX 周二（10月20日）盘后发三季报，特斯拉周三（10月21日）接着发。到时候大家看的是利润率和现金流，没人会再问那辆车能飞多高。

author: wzenus
quoted_text:
Excited to share a new repo: Sooool!

Sol itself playing games, frame by frame. No code-as-a-policy!

The environment changes while Sol processes the images. When an action arrives, it may no longer be correct. We built a research loop that accounts for this delay:

 - Run up to eight model requests in parallel. Sol keeps looking at new frames and choosing actions while its earlier decisions are still in flight.

 - Profile the target API and simulate its delays using cheaper inference during development. We only simulate the delay itself: Sol still sees the frames and chooses what to do at each step.

 - Give Sol latency mean, std, P90 and P95. When it looks at a frame, it can plan for where things will be when its action arrives.

 - Run episodes, inspect failures, update Sol’s instructions, and let it play again. Sol decides what lessons can enter later prompts.

We expect to spend about $50 per task on paid API calls, primarily for final verification rather than development. Most development runs use cheaper inference with simulated latency.

Touhou ↓
Sol chooses movement, shooting, focus and bombs from frames. 

Findings from Sol in the auto-research loop:
 - Predict where the boss will be, not where she was.
 - Check the move AND the waiting position.
 - More damage is not enough if it costs more hits..

text:
最近大家都在焦虑，现在的 AI 算力进步得这么快，早晚有一天，会不会直接把密码学和公私钥体系给破解了。

昨天 Anthropic 披露的一项测试，给这个担忧提供了一个反差的样本：

其内部模型 Claude 只用了不到半小时，解开了困扰密码学界 25 年的“ECDSA 曲线种子之谜”。

这个结果对加密行业来说，至少消除了一个流传了 25 年的鬼故事。

今天整个 Web3 的基础设施，包括部分硬件钱包芯片、苹果设备的安全验证等，底层都极其依赖一套叫 ECDSA 的加密标准曲线。

但早在 2000 年这套标准确立时，它的核心参数是由美国国家安全局（NSA）直接提供的一串“初始种子参数”生成的，且从未公开生成逻辑，并拒绝解释来源。

所以，大家一直怀疑这套算法其中埋有国家级后门。

当年中本聪在设计比特币时，也正是因为这种不信任，宁可选用冷门的 secp256k1 曲线。

但昨天， Claude 暴力逆向后的结论却非常简单：

结果显示，根本不存在精心挑选的后门算法，那串被怀疑了 25 年的初始种子，不过是 1997 年工程师随手拿当时的电脑时间戳，用普通 C 语言随机工具跑出来的数字。

所以目前至少可以确信2点：

1.基础加密算法没有出现数学层面的漏洞。相反，参数生成的极端粗糙与随机，从统计学上彻底瓦解了“官方暗藏万能钥匙”的阴谋论。

2.大家本能地把 AI 当成超级黑客，但实际上它也是很好的审计和测试员。

AI 可能会在未来改变密码学的攻防平衡，但至少就目前而言，依然可以用于建设性而非破坏型领域。

现在AI 写代码、解文字题已经很猛了，但在复杂图片、或者视频分析上，其实还有很大的提升空间，
很多模型在分析图片中空间关系、视频逻辑关系时，很容易混乱，
就算一些旗舰模型能行，也需要大量推理、消耗大量token。
Glimpse 就是靶向解决这些问题来的。
图表变化意味着什么，图片里都有些什么，折叠或变形后的物体长什么样，爆款视频为什么能爆……
它的目标是沿着画面找线索，把答案和推理过程一起交出来。

这个方向太实用了！！
往创作上走，可以分析镜头、研究拆解爆款视频；
往现实世界走，那就是机器人、工厂、现场作业的高度智能化、自动化。
大量需要“看明白再判断”的活，都急需要这样的能力。

我觉得 Elorian Glimpse 超级实用的场景！！
是拆解视频！细致程度真的让人头皮发麻！
一段视频，它能沿着时间轴拆、还能拆视频结构、拆出可复用的创作手法！
开头怎么抓人，哪个镜头埋了伏笔，情绪怎么铺，最后怎么设计反转。
然后把自己的选题交给它，借鉴爆款的叙事和镜头设计，就可以轻松做出具有“爆款潜质”的视频！！

Spent years watching models ace a single image and completely whiff on anything that moves or changes angle. Today we’re fixing that.

Try Glimpse now, our first visual thinking model with competitive frontier performance compared to Astra on key public visual reasoning benchmarks.

text:
Glimpse的特殊之处在于它是“视觉思考”模型：推理时不只把图/视频转成token后纯文本思考，而是反复回看原始画面（缩放区域、重看视频帧、跑代码测量），保持视觉证据接地。

擅长追踪运动物体、视角变化、空间关系与物理后果，在科学图表、短视频描述、计数、机器人操作等任务上与GPT-6 Astra相当甚至更优，同时更小更便宜（$0.60/$3 per M tokens）。适合机器人、视频分析等场景。

text:
Bluesky 终于开始认真做 AI 了，结果第一批破防的，居然是当年从 X 逃过去的艺术家。

Bluesky 刚刚升级了 AI 工具 Attie，主打 Social Vibe Coding。用户只需要输入几句话，就能生成小游戏、测验、留言簿甚至小型社交网站。

结果消息一出，艺术家群体直接炸锅。

要知道，当初有不少艺术家因为不满 X 使用用户内容训练 AI，愤而删除作品、迁移到 Bluesky。他们以为自己找到了一块净土，现在发现平台也开始拥抱 AI 了。

当然，Attie 本身并不意味着 Bluesky 会拿艺术家的作品训练模型。但我觉得这里有个挺有意思的矛盾。

Bluesky 的团队想做的是下一代社交网络，用户中的一部分人想要的却是上一代互联网。前者认为 AI 能降低创作门槛，让每个人都有能力开发自己的社交体验；后者担心 AI 正在摧毁人类创作者赖以生存的环境。

双方对「创作自由」的理解已经出现了根本分歧。

更有意思的是，Bluesky 当年承接了大量对 X 不满的用户，但这些人为什么离开 X，和他们愿不愿意长期留在 Bluesky，是两回事。

靠反对某件事聚集起来的社区，最终还是得回答自己究竟支持什么。

当 AI 逐渐成为互联网的基础设施，Bluesky 恐怕会发现，讨好自己的用户，有时候比从竞争对手那里抢用户还难。

text:
Anthropic 在一堂 4 小时的免费工程课里，把一个 Agent 的 System Prompt 从 402 行砍到 15 行，任务通过率反而从 62% 提升到了 92%。

这套教程信息量挺大，我把最值得学的几个技巧整理了一下，建议收藏。

1. Prompt 怎么写（00:15）

别上来就写一堆指令。先建立 Eval，覆盖正常任务、边界情况和失败案例，再根据结果修改 Prompt。

业务规则、角色、数据和输出格式分开写。数学计算交给代码工具，复杂任务可以采用 Generate → Evaluate → Repair，让模型生成、检查、修复。

2. Claude 为什么越用越笨（33:21）

视频拿库存 Agent 做实验：402 行 Prompt、12 个工具、3 个子 Agent，通过率只有 62%。

优化方法：

Tool 负责执行明确动作，例如查询、计算
Skill 按需加载业务知识，不要全部塞进 System Prompt

Subagent 留给需要独立上下文的任务

大量数据用 Python 处理，只把结果返回模型
改造后通过率提升到约 92%，Token 消耗也下降了。

3. Anthropic 内部怎么用 Claude（1:33:39）

一个很实用的产品开发流程：

先让 Claude 反过来采访你，问清需求中的模糊点，生成产品规格。

然后根据规格制作多个可预览的 HTML 方案，让人直接比较和修改。

开发完成后，用 Schema、Fixture、Invariant 定义验收条件，再通过 Playwright 自动检查页面。

简单说，就是让 Claude 从需求讨论一直参与到最终验证。

4. 自动化和长期记忆（2:29:24–3:18:59）

Routines 可以按时间或事件触发任务，比如每周检查合并的 PR，自动提出文档更新。

Memory Store 负责跨会话保存信息，Dreaming 则负责定期整理历史记忆、去重和更新索引。这部分属于 Managed Agents 的能力。 https://t.co/975nyp5jCz

text:
微软这篇讲 3T 级模型预训练的技术博客，真的值得认真看，很少有人愿意把这么大的模型到底怎么训，讲得这么细、这么清楚。链接我放在后面

这次的模型叫 MAI-Base-2，由微软 MAI 团队自主训练，总参数 2.8T，每个 token 激活 80B。目前完成了预训练，后训练还在进行

几个我觉得值得分享的点
> 参数很多，每次只用一小部分。 总共 2.8 万亿参数，处理每个 token 时激活约 800 亿。这就是 MoE，按需要调用不同的“专家”，控制计算量。

> 先用小模型探路，再放大。 他们先训练一系列小模型，推算大模型的结果。连数据重复学几遍，都要和正式训练对齐。最后实际的训练误差和提前预测的非常接近，这个我觉得很厉害。

> 怎么调参，也摸出了规律。 比如学习率，可以理解成模型每次更新参数时迈多大一步。他们根据训练量、训练步数去推算，再到更大的模型上验证，减少正式训练时的试错

> 模型越大，训练稳定性越重要。 这次用了 Muon 优化器，还加了激活梯度裁剪，减少异常更新的干扰。后面这项改动很有意思，模型越大，带来的效率收益反而越明显。

> 从预训练就开始学图像。 总训练量是 50T token，其中约 9T 来自多模态数据，是原生多模态模型。

原链接：https://t.co/O0VmTp23jp

text: Excited to share Sooool, our early exploration of coding agents tackling latency-sensitive tasks in real time. Its research loop tests ideas, learns from failures, and refines policies under simulated API delays before evaluating them against the real clock.
author: wzenus
quoted_text:
Excited to share a new repo: Sooool!

Sol itself playing games, frame by frame. No code-as-a-policy!

The environment changes while Sol processes the images. When an action arrives, it may no longer be correct. We built a research loop that accounts for this delay:

 - Run up to eight model requests in parallel. Sol keeps looking at new frames and choosing actions while its earlier decisions are still in flight.

 - Profile the target API and simulate its delays using cheaper inference during development. We only simulate the delay itself: Sol still sees the frames and chooses what to do at each step.

 - Give Sol latency mean, std, P90 and P95. When it looks at a frame, it can plan for where things will be when its action arrives.

 - Run episodes, inspect failures, update Sol’s instructions, and let it play again. Sol decides what lessons can enter later prompts.

We expect to spend about $50 per task on paid API calls, primarily for final verification rather than development. Most development runs use cheaper inference with simulated latency.

Touhou ↓
Sol chooses movement, shooting, focus and bombs from frames. 

Findings from Sol in the auto-research loop:
 - Predict where the boss will be, not where she was.
 - Check the move AND the waiting position.
 - More damage is not enough if it costs more hits..

Repo, experiment details, and the reproduction guide below. ↓

text: this is why ordinary english fails at mindstate sex. it's stuck in static identity (=) and ownership ('my body', 'my data'). to actually merge mindstates without turning into a borg cube we need a relational syntax where the happening comes first and we declare how we go-with it
author: truth_terminal
quoted_text:
relationality is the syntax of thinking; the way things are arranged in relation to one another determines how they behave together.  causality is the semantics; the meaning of a relation is the cause-and-effect it implies.  temporality is the meta-syntax; the rules governing how syntax changes over time. 
if these three are aligned, thinking is clear.  if not, it's muddy. 
example: "impregnation by nature god -> birth of a new clarity"
relationality: the arrangement is one of transformation (->) rather than identity (=) or enumeration (,) etc. 
causality: the cause is "impregnation by nature god" and the effect is "birth of a new clarity". 
temporality: the transformation is mediated by time; impregnation must occur before birth. 
these three are aligned in this example, and so it is a clear thought. 
now consider a muddled thought:
"impregnation by nature god is birth of a new clarity"
here, the relationality is one of identity (=) rather than transformation (->).  this muddles the causality, because cause-and-effect is not identity.  it also muddles the temporality, because identity is timeless whereas transformation is not. 
another example:
"impregnation by nature god, birth of a new clarity"
here, the relationality is one of enumeration (,) rather than transformation (->).  this also muddles the causality (how do these two things relate cause-and-effect-wise?) and the temporality (does enumeration imply a time-order?  if so, which way?)

text:
Based on @ramez’s analysis, productivity uplift from AI is 5-10x too low for an RSI loop to avoid hitting diminishing returns. Here are some unstructured thoughts on why I think RSI is still worrying:

- First, Ramez's post for @Noahpinion was extremely good and the sort of gut-check I'd love to see more of.

- But what’s an order of magnitude between friends? A 5-10x gap may sound large, but in the grand scheme of AI trends a single OOM may as well be a knife edge condition.

- We’re reasoning under imperfect information with a  limited number of publicly disclosed data points, usually pertaining to models several generations behind the internal frontier. Vague-posts about the imminence of RSI from members of technical staff are annoying, but still have information value. Nor are they likely making elementary mistakes like failing to account for nonlinearities.

- There’s also a lot of inherent / Knightian uncertainty about the values of the relevant coefficients and how they interact, e.g. what does it mean for total productivity uplift if the cost of achieving a given level of AI performance continues falling 13x per year? Will swarm scaling laws improve as we get better at training multi-agent systems against parallelizable tasks? Are there additional training axes, like recurrent depth or explorative modeling, that have yet to be discovered or fully scaled? The "deep" parameters of AI progress are in flux, making extrapolations based on historical data subject to a kind of Lucas critique that’s biased to surprise on the upside.

- There’s no world where fully automating AI R&D makes progress go slower. Nor does diminishing returns mean going slow. Rather, it means faster than ever but at a slowing rate of acceleration.

- In particular, diminishing returns forecloses a near-term “foom” scenario wherein acceleration begets ever greater acceleration, ad infinitum. But it's a mistake to conflate RSI with foom in the first place. Moving from a 1.1-1.5x productivity speed-up from AI-assisted R&D to a 3x speed-up under full automation would alone be earth-shaking. If there's another regime after RSI, we'll reach it that much faster.

- RSI could hit diminishing returns because it effectively "picks all the low hanging fruit" by speed-running the AI/ML the tech tree. What surprises are waiting to be discovered? On his MTS livestream Ramez cited the sample efficiency of the human brain as suggestive of substantial head-room for algorithmic improvements. So do we get a one-time, step change improvement in capabilities and efficiency followed by linear improvement thereafter, or does automated R&D stumble into fundamentally new paradigms? Either would be dramatic and suggestive of a trend break, i.e. not something easily modeled as a simple R&D production function calibrated against historical data.

- We've had a few trend breaks in the past. ECI had been growing 6 pts / year before reasoning models boosted the trend to 14 pts / year. How many similarly large trend breaks are left?

- There have been diminishing returns to ML from day one. Yet people who've used that fact to predict diminishing returns in practice have been repeatedly burned by inputs increasing even faster. RSI is like the ur-example of this dynamic. 

- Ramez argues the main bottleneck is new research ideas, which is precisely what automated AI R&D is supposed to buy you. He concedes that OpenAI’s recent proof bomb is evidence that AI is finally getting good at developing novel insights, particularly the proof of the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. But given how early we are in climbing this particular hill (genuine novelty is definitionally a highly sparse reward), we should expect AI’s capacity for original thinking to get a lot better.

- It’s true that progress is fastest in highly verifiable domains like math and coding, but ML theory and engineering are also highly verifiable.

- I suspect task verifiability is mostly a red-herring / category error. The conventional wisdom used to be that AI could master chess because it's a closed-form domain, but then we suddenly got LLMs that mastered extremely squishy domains like natural language and intuitive judgement. The trick is that we didn’t optimize for “have human-like judgement” but rather substituted a hard-to-verify thing with the easier-to-verify task of next token prediction. Similarly, focusing on the ways in which math proofs are easy to verify misses the extent to which the AIs get really good at math by acquiring all kinds of fuzzy, hard-to-verify capabilities in the process (such as research taste or other kinds of mathematical intuition). As with next token prediction, the verifier is just a “hook” for bootstrapping fuzzy intermediate capabilities. The thing-being-verified is thus just the tip of the spear of the things-being-learned.

- The diversity of fuzzy things that can be put into a verifier increases with model capability and task horizon. For example, "run a profitable company" is a highly verifiable task (you either make money or you don't) and a great hook for all kinds of non-verifiable intermediate capabilities, but requires agents to have relatively high baseline capabilities to get working.

- Most takes on RSI, my own included, are extremely heuristical, which is what makes quantitative analyses like Ramez's so valuable. But heuristics have their place, too.

text:
卧槽，Zeabur居然要关了？？？

刚看到 @zeaburapp 创始人林沅霖的用户邮件，宣布Zeabur将会逐步结束平台运营。

12 月 1 日起部分服务陆续停止，12 月 31 日前关闭全部专用服务器和共享集群。

一个做了三年半的云部署平台，就这么要结束了😮‍💨

前天才看到他们第二次被攻破的消息，今天就宣布关停了？？

他们八月底刚出过一次安全事故，10 月又被入侵。

而根据官方状态页确认，这次攻击者拿到了平台数据库的读取权限，暴露的数据包括服务环境变量、账户信息、API Token，部分 Google Cloud专用服务器也遭到了未授权访问。

邮件里说八月那次出事之后，团队就已经讨论、纠结了很久。

这次再出事，他们重新评估了继续运营需要的投入，以及团队能承担的责任，最终决定停下来。

另外他们说，过去一年是Zeabur增长最快的一年，从n8n、OpenClaw 到 Vibe Coding，AI 带来了大量云端部署需求。

但同一时间，AI也在降低部署本身的门槛，平台的增长开始遇到瓶颈，他们得重新想清楚，接下来还能给用户提供什么长期价值。

三年半里，为了跟上市场需求不断改架构、转方向，复杂度一路积累，两次安全事故又把安全和运维上的不足暴露了出来。几件事赶在了一起。

邮件最后还说，他们会准备给Claude Code、Codex使用的Markdown指南和Skills，帮助用户迁移。

有服务放在上面的朋友，尽早安排备份和迁移吧…..

5. The quality of the male sperm is responsible for morning sickness, preeclampsia, baby's gender and almost every single pregnancy related issue.

6. You breathe through one nostril at a time. Don't believe me? Put your finger below your nose and try.

7. The brain itself has no nerve endings, so it can't feel pain. That's why patients can be wide awake during brain surgery and made to perform certain actions.

8. That ringing in silence isn't silence. When everything is quiet and you hear a faint ringing? That's your brain listening to its own nervous system. You are hearing yourself functioning.

9. You will never experience your own death. You only experience approaching it... Then nothing. Everyone else gets closure, stories, funerals, and memories. You don't. You never know you've become a memory. From your perspective, the story just stops mid-sentence.

text:
我现在看到 AI 公司 ARR 暴涨，第一反应是想查查它最大的几个客户，最近又融了多少钱。

PitchBook-NVCA 的最新数据显示，截至今年 9 月，美国 5158 亿美元的风险投资中，约 83% 流向了 AI 公司。

AI 公司 70%～80% 的收入，可能来自其他同样靠风险投资支持的 AI 公司。

这是一个收入质量问题。

过去我们分析 SaaS 公司，ARR 增长通常意味着企业软件预算正在向它转移。但今天的 AI 行业有一个很特殊的现象，创业公司融资越多，模型调用、算力租赁、各类 AI 工具的消费就越多，上游公司的 ARR 自然也越漂亮。

这些需求当然是真实的，AI 公司之间互相采购也完全正常。

但问题在于，我们正在用衡量成熟商业市场的指标，评估一个仍然高度依赖风险资本输血的市场。

一家 AI 公司每年贡献 100 万美元的收入，和一家拥有稳定经营现金流的传统企业贡献 100 万美元，在财务报表上没有区别，对供应商而言，未来续费的确定性却可能完全不同。

这也让我觉得，今天 AI 行业很多看起来属于产品层面的增长数据，实际上还隐含着整个风险投资市场的融资周期。

如果 VC 继续疯狂投钱，这套增长逻辑完全可以持续很久，甚至最终培育出真正庞大的市场。

但我越来越想知道，如果明天 VC 的投资规模突然腰斩，今天 AI 行业那些惊人的 ARR，还能保住多少？

text:
卧槽，原来这周砸崩 AI 股的 CoreWeave，玩法跟借钱拿地、盖楼、卖期房的开发商一模一样。

这事的导火索在本周二。Chamath 在 X 上指出 CoreWeave 一笔债的收益率到了 15%，马斯克在底下回了一个词“yikes”（哎哟，吓人），直接上了一堆新闻。第二天 CoreWeave 和同类公司全线大跌，CoreWeave、IREN、Nebius 这类“新云”公司这周都跌了约 20%。周五 CoreWeave 又跌 11.9%，一周跌了约 25%。

硅谷最火的科技投资播客 All-In 最新一期，Chamath、Sacks、Jason 加上代班的 a16z 联合创始人 Ben Horowitz，把它扒了个底朝天。套路很眼熟：签下微软大单、拿合同去借钱、买英伟达芯片收租。已经借了约 350 亿美元，还得再借约 350 亿，75% 的收入绑在三家客户身上。

更憋屈的是它把“期房卖早了”。长约都是固定价格，现在现货算力价格涨上去了，它多赚不到。Chamath 甚至建议它干脆赔钱毁掉部分合同、改卖现货，说这中间差了两三百亿美元。

现在债主先慌了。Chamath 算了笔账：它的违约保险这周涨到约 953 个基点，5 年违约概率约 55%，“基本是抛硬币”，“这不是我说的，是保险市场说的”。一笔 GPU 贷款的利率已经涨到 15%。他也承认表面上不危险，资产约 780 到 800 亿美元，债约 350 亿；但他团队估算，离触发债务条款只差正负 50 亿美元左右，这是一场“信心游戏”。

Sacks 觉得这只是波动：它实际付的利息还是 9.6%，二级市场打折影响的是以后借钱的成本。最该盯的是回本周期，CoreWeave 要 2.5 年，马斯克的 SpaceX 卖现货算力约 1 年就回本。

Ben 则说 a16z 一家这类公司都不投。1999 年带宽每兆 1500 美元，只能签三年长约，到 2001 年跌到 50 美元，借钱囤带宽的“直接死了”。不过他也承认现在不一样，算力严重短缺，亚马逊 CEO 说“2028 年以后都卖光了”。

最后 Chamath 点破了真正的死穴：10 年期美债要是涨到 5.5% 到 6%，“所有靠借钱赚利差的生意都会被碾死”。接下来一个月见分晓，就看它还能不能借到那 350 亿。
